for the monastery of St. John at Moutiers-Saint-Jean, ibid., 316; for the abbey of Fontevraud, ibid., 334; for the monastery of Fesmy, ibid., 338; for Holy Cross at Bordeaux, ibid., 341; for the monastery of La Roë, ibid., 345; for the monastery of St. Serenus at Cantumerle, ibid., 351; for the monastery of Rieulay, ibid., 356; for the monastery of Bonmont, ibid., 359; for the monastery of St. Satyrius, ibid., 364; for the monastery of Manziac, ibid., 378; for the monastery of Pontigny, ibid., 423; for the church of Ragusa, ibid., 462; for the church of Jerusalem, ibid., 469; for the church of the Holy Sepulchre at Jerusalem, ibid., 474; for the monastery of St. Sylvester at Nonantola, ibid., 491; for John, bishop of Catania, ibid., 495; for the monastery of St. Reparata at Marradino, ibid., 501; for the church of Blessed Nicholas of Nugarol, ibid., 574; for the church of St. John at Monza, ibid., 576; for the monastery of Cormery, ibid., 586; for the church of Syracuse, ibid., 583; for the church of St. Mary of Reno, ibid., 588; for the church of Bologna, ibid., 605; for the church of St. Vincent at Bergamo, ibid., 610; for the church of Prémontré, ibid., 620; for the church of Blessed Remigius at Reims, ibid.; for the church of Noyon, ibid., 623; for the abbot of St. Mary at Virtu, ibid., 629; for the monastery of St. Peter at Modena, ibid., 635; for the church of St. Mary at Viberg, ibid., 449; for the church of St. Mammes at Langres, ibid., 661; for the Pisan canons, ibid., 663; for Stephen, canon of Reims, ibid., 664; for the hospital of St. Blaise at Monza, ibid., 685; for the monastery of Stephen of the Valleys, ibid., 688; for the Church of St. Andrew at Musciano, ibid., 693; for the church of the Holy Sepulchre at Jerusalem, ibid., 695; for the church of St. Mary at Gubbio, ibid., 712; for the church of St. Mary at Seckau, ibid., 717; for the church of St. Peter at Treviso, ibid., 722; for Mainard, abbot of Aquistrum, ibid., 727; for the monastery of St. Mary at Morimond, ibid., 734; for the monastery of Corbie, ibid., 861; for the convent of St. Mary at Sinningtwait, ibid., 890; for the canons of the church of Lausanne, ibid., 908; for the church of St. Martin at Tours, ibid., 915; for the church of Chartres, ibid.; for the church of Blessed Thomas, ibid., 917; for the church of Capua, ibid., 974; for the abbey [Col. 0066] of St. Martin of Chora, ibid., 992; for the church of St. Martin at Tours, ibid., 994; for the monastery of St. Bertin at Saint-Omer, ibid., 1041; for the church of St. Mary at Corbeil, ibid., 1043; for the monastery of Vallombrosa, ibid., 1067; for the monastery of St. John in Venere, ibid., 1073; for the monastery of Boscandon, ibid., 1077; for the church of Aquileia, ibid.; for the Scottish monastery of St. James at Regensburg, ibid., 1094; for the church of Poreč, ibid., 1101; for the church of Verona, ibid., 1110; for the monastery of St. Mary of the New Port, ibid., 1123; for the Church of Bonn, ibid., 1133; for the church of Ferrara, ibid., 1152; for the church of St. Margaret at Elentordesmere, ibid., 1156; for the monastery of St. Nicholas at Angers, ibid., 1176; for the church of Tropea, ibid., 1213; for the monastery of St. George in the Black Forest, ibid., 1216; for the monastery of St. Michael, ibid., 1219; for the church of Imola, ibid., 1221; for the monastery of Garsten, ibid., 1221; for the church of SS. Stephen and Willehad at Bremen, ibid., 1238; for the church of St. Mary at the End, ibid., 1241; for the church of Acerenza, ibid., 1246; for the church of Ascoli, ibid., 1254; for the monastery of St. Aper at Toul, ibid., 1252; for the monks of St. Benedict at Subiaco, ibid., 1265; for the church of Chalon, ibid., 1271; for the monastery at Liège, ibid., 1274; for the monastery of Monte Cassino, ibid., 1303; for the church of Treviso, ibid., 1314; for the Cluniacs, ibid., 1316.

To the bishop of Beauvais: commendation for his steadfast affection toward the Roman Church and the person of Pope Alexander, and exhortation to the same, CC, 96.—Constitutes Hugh, Archbishop of Palermo, metropolitan over the bishops of Agrigento, Mazara, and Malta, ibid., 97.—Commends the piety and merits of the kings of the Franks, especially of the reigning Louis VII, toward the Apostolic See, ibid., 100.—To the clergy of England, concerning the canonization of St. Edward, king of England, ibid., 106.—Praises Master Nicholas’s zeal toward the Apostolic See, ibid., 109.—Praises Henry, bishop of Beauvais, for his zeal toward the Apostolic See and in repressing schismatics, ibid., 111.—Commends the Church of Ferrara to Louis, king of the Franks, ibid., 129.—To Henry, Archbishop-elect of Reims, concerning the sending of the pallium, ibid., 136.—Confirmation of the property of the Electensian monastery, made for Abbot Bernard, in which mention is made of its founder, ibid., 140.—To Hugh, bishop of Soissons: he commends the dean of St. Anthony, ibid., 161.—Congratulates Eberhard, Archbishop of Salzburg, because he has remained steadfastly faithful to the Church, ibid., 169.—Commends to Louis, king of the Franks, Bernard, bishop of Porto, his legate, ibid., 179.—To Louis, king of the Franks, that he protect a certain poor man, ibid., 194.—For the church of St. Remigius concerning a certain piece of land, ibid., 196.—For a certain woman, that her dowry be restored to her, ibid., 203.—Grants Dominic, abbot of the monastery of St. Facundus, authority to bind and loose, and use of the mitre in the town of St. Facundus, ibid., 228.—Confirms the congregation of Piacenza founded by Bishop Sigefrid, and the brethren’s right to elect an archpriest, ibid., 243.—To Henry, Archbishop of Reims, concerning the absolution of a certain person, ibid., 244.—Confirmation of a peace sworn between the Cluniac church and the count of Forez and the barons, etc., and remission of one year’s penance for those who observe that peace, ibid., 249.—Commends the devotion of Hugh, bishop of Soissons, and promises him every favour, ibid., 262.—To Henry, Archbishop of Reims, concerning the absolution of William, a monk, ibid., 298.—Assigns the hospital at Compiègne to the abbey of the same city, ibid., 314.—[lacuna] and very many similar benefactions are recorded from col. 318 to 1349.

AMEDEUS, count.—Charter by which he gives to the monastery of Cluny the church of St. Maurice in the district of Maltacena, CXLII, 1042.

AMELIUS, bishop of Toulouse.—Confirms to Cluny the church of St. Columba, CLXVI, 848.

ANASTASIUS III, pope.—Privilege for the church of Vercelli, by which he grants Bishop Ragembert use of the pallium for celebrating solemn masses, CXXXI, 1183.—Confirms the privileges, rights, and possessions of the Church of Hamburg, ibid., 1185.

ANASTASIUS IV, pope.—A privilege by which the church of St. Mary at Pisa, with its appurtenances, is received under the protection of Blessed Peter, CLXXXVIII, 989.—Takes the church of Benevento under protection and confirms the rights of Archbishop Peter, ibid., 992.—Confirms the rights of the monastery of St. Antimus, ibid., 994.—Confirms to the monastery of Monte Cassino the church of St. Julian in the territory of Faresenone and the church of St. Caesarius at Anagni, ibid., 995.—Takes under protection of the Roman pontiff the church of St. Thecla at Milan and confirms all its possessions and rights, ibid., 996.—Takes the monastery of Vallombrosa under protection of the Roman See and confirms to Abbot Ambrose all the immunities and possessions already granted to this monastery, [Col. 0067] ibid., 997.—At the request of Bishop Guy, confirms the boundaries of the bishopric of the Abruzzi and the possessions of its church, ibid., 999.—Confirms the rights and privileges of the monastery of St. Lawrence in Campo and of its abbot Colbert, ibid., 1001.—At the request of Bishop Blancone, takes the church of Treviso under protection and confirms its goods, ibid., 1002.—Privilege for the monastery of St. Denis, by which the monastery of St. Michael is to pay it a rent, ibid.—Privilege for the monastery of St. Denis, by which he grants it certain new possessions, ibid., 1004.—Confirms to Pacificus, abbot of St. Genesius at Brescia, its ancient privileges, ibid.—Bull by which, at the request of Raymond, bishop of Maguelonne, he takes the Church of Maguelonne under his own protection and that of Blessed Peter, ibid., 1007.—Privilege for the church of St. Victor at Marseilles, by which the archbishops of Arles, Aix, and Embrun are bound to pay to that church long-established tithes from the various places occupied by them, ibid., 1007.—Receives the church of Arles under the protection of Blessed Peter and himself and confirms its rights, ibid., 1012.—Confirms to Bishop Peter the goods of the Church of Marseilles, ibid., 1014.—For the Church of Fiesole, ibid., 1015.—Letter to Peter, Archbishop of Tarentaise: he confirms to him the grant of La Strada recently made by the count of Maurienne, ibid., 1017.—Takes the monastery of Agnano under his own protection and that of Blessed Peter, and confirms its possessions and places, ibid., 1022.—Concerning the monastery of Glanfeuil, ibid., 1023.—Grants Berald, abbot of the monastery of St. Sixtus at Piacenza, use of the mitre, ibid., 1026.—Takes the Church of Rieti under protection of the Apostolic See and confirms its rights and possessions, ibid., 1026.—For the convent of the Holy Spirit of the Paraclete, ibid., 1028.—Confirms to the church of St. John at Kaltenborn the church of Revigne and other goods, donations, tithes, whether given, acquired, or yet to be acquired, ibid., 1029.—Confirms the goods, possessions, and immunities of St. Germanus of the Meadows, ibid., 1030.—Grants Wibald, abbot of Stavelot, use of the ring for life only, ibid., 1032.—Takes the church of Pistoia under protection and confirms its goods and rights, ibid., 1034.—Privilege concerning restitution to be made by the abbot of Muratorio to Peter, abbot of Cluny, after a long controversy settled through judicial process by the supreme pontiff, ibid., 1037.—That Gerard, bishop of Bergamo, and his successors may receive donations, and confirms existing ones; and that the canons of SS. Vincent and Alexander render him canonical obedience, ibid., 1038.—At the request of Bishop Godfrey, takes the church of St. Mary at Luni under protection and confirms its goods and rights, ibid., 1046.—Concerning the convent of St. Firmus at Floriano, ibid.—Concerning the monastery of St. Mary at Pomposa, ibid., 1048.—Concerning the monastery of Fruttuaria, ibid., 1051, 1054.—Concerning the abbey of the monastery of Savigny, ibid.—Concerning the monastery of St. Mary of the Meadow, ibid., 1055.—Concerning the hospital house of Mercy at Piacenza, ibid., 1062.—Concerning the monastery of St. Peter at Flavigny, ibid., 1063.—Concerning the church of St. Michael of the Rods, ibid., 1068.—For the monastery of St. Eusebius, in the diocese of Apt, ibid., 1071.—Concerning the prior and monastery of St. Saviour at Venice, ibid., 1074.—Concerning the hospital of Altopascio, ibid., 1076.—Invests the abbot of the monastery of Fulda with authority, after prior warnings, to bind by excommunication wrongdoers against his church, ibid., 1077.—Takes the hospital house of Jerusalem under protection and confirms its possessions and privileges, ibid., 1078.—Concerning the monastery of Longpont, ibid., 1084.

ANGELRAMNUS, bishop of Metz.—Grants to the monastery of Gorze Fahon, Gaudiacum, and the estate of Warangesi; and grants to the monastery of St. Avold certain estates situated in Alsace, XCVI, 1097–1100.

ANSBALD, monk.—Makes many gifts to Willibrord, bishop of Utrecht, LXXXIX, 544, 545.

ARNOLD, viscount of Ghistelles.—Endows the abbey of Aldenburg, CLXXIV, 1578.

ARNULPHUS, St, bishop of Soissons.—Diploma concerning the donation to Aldenburg Abbey of the tithes of the town of Aldenburg, CLXXIV, 1369.

AVENTIUS, bishop of Metz.—Privilege for the abbey of Gorze, by which all its ancient rights and privileges are restored in full, CXXI, 1149.

BALDWIN, count of Flanders.—Confirms to Pons, abbot of Cluny, the abbey of St. Bertin, CLXVI, 846.—Confirms the grants of all tithes of the church of Blessed Mary at Aldenburg, CLXXIV, 1584.—Letters concerning the peace made between Count Baldwin and the counts of Tournai, CCIX, 913.—A pact between Baldwin himself and the king of England, ibid., 922.—Charter for the monastery of Clairvaux: setting out for Jerusalem and moved to contrition by the holiness of the monks of Clairvaux, he makes them a donation, ibid., 923.

BALDWIN, King of Jerusalem.—Privilege confirming all possessions of the Holy Sepulchre, CLV, 1142.—Concerning the remission of the claim which he was making against the Syrians, etc., ibid., 1149.—Concerning the confirmation of Vuetmoamel, ibid., 1150.—For the church of Bethlehem, ibid., 1261.—And other various gifts and privileges for the land of Jerusalem, ibid., 1111–1260.

BARTHOLOMEW, bishop of Laon.—Pious donations made to St. Norbert and the Premonstratensians, CLXX, 1350.—Charter of the donation of Prémontré, ibid., 1359 and 1362.

BENEDICT III, pope.—Confirms the Second Synod of Soissons, together with the privileges of the Church and archbishop of Reims, CXV, 689.—To the bishops of Gaul, confirming the privileges of Corbie, ibid., 693.—Confirms the privileges of the monastery of St. Denis in France, ibid., 701.—Receives the monastery of Fulda under the protection of the Apostolic See and confirms its immunities, ibid., 702.—Confirmation of the privileges of Corbie, CXXIX, 1001.—Privilege for the monastery of the Saviour at Fulda, ibid., 1010.—For the city of Terni, ibid., 1011.

BENEDICT IV, pope.—Privilege granted to Hugh, abbot of Fulda, by which the monastery is received under the protection of the Holy See, etc., CXXXI, 43.

BENEDICT VII, pope.—Letter to Frederick, bishop of Salzburg, and his fellow-provincial bishops. He grants to him and his successors apostolic vicariate powers in Noricum and Pannonia, CXXXV, 1081.—Privilege for Theodoric, bishop of Trier, ibid., 1082.—Confirms all the goods of the monasteries of St. Benedict and St. Scholastica, ibid., 1084.—Privilege for the monastery of Vézelay, ibid., 1085.—Confirms the goods and privileges of the monastery of St. Peter of Rhodes, ibid., 1088.—Concerning the monastery of St. Cecilia of Montserrat, ibid., 1090.—Letter to the Gauls and Germans, by which he decrees that the church of Lorch—that is, Passau—is metropolitan; he defines the boundaries of this see and of Salzburg, and delegates apostolic vicariate powers to Pilgrim, archbishop of Lorch, CXXXVII, 315.—Grants to Theodoric, archbishop of Trier, and his successors the cell of the Four Crowned Saints, ibid., 318.—Confirms to the archbishop and church of Trier the right of papal legation, the privileges of riding with the *naccus* [a covered conveyance] and cross, etc., ibid., 320.—Confirms and enlarges with privileges the monastery of St. Martin at Trier, ibid., 323.—Concerning the church of St. Apollonius; the monasteries of St. Pantaleon, Monte Cassino, and St. Peter at Perugia; and the church of Ausona, ibid., 325–331.—Concerning the monasteries of Cluny, St. Peter of Rhodes, Bisuldun, and the abbey of Rufilly in the diocese of Fréjus, ibid., 332–335.—Concerning the monasteries of Corbie, St. Vincent at Volturno, St. Hilary of Carcassonne, the Saviour, and St. Peter of Gembloux, ibid., 339–345.—Concerning the monastery of St. Mary at Nienburg and the church of Tivoli, ibid., 349.

BENEDICT VIII, pope.—Letter to Bruno, bishop of Langres, confirming the privileges and rights of his diocese, ibid., 1580.—Privilege for the monastery of St. Benignus at Dijon, ibid., 1581.—Confirms all rights and goods of the Church of Urgell, ibid., 1582.—Concerning the Church of Bamberg, ibid., 1585.—Concerning the abbey of Farfa, ibid., 1586.—Grant of lands made to the abbey of Farfa and its abbot by Benedict VIII himself, ibid., 1587.—Bull for the monastery of the Holy Sepulchre at Noceto, ibid., 1589.—He gives Emperor Henry three estates situated in the duchy of Bavaria, in exchange for which he receives the royal estate of Colle Calvo, ibid., 1510.—Confirms the liberty and possessions of the monastery of Blessed Peter of Bremet, ibid., 1591.—Privilege for the monastery of Monte Cassino, ibid., 1592.—For the Church of Paderborn, ibid., 1595.—Confirms to the abbey of Farfa the castle of Bucciano, recently recovered by himself, ibid., 1596.—Roman synod of Benedict VIII, at which the privilege of the abbey of Fruttuaria was issued, ibid., 1597.—Sends the pallium to Poppo, archbishop of Trier, ibid., 1599.—Grants the pallium to the archbishop of Salerno and confirms the rights of his church, ibid., 1600.—Elevation of the Church of Bisuldun to a bishopric, ibid., 1604.—Confirms the goods of the monastery of St. Stephen of Bagno, in the diocese of Bisuldun, ibid., 1608.—Privilege for the monastery of St. Peter at Camporotondo in the county of Bisuldun, ibid., 1633.—Bull granting the abbey of Farfa the monastery of St. Lawrence in the district of Macri, in Campania, ibid., 1616.—Confirms the privileges and possessions of the Church of Porto, CXXXIX, 1617.—Grants Amatus, archbishop of Salerno, use of the pallium and confirms the privileges of his church, ibid., 1623.—Privilege for the nunnery of St. Mary and St. Andrew, ibid., 1623.—Concerning the confirmation of the bishop of Bamberg, ibid., 1624.—Confirms the possessions and privileges of the monastery of St. Sophia at Benevento, ibid., 1625.—Concerning the monastery of Pomposa, [Col. 0069] ibid., 1626.—Concerning the monastery of Monte Cassino, ibid., 1627.—Grants that in the church of the monastery of Ripoll “Alleluia” and “Glory in the highest” may be sung on the feast of the Hypapante (that is, the feast of the Purification of Blessed Mary), even if it falls after Septuagesima, ibid., 1630.—Confirms the property and rights of the monastery of St. Hilary, ibid., 1632.—Concerning the monastery of St. Savin, ibid., 1632.—Gives the monastery of St. Andrew to Richard, abbot of Fulda, ibid., 1635.—Sends the pallium to Unwan, archbishop of Hamburg, and grants to his successors legatine and archiepiscopal authority over all the northern kingdoms, ibid., 1635.—Bull by which he confirms to the monastery of Monte Cassino gifts offered by Emperor Henry for the restoration of his [Benedict’s] health, ibid., 1636.—Confirms the privileges and rights of the monastery of St. Peter of Luxeuil, ibid., 1638.

BENEDICT IX, pope.—Privilege granted to Gumbald, abbot of Holy Cross at Bordeaux, for the benefit of the cell of Blessed Mary of Soulac, CXLI, 1343.—Confirms the goods of the Church of Santa Rufina (*Silva Candida*) and the rights of its bishops, ibid., 1347.—Confirms the integrity and liberty of the patriarchate of Grado, ibid., 1362.

BERNO, abbot of Cluny.—Will of this first abbot of Cluny, CXXXIII, 853.

BERTILENDIS, abbess.—Charter for Willibrord, bishop of Utrecht, by which she gives whatever she possesses from her maternal inheritance in Toxandria, LXXXIX, 543.

CALIXTUS II, pope.—To Bernard, archbishop of Auch: grants that thereafter the bodies of the dead may be freely buried at the church of St. Mary at Auch, CLXIII, 1094.—Privilege for Tournus, ibid., 1096.—Privilege for the monastery of the Valley, ibid., 1098.—Bull declaring the chapter of Brevans directly subject to the Roman Church, and granting it the right to receive chrism, holy oil, consecrations of churches or altars, and ordinations of clerics from whatever bishop it may prefer, ibid., 1099.—Bull for the monastery of St. Blasien, ibid., 1100.—Confirms the privileges and possessions of the hospice of Jerusalem, ibid., 1102.—Bull for the monastery of Blessed Mary of Électe, ibid.—Confirms the rights and goods of the monastery of St. Giles, ibid., 1103, 1105.—Permits the abbot of Marseille and his brethren to celebrate the divine office in the church of St. Nicholas at Tarascon and to have it consecrated, ibid., 1107.—Bull for the benefit of the monastery of St. Mary of Soricino, ibid., 1108.—The church of St. Polycarp is confirmed to the monastery of Électe, ibid.—Bull concerning the gift of the church of St. Liberata, made by Hildebert, bishop of Agen, to Stephen, abbot of Chaise-Dieu, ibid., 1110.—Grants Berengar, abbot of the monastery of Lagrasse in Septimania, and his successors, the church of St. Peter of Valéries, subject to an annual rent of two gold coins, ibid., 1114.—Bull for Guy, abbot of Turturiac, ibid., 1117.—For Holy Trinity at Poitiers, ibid., 1119.—For the abbey of St. Vincent at Senlis, ibid., 1119.—To certain bishops: commends to them the monastery of Savigny, ibid., 1120.—Confirms the possessions and privileges of the nunnery of St. Mary of Fontevraud, ibid., 1121.—Confirms the possessions of the monastery of SS. Peter and Paul and of St. Ghislain at Celles, ibid., 1124.—Confirms the privileges of the monastery of Vendôme, ibid., 1125.—Privilege for the abbey of St. Denis near Paris, ibid., 1126.—Grants Godebald, bishop of Utrecht, the episcopal mitre, ibid., 1130.—Receives the monastery of Murbach under protection and confirms its privileges, ibid.—Confirms the privileges of the church of St. Martin at Tours, ibid., 1131.—Confirms the liberty and privilege of the monastery of St. Bertin at Saint-Omer, ibid., 1133.—Confirms the privileges of the Church of Cambrai, ibid., 1134.—Bull concerning the privileges of the monastery of St. Mary of Josaphat in the diocese of Chartres, ibid., 1136.—Confirms the decree against simony issued by Geoffrey, bishop of Chartres, ibid., 1137.—Confirms the monastery of Springiersbach and its discipline, ibid., 1138.—Confirms the privileges of the monastery of St. Remigius at Reims, ibid.—Confirms the possessions and privileges of the monastery of St. Martin-des-Champs at Paris, ibid., 1142.—Bull for Abbot Pacanus and the monks of Blessed Mary of Étampes, ibid., 1145.—Confirms the statutes of the Cistercian monastery, ibid., 1147.—Declares Bruno, archbishop of Trier, free from every authority of a legate unless one is sent *a latere* [from the pope’s side], ibid., 1148.—Confirms for the same man metropolitan right and other ancient insignia, ibid.—Privilege for the monastery of the Saviour at Schaffhausen, ibid., 1150.—Grants Hugh, bishop of Auxerre, authority to confer upon churches of canons and monks churches which laymen had held, ibid., 1152.—Confirms the immunity and possessions of the monastery of Vézelay, ibid., 1155.—Informs Adalbert, abbot of Schaffhausen, that he has undertaken the monastery’s protection, ibid., 1156.—Confirms the privileges of the nunnery of Belle-Lieu, ibid.—Privilege for the monastery [Col. 0070] of St. Mary of Bonneval, ibid., 1157.—Bull for the monastery of Saint-Cucufa in the region of Val, ibid., 1159.—Confirms the goods and privileges of the canons of the church of St. John at Besançon, ibid., 1162.—Privilege for the monastery of Cluny, ibid., 1164.—Delegates to the Church of Compostela the metropolitan dignity of the Church of Mérida, ibid., 1168.—Informs the bishops, abbots, clerics, etc., established throughout the provinces of Mérida and Braga, that he has committed his vicariate authority in those regions to Diego, archbishop of Compostela, ibid., 1170.—Receives the Church of Portugal under protection and confirms its possessions, ibid., 1171.—Privilege for the church of St. Mary Magdalene at Besançon, ibid., 1172.—Confirms the discipline, possessions, and privileges of the canonry serving the people of the martyrs at Uxelles, ibid., 1173.—Confirms the possessions of the church of St. John at Monza, ibid.—Confirms all goods and rights whatsoever of the monastery of the Saviour at Pavia, ibid., 1174.—Undertakes the patronage of the monastery of St. Paul of Argon, and confirms its goods and privileges, ibid., 1176.—Confirms the privileges and possessions of the church of St. Evasius at Casale, ibid.—Grants Oberto, bishop of Cremona, and his successors the right to consecrate the abbots of the monastery of St. Peter, ibid., 1177.—Confirms the possessions of the monastery of St. Saturninus at Carlat, ibid., 1178.—Consecrates the cathedral church at Volterra, ibid., 1178.—Privilege for the monastery of Sesto, ibid.—Bull for the monastery of St. Mary of Morrona and its abbot Gerard, ibid., 1179.—Confirms all donations made to the monastery of Monte Cassino by Gunnarius and his wife, ibid., 1181.—Consecrates Gerard as archbishop of Ragusa, grants him the pallium, and confirms the possessions and rights of his church, ibid., 1184.—Bull for the monastery at Volturno, ibid.—Undertakes the protection of the monastery of St. Sophia at Benevento and confirms its goods and rights, ibid., 1186.—Confirms the privileges of the hermitage of Turrita, ibid., 1189.—Assigns the church of St. Theodore to Cluny, ibid.—Bull for the monastery of the Holy Apostles Peter and Paul at Canterbury, ibid., 1191.—Receives the nunnery of Marcigny under protection, ibid., 1192.—Confirms the possessions of the canons of St. Lawrence at Genoa, ibid., 1194.—Confirms the primacy of Humbert, archbishop of Lyon, ibid., 1195.—Confirms the rights of the Church of Ravenna, ibid.—Receives under protection the monastery of SS. Philip and James and St. Walburga in the Sacred Wood, and confirms its goods, ibid., 1197.—Confirms to the monastery of Affligem the church of Bornem, ibid., 1199.—Confirms the boundaries of the bishopric of Modena and the goods of its church, ibid., 1200.—Confirms the possessions and privileges of the monastery of St. Clement at Pescara, ibid., 1201.—Authorizes Otto of Castel d’Iring to build a church and monastery, under certain conditions, ibid., 1203.—Undertakes the protection of the church of St. Mary and St. Walburga at Furnes, and confirms its goods and privileges, ibid., 1204.—Approves the institution of the regular canons of Bergtestaden, ibid., 1206.—To Franco, abbot of Tournus: privilege of immunity and another privilege, ibid., 1207, 1208.—Confirms the rights and goods of the canons of Verona, ibid., 1210.—To the burgesses of the monastery of St. Giles: absolves them from the oath of fidelity rendered to Count Ildefonsus, who had compelled them to perjury, ibid., 1213.—Concerning confirmation of the regular canons of the church of the Holy Sepulchre at Jerusalem and their possessions, ibid., 1215.—To the archbishop of Caesarea and the other bishops, abbots, etc., established throughout the province of Jerusalem, and to King Baldwin, etc.: announces that he has sent the pallium to Patriarch Garmond, ibid., 1216.—At the request of Louis, king of the Franks, confirms the union of the bishoprics of Noyon and Tournai, ibid., 1125.—Confirms the privileges of the Church of Malta, ibid., 1226.—Privilege for the abbey of St. Germanus of the Meadows, ibid., 1230.—Privilege for the monastery of St. Peter of Melun, ibid., 1233.—Privilege of the mother-church of St. John in relation to the church of the Holy Sepulchre, ibid., 1235.—Privilege for the monastery of Zwiefalten, ibid., 1239.—Confirms the monastery of SS. Peter and Paul at Echenbrunn, ibid., 1240.—Privilege for the monastery of St. Mary at Godesberg, ibid.—Receives the monastery of the Saviour at Milat under protection and confirms its rights, ibid., 1242.—Strengthens certain privileges of the Church of Lucca, ibid., 1243.—Privilege for the monastery of St. Mary at Pratalea, ibid.—Confirms the possessions and privileges of the monastery of the Saviour and St. Boniface at Fulda, ibid., 1244.—Privilege for the monastery of Carin, ibid., 1250.—Bull for the monastery of the Saviour at Leutewitz, ibid., 1254.—Approves the institution of the regular canons of Bernried, ibid., 1257.—Confirms all rights and privileges of the monastery of St. Eustace of Nervesia, ibid., 1258.—Confirms certain possessions of the monastery of St. Mary at Pinerolo, ibid., 1261.—Confirms the possessions and [Col. 0071] privileges of the hospice of St. John at Jerusalem, ibid.—Exhorts the monks of Monte Cassino to obey Oderisius, elected abbot, ibid., 1262.—Enumerates the goods and rights of the monastery of St. Euphemia at Brescia and receives it under the protection of the holy Roman Church, ibid.—Confirms all rights and privileges of Archpriest Frederick and the canons of Carpi, ibid., 1263.—Confirmation of the privileges of the church of St. Rupert at Salzburg, ibid., 1265.—Privilege for the abbey of St. Mary at Vangadice, ibid., 1267.—Confirms the privileges and goods of the canons of the church of Cremona, ibid., 1269.—Receives the monastery of Siena under protection and confirms its privileges, ibid., 1271.—Privilege for the church of Blessed Mary at Blois, ibid.—Privilege for the monastery of Usinnhoven, ibid., 1272.—Confirms to the monastery of Holy Cross at Bordeaux the church of St. Macarius, ibid., 1276.—Confirms the liberty and possessions of the Church of Monopoli, ibid., 1277.—Commends to the people of Hamburg Adalbero, archbishop consecrated and invested with the pallium by himself, ibid., 1278.—Confirmation of all rights of the Church of Squillace, ibid., 1279.—Concerning privileges granted to the Church of Bamberg, ibid., 1281.—Privilege for the monastery of St. Benedict at Crema, ibid.—Receives under protection the nunnery of the Saviour and St. Julia at Brescia, and confirms its possessions and privileges, ibid., 1283.—Privilege for the church of St. Deodatus, ibid., 1284.—Confirms to the monastery of St. Ghislain certain altars granted by Burchard, bishop of Cambrai, ibid., 1285.—Restores the former rights of the church of Segovia, ibid., 1290.—Privilege for the monastery of St. Victor at Marseille, ibid., 1291.—Privilege for the church at Pavia, ibid., 1292.—Grants Amadeus, bishop of Maurienne, the provostship of the church of St. Mary at Susa and parochial jurisdiction over the city of Susa itself, ibid., 1293.—Confirms the liberty, privileges, and possessions of the monastery of St. George at Venice, ibid., 1294.—The monastery of St. Mary in the diocese of Glastonbury is received under the protection of the Apostolic See, and all its goods and donations are confirmed, ibid., 1295.—Confirms the possessions, liberty, and privileges of the monastery of All Saints at Bari, ibid., 1296.—To Louis, king of the Franks: commends Peter, cardinal and his [the pope’s] legate, ibid., 1297.—Grants certain privileges to Richard, provost of Springiersbach, and his brethren, ibid., 1298.—Informs the suffragan bishops and abbots of the province of Besançon of the judgment he has rendered concerning the mother-church status of the church of St. John, ibid.—Concerning the privileges of the church of Bracara, ibid., 1299, 1300.—Grants Benedict, bishop of Lucca, use of the pallium, ibid., 1300.—Privilege for the monastery of Andres, ibid., 1301.—Grants remission of sins to all buried in the church of Compsa, ibid., 1304.—Ratifies all privileges of the people of Vendôme, ibid., 1306.—Confirms the goods, rights, and privileges of the monastery of Hugshofen, founded by Count Werner of Ortenberg, ibid., 1308.—Bull confirming the properties belonging to the church of St. Mary of Leton, ibid., 1314.—Privilege for the abbey of Mont-des-Anges, ibid., 1317.—Privilege for the monastery of Bifurca, ibid., 1318.—Concerning privileges granted to the Church of Bamberg, ibid., 1319.—Confirms the privileges of the monastery of Dervent, ibid., 1320.—Commends the monastery of Dervent as subject to the Roman Church, ibid.—Confirms the privileges of the church of St. Fridianus at Lucca, ibid., 1321.—Receives the monastery of Rastede under protection and confirms its goods and privileges, ibid., 1324.—Privilege for the monastery of St. Bertin at Saint-Omer, ibid., 1327.—Receives the monastery of St. Mary at Pomposa under protection and confirms its goods and privileges, ibid., 1328.—Privilege for the church of St. Benignus at Dijon, ibid., 1330.—Privilege for the church of St. Stephen at Dijon, ibid., 1333.—Receives the monastery of St. Nicholas at Buttenburg under protection and confirms its goods and privileges, ibid., 1334.

CHARLEMAGNE, emperor.—Diploma by which he gives the priory of St. Deodatus to the monastery of St. Denis, XCVII, 914.—Diploma granting immunity to the abbey of Saint-Omer, CCVI, 917.—Charter by which he grants the estates of Faverolles and Noron to the abbey of St. Denis, XCVII, 920.—Charter of immunity granted to the abbey of Murbach under Abbot Charibert, ibid., 925.—Diploma granted to Heddo, bishop of Strasbourg, by which he confirms to the Church of Strasbourg the whole territorial district in the valley of the Bruche, ibid., 926.—For the Church of Strasbourg, ibid., 928.—Edict for the monastery of St. Martin at Tours, ibid., 931.—Charter for the monastery of St. Denis, ibid., 933.—Diploma for the monastery of Lérins, ibid., 935.—Edict by which he gives the monks of St. Denis the estate of Luzarches, ibid., 939.—Diploma concerning the immunity of the abbey of St. Denis, ibid., 940, 941.—Edict by which he confirms to the monastery of St. Denis various goods recovered for it under King Pippin, ibid., 943.—Edict by which he gives certain estates to the monastery of St. Denis, ibid., 946.—Edicts for the monasteries [Col. 0072] of Murbach, Flavigny, and St. Martin at Tours, ibid., 947, 948, 949.—Diploma by which he confirms the privilege of Solgne against the bishop of Metz, ibid., 952.—Diploma for the monastery of Urom, ibid., 953.—Judicial assembly for the abbey of Honau, ibid., 954, 957.—Diploma for the monastery of Solgne, ibid., 958.—Edict by which he confirms all immunities of the monastery of St. Denis, ibid., 659.—Edict for Nimfrid, abbot of the monastery of Lagrasse, ibid., 962.—Diploma by which he grants the Church of Lebraha tithes from lands belonging to it, ibid., 966.—Diploma by which he declares the monastery of Honau exempt from tolls, ibid., 967.—Diploma for the monastery of St. Arnulf at Metz, ibid., 973.—Edict for the monastery of Saint-Germain-des-Prés, ibid., 974.—Edict concerning goods sold to the monastery of St. Denis by Count Hrodhard, which goods the king confirms to that place, ibid., 977.—Edict for the monastery of St. Victor at Marseille, ibid., 978.—Edict for the monastery of St. Martin at Tours, ibid., 979.—Edict concerning all property of the Church of Le Mans, ibid., 981.—Diploma by which he confirms gifts made to the monastery of St. Denis by his sister Gisela, ibid., 985.—Diploma for the monastery of Centula, ibid., 980.—Diploma by which he confirms Cella Nova to the monastery of Amay, ibid., 988.—Edict concerning the immunity of the monastery of Carrof, ibid., 989.—Edict for the monks of St. Martin at Tours, ibid., 990.—Edict for the monastery of Cormery and the church of Le Mans, ibid., 992, 994.—Edict by which he confirms the privilege of immunity granted by his father Pippin to the monastery of Noyon, ibid., 997.—Confirmation of immunities made to Frodoenus, abbot of Novalesa, ibid.—Gift made by Charlemagne to the monastery of Bobbio, ibid., 1000.—Charter of donation made by Charlemagne to the monastery of Nonantola, ibid., 1002.—Diploma by which Charlemagne grants certain privileges and rights to the monastery at Volturno, ibid., 1006.—Diploma for the church of Reggio, ibid., 1007, 1009.—Diploma for Apollinaris, bishop of Reggio, and his church, ibid., 1010.—Diploma by which he grants a privilege to the church of Arezzo, ibid., 1014.—Diploma for the church of Modena, ibid., 1015.—Diploma for the monastery of St. Vincent at Volturno, ibid., 1016.—Diploma for the church of Benevento, ibid., 1018.—Diploma for the church of Milan, ibid., 1019.—Diploma for the church of Ceneta, ibid., 1020.—Diploma for the church of Arezzo, ibid., 1021.—Diploma by which he confirms a donation made by Ludiger for the church of Ascoli, ibid., 1023.—Diploma for the church of Concordia, ibid., 1025.—Diploma by which he confirms all goods, privileges, and rights of the abbey of Farfa, ibid., 1027.—Diploma for the church of Grado, ibid., 1028.—Diploma for the church of Como, ibid., 1029.—Diploma for the monastery of St. Mary of Organo, ibid., 1030.—Diploma for the monastery of Trois-Fontaines, ibid., 1031.

Renewal of the testament of Abbo, patrician, for the abbey of Novalesa, ibid., 1035.—Diploma for the church of Piacenza, ibid., 1036.—Edict for Manfred, ibid., 1037.—Privilege for the church of Milan, ibid., 1038.—Edicts for the monastery of Monte Cassino, ibid., 1041, 1044.—Diploma for the church of Aquileia, ibid.—Confirmation of donations made by predecessors to the monastery of Utrecht, ibid., 1047.—Writ of vindication issued to the monastery of Lorsch, ibid., 1048, 1049.—Edict for the church of Fulda, ibid., 1051, 1052.—Immunity granted to the monastery of Prüm, ibid., 1053, 1054.—Grants the privilege of liberty to the monastery of Lorsch, ibid., 1055.—Privileges, etc., for the monasteries of Liesse, St. Maximin, etc., ibid., 1057–1082.—Diploma for Patriarch Paulinus, securing freedom for the Aquileian clergy in the election of patriarchs, XCVIII, 1447–1449.—Receives the monastery of Aniane, with its appurtenances and adjacent properties, under his protection, CIII, 1419.

CANUTE I, king.—Confirms the Church of the Saviour at Canterbury as mother and mistress of all churches in the English kingdom, CLI, 1185.—Charter for the abbey of St. Benedict at Holme in Suffolk, ibid., 1184.—For the church of St. Edmund, ibid., 1186.—Charter by which he subjects all causes on the island of Glastonbury, both ecclesiastical and secular, to the abbot’s jurisdiction, excluding every other authority, ibid., 1188.

CARLOMAN, king.—Confirms for the monastery of St. Denis its immunities and exemption from all tolls incurred by those coming to the feast or fair of St. Denis, XCVI, 1572.—Concerning the immunity of the Church of Argenteuil and of the monastery of Honau, ibid., 1577.—Charter confirming to the monastery of Noyon goods which Duke Adalric of Alsace had granted to that monastery, ibid., 1578.

[Col. 0073] CHARLES, mayor of the palace.—Concerning his receipt of Bishop Boniface into protection and defence, LXXXIX, 506.—Grants gifts to the monastery of Maastricht, ibid., 551, 552.

CHARLES, Count of Flanders.—Diploma concerning the gift of tithes and of all the produce of the entire parish of Aldenburg, CLXXIV, 1568.

CHRISTOPHER, usurper of the Apostolic See.—Diploma by which he confirms the privileges of the abbey of Corbie in the diocese of Amiens, CXXXI, 46.

CONRAD II, emperor.—Privilege for the abbey of Wissembourg, CLI, 1044.—Privilege for the monastery of Corbie, ibid., 1045.—Diploma by which he confirms the rights of the monastery of St. Pontianus at Lucca, ibid., 1046.—Concerning the abbey of Farfa, ibid., 1047.—For the monastery of nuns of the Lord the Saviour at Lucca, ibid., 1048.—Concerning the monastery of the Holy Saviour at Amiale in the diocese of Chiusi, ibid., 1049.—Privileges for the churches of Paderborn, St. Gorgonius, and St. Kilian, ibid., 1051, 1057.—Privilege for the monastery of New Corbie, ibid., 1052.—Confirms to Ubaldo, bishop of Cremona, various rights and the county of that city, ibid., 1057, 1058.—Confirmatory privilege of all rights of the Pavia monastery of St. Peter, called *in Cœlo Aureo* [“in the Golden Heaven”], ibid., 1065.—Privilege for the Church of Bremen, ibid., 1068.—Diploma by which he receives the Church of Mantua under his protection and confirms its rights, ibid., 1069.—Concerning the monastery of St. Theonestus at Treviso, ibid., 1070.—Concerning the monastery of St. Justus at Susa, ibid., 1072.—Concerning the nunnery of St. Sixtus in the city of Piacenza, ibid., 1074.—Concerning the monastery of St. Vincent at Volturno, ibid., 1075.—Concerning the Church of Modena, ibid., 1079.

CLEMENT II, pope.—Bull by which he gives the Church of Fulda the monastery of St. Andrew, situated in Rome beside the Church of St. Mary at the Manger, CXLII, 577.—Privilege for the monastery of Fulda, ibid., 579.—Privilege for the Church of Hamburg, ibid., 583.—Receives under protection the monastery of Holy Trinity at Vendôme, founded by Geoffrey, and confirms its possessions, ibid., 584.—Privilege for the monastery of Tharise, ibid., 585.—Letter to John, archbishop of Salerno, confirming his transfer from the bishopric of Paestum to that of Salerno and granting him the pallium, ibid., 586.—Privilege for the Church of Bamberg, ibid., 588.

CLEMENT III, pope.—Confirms all monasteries belonging to the Camaldolese congregation and subjects them to the governance of the prior of that congregation, CCIV, 1276.—Secures for the monastery of Royaumont the churches of Rengis-valle and Jovillere, ibid., 1278.—Takes the monastery of Vallombrosa under protection and confirms its possessions and rights, ibid., 1279.—Concerning the monastery of St. Michael of Orticara, ibid., 1282.—Concerning the church of St. Michael at Arezzo, ibid., 1283.—Confirms the abbeys of Hérival, Hermeries, Mont d’Été, and Gif, ibid., 1284.—Takes the monastery of St. Cassian of Carisy under protection and confirms its possessions and privileges, ibid., 1285.—Grants Maurice, bishop of Paris, authority, whenever prebends fall vacant, to assign them to suitable persons, ibid., 1295.—Confirms the privileges and possessions of the Church of Paris, ibid., 1292.—Grants Gerard, abbot of Vézelay, and his successors the use of sandals, ibid.—Secures for Gunteran, bishop of Siena, the church situated on Mount Bonitius, ibid., 1296.—Privilege for the monastery of St. Mary at Florence, ibid., 1297.—Takes the church of St. Mary of Grandgurgitis under protection, etc., ibid., 1298.—Concerning the Church of Camin, ibid., 1301.—Secures for Hugh, abbot of Cluny, the monastery of Baume, ibid., 1303.—Takes the monastery of Cluny under protection and confirms certain goods and privileges, ibid., 1305, 1307.—Concerning the monastery of St. Mary of Mont Flabon, ibid., 1313.—Bull confirming the abbey of Blessed Mary of Hérival, ibid., 1314.—Secures for the monastery of Cluny the estate of Sana, ibid., 1317.—Takes the monastery of St. Mary of Moncel under protection and confirms its possessions and privileges, ibid., 1318.—Concerning the church of St. Mary of Reno, ibid., 1324.—Secures for the abbots and brethren of the Premonstratensian order exemption from tithes, ibid., 1326.—Takes the church of St. Piat under protection and confirms its goods and privileges, ibid., 1328.—Concerning the Venetian church of St. Saviour, ibid., 1329.—Grants the prior and chapter of Venetian St. Saviour authority to appoint an economus, ibid., 1332.—Takes the monastery of Prémontré under protection, etc., ibid., 1333.—Permits Lanfranc, bishop of Bergamo, to recover possessions of the Church alienated against the will of the chapter, ibid., 1335.—Grants Lanfranc, bishop of Bergamo, authority to punish disobedient clerics, ibid., 1336.—Secures for the convent of Cassino money assigned by Abbot Blessed Peter for the brethren’s use, ibid.—Takes the Florentine church of St. Lawrence under protection and confirms its goods and privileges, [Col. 0074] ibid., 1337.—Grants the prior and Carthusian brethren freedom to receive any clerics or laymen of a lesser religious profession who decide to enter their order; and adds other privileges, ibid., 1339.—Takes the monastery of St. Benedict of Gualdo under protection and confirms its possessions and privileges, ibid.—Confirms a judgment rendered between the sisters of St. Hilary and the provost of Florence, ibid., 1342.—Privilege for the church of St. John at Monza, ibid.—Privilege for the church of St. Germanus, ibid., 1344.—For the church of Ravello, ibid., 1347.—Takes the Church of Brandenburg under protection and confirms its goods and rights, ibid., 1348.—Confirms the possessions and privileges of the chapter of Brandenburg, ibid., 1349.—Concerning the church of St. Nicholas at Stendal, ibid., 1351.—Secures for the canons of the church of St. Peter, Rome, the privilege granted by Eugenius III, ibid., 1353.—Privilege for the monastery of St. Gilbert of Sept-Fonts, diocese of Clermont, ibid., 1355.—Takes the church of St. Mary at Viborg under protection and confirms its goods and privileges, ibid., 1358.—Permits Absalon, archbishop of Lund, to enroll Ketil, a certain provost of St. Mary at Viborg, among the saints, ibid., 1360.—Approves the judgment rendered by Gerard, bishop, and Vitalian, archdeacon of Padua, concerning certain tithes, between Mark, bishop of Castello (Venice), and the parish priests and priests of certain churches. Confirms the possessions of the church of St. Cantianus, ibid., 1361.—By apostolic authority confirms for the priests and clerics of St. Mary the portion of tithes granted them by Mark Nicholas, bishop of Castello, and decrees that the goods of that church remain safe and unimpaired, ibid., 1364.—Receives the church of St. Cassian at Venice under St. Peter’s protection and confirms its rights and revenues by apostolic authority, ibid., 1365.—Commends the church of St. Honoratus to the consuls of Grasse, ibid., 1368.—Takes the Church of Ragusa under protection and confirms its privileges, ibid.—Takes the Florentine church of St. Lawrence under protection and confirms its goods, ibid., 1371.—Privilege for the church of St. Ansgar at Bremen, ibid., 1373.—Confirms the Rule of Grandmont, ibid., 1376.—Grants Maurice, bishop of Paris, a privilege concerning procurations to be supplied by the canons regular of the churches, both to him and to his archdeacons while visiting parishes, ibid., 1377.—Confirms the possessions of the monastery of Jesus of Nazareth, at Mount Aragon, ibid., 1379.—Secures for Hartwig, archbishop, and the Church of Hamburg, the bishoprics of Lübeck, Schwerin, Ratzeburg, and Uxkull as suffragans, ibid., 1380.—Secures for the same the bishopric of Växjö, ibid., 1381.—Privilege for the monastery of Osterholz, ibid., 1382.—For the church of Furcon, ibid., 1383.—Confirms donations made to the canons of the church of Caesaraugusta, ibid.—Confirms the privileges of William, archbishop of Montreale, and grants him use of the pallium, ibid., 1385.—Confirms the decision of the bishops of Equilio and Torcello concerning the reception of the bishop of Castello by the abbot of St. Nicholas of the Shore on Ascension Day, ibid., 1389.—Privilege for the monastery of Cassino, ibid., 1395.—Takes the monastery of Cassino under the protection of Blessed Peter and the Apostolic See; declares that this monastery is to be preferred above the rest throughout the West, etc., ibid.—Takes the church of St. Michael at Nonantola under protection and confirms its possessions and privileges, ibid., 1396.—Takes the monastery of St. Martin at Metz under protection and confirms its discipline and possessions, ibid., 1398.—Takes the monastery of St. Nicholas of Fruttuaria under protection and confirms its discipline, etc., ibid., 1403.—Confirms the peace negotiated between the Pisans and Genoese by Peter, cardinal priest of St. Cecilia, and Sofredus, cardinal deacon of St. Mary in Via Lata, ibid., 1407.—Privilege for Roffridus, abbot of Cassino, ibid., 1411.—For the monastery of St. Peter of Massa on Mount Nerone, ibid., 1412.—Confirms certain rights of the chapter of the church of St. Alexander at Bergamo, ibid., 1414.—Takes the church of SS. Felix and Regula at Zurich under protection and confirms its possessions, ibid.—Takes the monastery of St. Salvius at Florence under protection and confirms its goods and rights, ibid., 1416.—Receives the monastery of Muri into Blessed Peter’s protection, confirms all privileges granted even by Pope Alexander, and adds new ones, ibid., 1421.—Concerning the monastery of St. Mary at Esrum, ibid., 1423.—Grants the prior and brethren of Fonte Avellana authority to reform the condition of the monastery of St. Victor, ibid., 1425.—Takes the church of St. Peter at Douai under protection, etc., ibid., 1427.—Concerning the church of Siena, ibid., 1430.—Takes the monastery of Subiaco and its goods under the protection of the Holy Roman Church; forbids anyone except the Apostolic See to exercise jurisdiction in that monastery; declares that the election of the abbot belongs to the monks and consecration to the supreme pontiff; . . . bestows a blessing upon its benefactors, CCIV, 1432.—Takes the Church of Ferrara under protection, etc., ibid., 1436.—Secures for the monastery of St. Denis the church of St. Blaise of Grand-Puits, ibid., 1439.—Takes the monastery of St. Matthew of the Castle under protection, etc., ibid., 1440.—Absolves the whole chapter of Trier, and all clergy and people living throughout the archbishopric, from obedience in spiritual and temporal matters to Archbishop Fulmar and Provost R., ibid., 1442.—Secures for the monastery of St. Chrysogonus at Zadar the church of St. Martin, ibid., 1444.—Secures for Herman, master, and the brethren of the Hospital of Jerusalem those things which Philip, archbishop of Cologne, had donated to the Hospital of the Holy Sepulchre at Duisburg, ibid.—Secures for the canons of the Parisian church of St. Thomas of Luparea the possessions bestowed by Count Robert, ibid., 1445.—Grants privileges to the provost and brethren of the church of St. Nicholas at Stendal, ibid., 1446.—Takes the monastery of Baumburg under protection, etc., ibid., 1447.—The same for the monastery of St. Quentin at Beauvais, ibid., 1450.—Confirms the judgment on the right of foundation of the three churches of Chilcheim, Eimuoting, and Matra, pronounced by Otto, formerly bishop of Constance, ibid., 1453.—Secures for the abbot and convent of Cîteaux the church of Schardeburg, donated by Richard, king of England, ibid., 1454.—Privilege for the church of Theren; confirms for it gifts conferred by Albert, archdeacon, ibid., 1456.—Privilege for the church of Radesdorf, ibid.—Takes the nunnery of St. Cosmas at Talliacot under protection, etc., ibid., 1458.—Privilege for the Church of Trier, ibid., 1461.—Takes the Carthusian brethren under protection, etc., ibid., 1462.—Grants the priors and brethren of the Carthusian order that no prior or brother may have leave to appeal without the consent of the chapter of his house, ibid., 1464.—Secures two altars for the monastery of Eynsham, ibid., 1465.—Confirms the peace restored between the canons of St. Vincent and St. Alexander at Bergamo, ibid.—Bull of canonization of Blessed Malachy, ibid., 1466.—Takes the church of the Holy Cross at Guingamp under protection, etc., ibid., 1467.—Bull confirming the goods of the church of St. Mary of the Golden [church] at Toulouse, ibid., 1470.—Grants the provost of St. Mary at Magdeburg the use of gloves, ibid., 1471.—Takes the monastery of St. Denis at Nogent under protection, etc., ibid., 1472.—Secures for Maurice, bishop of Paris, the right, whenever a deanery becomes vacant, to receive its revenue, ibid., 1475.—Establishes an episcopal see in the city of Piacenza, etc., ibid., 1476.—Privilege for the Church of Harter, ibid., 1478.

COELESTINE II, pope.—Privilege for the church of St. Marian at Gubbio, CLXXIX, 705.—Privilege confirming the church of St. John at Monza, ibid., 708.—Various privileges for the churches of Oberzell at Würzburg, St. Mary Major at Augsburg, and St. Alexander at Bergamo, ibid., 770–775.—For the monasteries of St. Martin at Ahusen, Thenol, SS. Saviour and Quiricus, and Prémontré, ibid., 772–778.—Takes the church of St. Mary at Halberstadt under protection and confirms the possessions of its canons, ibid., 784.—Concerning the monastery of Stavelot, ibid., 785.—Privileges for the church of Aachen and the monastery of Rott, ibid., 788.—Entrusts Walter, bishop of Augsburg, with the protection of the monastery of Rott, ibid.—Privilege for the church of the Holy Sepulchre at Jerusalem, ibid., 790.—Grants to the brethren of the Church of Lucca, heirs of Cardinal Almeric, the privilege that henceforth cardinal deacons of the church of Blessed Mary the New shall be chosen from their number, ibid., 792.—To Peter, prior, and the canons of the Holy Sepulchre at Jerusalem: grants them a church in the city of Rome, ibid., 793.—Privilege for the monastery of St. Bertin at Sithiu, ibid., 794.—To Gerolius, provost of Reichersberg: consoles him because he suffers many things from adversaries, and invites him to come to him, ibid., 797.—Privilege for the nunnery of St. Hilary, ibid., 798.—For the monasteries of Mount St. John and St. Saviour of Florence, and for the church of Pistoia, ibid., 799–801.—For the churches of St. Mary of Undersford and Stromberg, ibid., 804.—Takes the monastery of Ensdorf under protection, confirms its goods, and establishes its rights, ibid., 808.—Secures for the monastery of Cluny the church of St. Vincent, granted by Berengar, bishop of Salamanca, ibid., 810.—Privilege for the monastery of St. Mary of Bonosolatio, ibid.—Privileges for the monastery of Michelsfeld and for the churches of the Island and of St. Mary Magdalene, ibid., 814.—Privileges for the churches of Fiesole and Ferrara, ibid., 815, 816.—Takes the abbey of Aldenburg under his protection and adorns it with various privileges, ibid., 1583.

COELESTINE III, pope.—Takes the church of St. John at Rastorf under protection and confirms its possessions and privileges, [Col. 0076] CCVI, 867.—Concerning the monastery of St. Mary and St. John the Evangelist, ibid., 872, 873.—Concerning the church of St. Lawrence at Florence, ibid., 876.—Concerning the monastery of Nonantola, ibid., 878.—Concerning the church of St. Sigismund, ibid., 879.—Concerning the monastery of St. Peter at Pescaria, ibid., 881.—Concerning the monastery of St. Anastasius at Acquae Salviae, ibid., 886.—Concerning the monastery of Gisl, ibid., 887.—Concerning the monastery of Ragnibert in the Jura, ibid., 893.—Concerning the church of St. Nicholas at Stendal, ibid., 895.—Concerning the church of St. Mary and St. John the Evangelist, ibid., 896.—Concerning the monastery of St. Peter at Savilly, ibid., 900.—Concerning the monastery of the Valley of St. Mary at Helmstedt, ibid., 912.—Concerning the monastery of Goldbach, ibid., 913.—Concerning the church of Scala, ibid., 919.—Concerning the nunnery of St. Peter at Florence, ibid., 923.—Concerning the monastery of St. Justina, ibid., 924.—Concerning the monastery of St. Mary of Lodi, ibid., 927.—Concerning the Church of Lucca, ibid., 931.—Concerning the abbey of Le Boschet, or Vallis Lucida, ibid., 934.—Concerning the monastery of St. Arnulf at Metz, ibid., 935.—Concerning the monastery of St. Vincent at Metz, ibid., 938.—Concerning the monastery of St. Mary in the River, ibid., 943.—Concerning the church of SS. Andrew and Nicholas at Empoli, ibid., 944.—Concerning the nunnery of St. Cosmas at Talliacot, ibid., 948.—Concerning the monastery of Altorf in Alsace, ibid., 950.—Concerning the monastery of St. Mary at Pomposa, ibid., 958.—Concerning the monastery of St. Michael at Hildesheim, ibid., 973.—Concerning the monastery of St. Benedict at Ringstadt, ibid., 975.—Concerning the monastery of St. Mary of Ferraria, ibid., 978.—Concerning the monastery of St. Mary at Esrum, ibid., 980.—Concerning the monastery of St. Benignus at Dijon, ibid., 989.—Concerning the church of Blessed Peter at Guastalla, ibid., 997.—Concerning the monastery of St. Mary and St. Buruno at Tavistock, ibid., 999.—Concerning the nunnery of Sixen, ibid., 1001.—Concerning the monastery of St. Peter of Mount Heisterbach, ibid., 1003.—Concerning the church of Melfi, ibid., 1007.—Concerning the church of Balnea, ibid., 1012.—Concerning the church of St. John at Calcinaia, ibid., 1019.—Concerning the monastery of St. Lawrence at Aversa, ibid., 1029.—Concerning the church of Nidaros, ibid., 1039.—Concerning the church of St. Peter at York, ibid., 1042.—Concerning the church of Alia, ibid., 1048.—Concerning the nunnery of St. Mary at Hinsberg, ibid., 1050.—Concerning the monastery of Bonne-Espérance, ibid., 1051.—Concerning the monastery of the Holy Cross at Donauwörth, ibid., 1056.—Concerning the Scottish monastery of St. James at Regensburg, ibid., 1059.—Concerning the church of St. Reparata at Lucca, ibid., 1060.—Concerning the monastery of St. Zeno at Reichenhall, ibid., 1073.—Concerning the church of St. Mary in Uzna, ibid., 1077.—Concerning the Scottish monastery at Würzburg, ibid., 1080.—Concerning the monastery of St. Alexander at Parma, ibid., 1081.—Concerning the monastery of Ranshoven, ibid., 1091.—Concerning the nunnery of Vilich, ibid., 1093.—Concerning the church of Auch, ibid., 1111.—Concerning the church of St. Mary of Newcastle, ibid., 1119.—Concerning the monastery of St. Mary at Gemerode, ibid., 1123.—Concerning the monastery of St. Mary at Dole, ibid., 1133.—Concerning the monastery of St. Mary at Baumgarten, ibid., 1137.—Concerning the church of St. Alban at Basel, ibid., 1148.—Concerning the monastery of St. Maurice at Agaunum, ibid., 1159.—Concerning the church of St. Mary of Porto at Ravenna, ibid., 1165.—Concerning the Church of Paris, ibid., 1468.—Concerning the monastery of the Holy Trinity at Fécamp, ibid., 1173.—Concerning the monastery of Sorø, ibid., 1195.—Concerning the monastery of Capella, ibid., 1196.—Concerning the church of St. Mary and St. John the Evangelist, ibid., 1204.—Concerning the monastery of Wadegozingen, ibid., 1208.—Concerning the monastery of Amelungsborn, ibid., 1226.—Concerning the monastery of Cison, ibid., 1236.—Concerning the monastery of the Place of God, ibid., 1240.

Privileges, bulls, diplomas, immunities, etc.: for Henry the Lion and his sons, CCVI, 892; for the canonization of St. Bernward, bishop, ibid., 970; for the monastery of Fécamp, ibid., 985; for the church of Genoa, ibid., 992; in favour of St. James at Provins, ibid., 1026; for the church of St. Genesius, ibid., 1085; for the monastery of Lucca, ibid., 1091; for the monastery of Bec, ibid., 1120; for the church of the Holy Sepulchre at Jerusalem, ibid., 1142; for the monastery of St. Denis, ibid., 1188; for the monastery of Tepl, ibid., 1229; for the monastery of Murbach, ibid., 1241; for the monastery of St. Modestus at Benevento, ibid., 1243.—Secures for the Church of Porto a concession made by the abbot of St. John at Ravenna, ibid., 867.—Grants various privileges to the prior and convent of Canterbury, ibid., 884.—Confirms the transfer of Berengar, bishop of Huesca, to the metropolitan see of Narbonne, ibid., 886.—Grants Humbert, archbishop of Arles, authority to suppress through ecclesiastical censures disorders which have arisen in Provence, ibid., 897.—Secures certain possessions for Hugh, bishop of Coventry, ibid., 903.—Secures for the clerics of Caen the church of Liemon, ibid., 903.—Secures for the archbishop of Esztergom the right of crowning the king of Hungary, binding the provosts of officials of the royal household by the bond of anathema, and judging in spiritual causes, ibid.—Confirms, in letters issued to the archbishop of Esztergom, the liberty granted to the provostship of the Church of the Transylvanian Germans, ibid.—Confirms the goods and privileges of William, lord of Montpellier, ibid.—Confirms all goods of Theobald, bishop of Chiusi, and of his church, ibid., 904.—Confirms the privilege of the monastery of St. Augustine at Canterbury concerning the abbot’s blessing, ibid., 907.—Confirms for the monastery of St. Augustine at Canterbury the prebend of Gustone for the monks’ clothing, and the church of Northbourne with its chapels for the use of the almonry, ibid.—Confirms the goods and privileges of the monastery of Murbach, ibid., 911.—Secures for the chapter of Genoa the authorization granted by Joscius, archbishop of Tyre, to establish a chapel in the city of Tyre, ibid., 913.—At the request of Bishop Bentivolus, confirms the possessions of the Church of Gubbio, ibid., 917.—Secures certain churches for the monastery of Cluny, ibid., 918.—Confirms the liberties of the Scottish Church, ibid., 921.—Grants the abbot of the monastery of St. Sixtus at Piacenza the use of a ring, ibid., 922.—Secures for the convent of Uxelles the chapel of the Holy Cross in Auvergne, situated in the territory of Camalaria, ibid., 934.—Grants the abbot of the monastery of St. Denis authority, notwithstanding a frivolous appeal, freely to discharge the duty of his office in correcting monks and lay brothers, ibid., 942.—Secures for the canons of the church of SS. Peter and Andrew at Paderborn the estate of Helmgerdere and privileges concerning the election of provosts and bishops, ibid., 947.—Grants all Carthusian priors and brethren that no prior or brother among them may have leave to appeal without the consent and will of the chapter of his own house, or of its greater and sounder part, ibid., 952.—Confirms the possessions and rights of the canons of the church of St. Mary at Savona, ibid., 953.—Confirms certain privileges of the prior and Carthusian brethren, ibid., 957.—Confirms the privileges of the monastery of St. Mary at Pomposa, ibid., 958.—Secures for the abbot and convent of Cîteaux the church of Schardeburg, donated by Richard, king of England, ibid., 961.—Approves the foundation of the church of St. Peter at Marchtal, ibid., 966.—Secures for the prior and brethren of the Hospital of Jerusalem the church of Reichartfrod, ibid., 968.—Secures for Absalon, bishop of Lund, that the castle of Hafn shall pass after his death to the church of Roskilde, ibid., 983.—Secures for the monastery of Stringad the goods bestowed by Duke Welf, ibid., 1028.—Exempts the priory of Bromholm from the jurisdiction of the monks of Acre, ibid., 1031.—Grants Roger, abbot of the monastery of St. Severinus at Naples, the use of a ring, ibid., 1051.—Confirms certain possessions of the canons of Maurienne, ibid., 1065.—Secures for the church of St. Donatian at Bruges the legacy established in the testament of Margaret, formerly countess of Flanders, ibid., 1069.—Secures for the monastery of Raitenhaslach the chapel of Ceidiarn, ibid., 1072.—Entrusts Hubert, archbishop of Canterbury, with the legation of the Apostolic See, ibid., 107 [lacuna].—And similar privileges are still read from cols. 1075 to 1240.

DAGOBERT I, king of the Franks.—Diploma by which he transfers the abbey of St. Maurice, or the monastery of Tholey, to the church of St. Peter at Trier, LXXX, 499.—Diploma by which he confirms the possessions of the church of Blessed Peter at Trier; orders that the cell of St. Hilary, or of St. Maximin, remain under the right of this church; and gives both an advocate, Arnulf, duke of Moselle Austrasia, ibid., 501.—Diploma by which he confirms the possessions of the church of Blessed Peter at Trier; orders that the cell of Blessed Eucharius, or of St. Matthias, remain under the right of this church; and gives both an advocate, Arnulf, duke of Moselle Austrasia, ibid., 504.—Diploma by which he transfers to the basilica of Worms possessions of his own right in the district of Ladenburg, and confirms its possessions with immunities, ibid., 505.—Diploma by which he confirms a portion of goods divided between Ursinus and his brother Beppolenus, ibid., 507.—Order by which he commands Desiderius to assume the bishopric of Cahors, ibid., 508.—Diploma by which he establishes the market of St. Denis, ibid., 510.—That Desiderius’s consecration as bishop of Cahors shall take place at the Easter solemnity, ibid., 512.—Diploma concerning many churches built by himself in honour of St. Denis and made subject to the principal church of Denis, ibid., 514.—Diploma by which he confers the right of asylum upon the monastery of St. Denis, ibid., 515.—Declares and confirms all property belonging to the church of Blessed Peter at Trier, ibid., 517.—Diploma by which he gives Sigirannus the place Longoretum for constructing a monastery, and Milepecum for constructing a basilica, ibid., 519.—Diploma by which, after an inquiry into the origins of the monastery of St. Maximin, he grants it privileges and confirms donations made to it, while himself conferring new gifts, ibid., 522.—Diploma for the foundation of the monastery of Haslach, ibid., 524.—Diploma by which he bestows gifts and grants privileges upon the church at Wissembourg founded by him, ibid., 527.—Concerning the foundation of the church of the Holy Cross of St. Ouen, [Col. 0078] ibid., 530.—Diploma by which he gives the monastery of St. Denis the estate of Vallis and the estate of Argenteriae, ibid., 533.—Diploma by which he grants Landelin the estate of Wallare in the forest of Fania, with very many appurtenances, to build a monastery there, ibid., 533.—Diploma by which he gives the estate of Sarclidas to the poor matricularii of St. Denis, ibid., 535.—Diploma by which he gives the estate of Aquapula to the monastery of St. Denis, ibid., 536.—Diploma concerning the foundation of the monastery of Resbach and the immunities granted to it, ibid., 537.—Diploma by which he gives the monks of St. Denis the estates of Tauriacum, Tibernion, Rubrida, Monarville, and the Valley of Vascon, ibid., 539.—Diploma by which he gives Mouliac to the monks of St. Denis, ibid., 540.—Diploma by which he makes many gifts to the monastery of St. Denis in the borderlands of Limousin and Berry, ibid., 543.—Diploma by which he gives the estates of Noth and Porcellarium to the monks of St. Denis, ibid., 546.—Diploma by which he grants the estate of Hicenascoa to the church of St. Denis, ibid., 547.—Diploma by which he grants Bishop Amandus a place between the rivers Elnon and Scarpe, suitable for organizing there those who serve God, ibid., 548.—Diploma by which he grants the monastery of St. Denis immunity from every authority, ibid., 550, 552.—Diploma by which he grants Ruilliac and many other gifts to the monastery of St. Denis, ibid., 554.—Diploma by which he gives the matricularii of the church of St. Denis the estates of Acuciacum, Cosdunum, and many others, ibid., 556.—Diploma by which he gives the estate of Esterpiniacum to the basilica of St. Denis, ibid., 557.—Diploma by which he gives the monastery of St. Denis the estate of Giuretis, ibid., 559.—Diploma by which he orders that the children of bondsmen or slaves of the monastery of St. Denis be subject in perpetuity, with their offspring, to the servile law of ecclesiastical dependants, ibid., 560.—Diploma by which the precarial charter of Sigrannus, abbot of Anisole, and Hadoindus, bishop of Le Mans, concerning the monastery of Anisole, is confirmed, ibid., 561.—Diploma by which he gives the church of Plumbata and other churches, with appurtenances, to the church of St. Denis, and grants it privileges, ibid., 562.—Diploma by which he confers many gifts upon the oratory of Blessed Mary at Cambrai, ibid., 364.

DEODUINUS, bishop of Liège.—Privilege for the collegiate church of Blessed Mary at Huy; makes it an extremely generous donation at its dedication and chooses it as his burial place, CXLVI, 1443.—Establishes fifteen canons in the church at Huy, ibid., 1446.

EGIDIUS, monk.—Makes a notable donation to the monastery of Prüm, XCVI, 1552.

EGINHARD, abbot.—Charter by which, with the consent of his wife Imma, he grants the cell of Michelstadt with its appurtenances to the monastery of Lorsch, retaining its usufruct, CIV, 601.—Charter of Eginhard, abbot of the monastery of St. Servatius the Confessor, by which he formally manumits Meginfrid, a serf of that monastery, who has been chosen for holy orders, ibid., 603.—Charter of Eginhard, abbot of St. Bavo at Ghent, by which he grants Nordbert in precaria certain property which the latter had conveyed to the monastery of Blandinium, ibid., 605.

EUGENIUS II, pope.—Privilege for the church of St. Peter at Rouen, CXXIX, 985.—Letters in favour of the monastery of Agaunum, ibid., 987.—Privilege for the monastery of Lauriacum, ibid., 989.

EUGENIUS III, pope.—Confirms the possessions of the Church of Huesca, CLXXX, 1015.—Concerning the monastery of the Holy Trinity of Curba-Fossa, ibid., 1017.—Privilege for the monastery of St. John at Kaltenborn, ibid., 1018.—Confirms the privilege of the brethren of St. Frigidianus at Lucca, ibid., 1020.—Privilege confirming the liberty and all the goods of the Church of the Greater Monastery, ibid., 1022.—Granting of privileges to the monastery of St. Saviour in the diocese of Pavia, ibid., 1026.—Privilege for the monastery of St. Peter at Perugia, ibid., 1029.—For the monastery of St. Bertin at Sithiu, ibid., 1031.—Confirms the exchange between the monastery of St. Bertin at Sithiu and Theodoric, count of Flanders, and that monastery’s privilege concerning the election at Alchias, ibid., 1832.—Takes the monastery of St. George at Prague under the protection of the Apostolic See and confirms its possessions, ibid., 1032.—Confirms donations made to the monastery of Scheyern in Bavaria by nobles, bishops, and others of Germany, ibid., 1034.—Privilege for the nunnery of Fontevraud, ibid., 1037.—Privilege for the church of St. Mary at Verona, ibid., 1038.—For the monastery of St. Mary of the Dove, ibid., 1041.—Takes the monastery of Litomyšl under the protection of the Apostolic See and confirms its possessions, ibid., 1045.—Privilege for the monastery of St. Saviour, ibid., 1046.—For the church of St. Peter at Guastalla, ibid., 1048.—For the abbey of St. Mary at Châtillon, ibid., 1050.—Bull in favour of Albert, abbot of St. Theodard, ibid., 1051.—Privilege for the church of Berchtesgaden, [Col. 0079] ibid., 1057.—Takes the monastery of SS. Peter and Paul at Hadmersleben under protection and confirms its privileges and possessions, ibid., 1059.—Confirmation, or renewal and new grant, of privileges to the Benedictine monastery of St. John the Evangelist in the diocese of Parma, CLXXX, 1059.—Confirms the possessions and privileges of the monastery of Molesme, ibid., 1062.—Grants an indulgence to those devoted to Blessed James, ibid., 1063.

Privilege for the monastery of St. Stephen at Freising, CLXXX, 1066.—For the monastery of the Restored Place, ibid., 1067.—For the monastery of St. Remigius at Reims, ibid., 1069.—For the Carthusians of Mont-Dieu, ibid., 1071.—For the monastery of Belleval, ibid., 1072.—For the monastery of St. Mary at Cuissy, ibid., 1074.—For the church of St. John the Evangelist at Ravenna, ibid., 1077.—Takes the church of Blessed Peter at Regensburg under protection and confirms its possessions, ibid., 1078.—Privilege for the monastery of St. Mary at Springiersbach, ibid., 1080.—For the church of St. John at Kaltenborn, ibid., 1084.—For the monastery of St. Mary in Regula, ibid., 1085.—Takes the monastery of St. Peter at Ghent, or Blandinium, under protection and confirms its goods and privileges, ibid., 1087.—Privilege for the nunnery of Faremoutiers, ibid., 1089.—For the monastery of St. Lambert at Suben, ibid., 1091.—For the monastery of St. Michael of the Mountain, ibid., 1092.—Confirmation of all goods and privileges granted to the monastery of Tronçay by the supreme Roman pontiffs, ibid., 1093.—Bull confirming the goods of the monastery of Crisenon, ibid., 1096.—Bull in favour of the monastery of St. Marian, ibid., 1097.—Privilege for the monastery of St. Zeno at Reichenhall, ibid., 1099.—For the monastery of Casa Dei, ibid., 1102.—For the monastery of Nantua, ibid., 1103.—For the monastery of Mortemer, ibid., 1104.—For the monastery of Cluny, ibid., 1105.—For the church of St. Martin at Buron, ibid., 1107.

Bull for St. Evurtius at Orléans, ibid., 1109.—Privilege for the church of St. Mary at Parma, ibid., 1111.—For the church of St. Andrew at Rochester, ibid., 1113.—Confirms the rights and possessions of the canons regular of the church of Blessed Peter at Tarentaise, etc., ibid., 1114.—Privilege for the monastery of SS. Peter and Paul at Westminster, ibid., 1116.—Concerning the primacy of Peter, archbishop of Bourges, over the provinces of Bourges and Bordeaux, ibid., 1119.—Bull confirming the goods and immunities of Tongerlo, ibid., 1120.—Commends Anselm, bishop of Tournai, whom he had consecrated, ibid., 1122.—Privilege for the monastery of St. Peter at Salzburg, ibid., 1125.—For the monastery of St. Nicasius at Reims, ibid., 1127.—Confirms privileges for the monastery of Fleury, ibid., 1129.—Privilege for the nunnery of Blessed Mary in the Forest of Nyd-Merli, ibid., 1130.—For the canons of the church of St. Ursus at Aosta, ibid., 1133.—For the monastery of Reichersberg, ibid., 1134.—For the monastery of SS. Peter and Paul at Paderborn, ibid., 1137.—For the church of St. Lawrence at Clerholt, ibid., 1139.—Confirms the rights of the monastery of Varlar concerning election of the abbot and presentation of the advocacy, ibid., 1141.—Takes the church of St. Mary and St. Blaise at Fridesel under protection and confirms its possessions, ibid., 1142.—Privilege for the monastery of Stavelot, ibid., 1144.—Takes the Church of the Holy Sepulchre at Jerusalem under protection and confirms its possessions, ibid., 1145.—Confirms the bishopric of Tournai as exempt from the authority of the bishops of Noyon, ibid., 1151.—Bull for the monastery of Gellone, ibid., 1154.

Privilege for the church of St. Zeno at Halle, CLXXX, 1156.—For the church of St. Donatian at Bruges, ibid., 1158.—For the monastery of Petersberg, ibid., 1160, 1163.—For the monastery of St. George in the diocese of Protening, ibid., 1165.—For the monastery of St. Margaret at Osterhofen, ibid., 1167.—For the monastery of Windberg, ibid., 1168.—For the monastery of St. Mary at Abingdon, ibid., 1170.

The order of Regular Canons of St. Augustine, established at Klosterneuburg, together with its other privileges and immunities, both temporal and spiritual, is confirmed by apostolic authority, CLXXX, 1172.—Grants Eberhard, bishop of Bamberg, the right to wear the pallium and other privileges, ibid., 1175.—Restores and commends Henry, bishop of Moravia, to Conrad, king of the Romans, ibid., 1175.—Privilege for the monastery of St. Nicholas of Sept-Fonts, ibid., 1176.—Confirms the possessions and privileges of the monastery of St. Augustine at Canterbury, ibid., 1177.—Establishes Hugh, archbishop of Tours, as metropolitan both of Dol and of the other bishops of Lesser Brittany, ibid., 1183.—Confirms the possessions and privileges of the monastery of Vives, ibid., 1185.—Privilege for the monastery of Raitenhaslach, ibid., [Col. 0080] 1186.—Bull for the Camaldolese congregation, ibid., 1187.—Privilege for the nunnery of St. Peter of Le Luc, ibid., 1190.—For the monastery of St. Peter at Pozzuoli, in the diocese of Lucca, ibid., 1192.—For the monastery of St. Denis, ibid., 1194.—Confirms the privileges and possessions of the abbey of SS. Solutor and Adventor at Turin, ibid., 1196.

Privilege for the monastery of Bonneval, of the Cistercian Order, CLXXX, 1198.---For the nunnery of Tart, ibid., 1199.---For the church of St. Pancras at Ranshoven, ibid., 1201.---For the monastery of Fesmy, ibid., 1204.---For the monastery of St. Mary of Thenolles, ibid., 1206.---For the monastery of Ferrières, ibid., 1207.---For the monastery of Grimbergen, ibid., 1209.---For the church of St. Martin of Laon, of the Premonstratensian Order, ibid., 1210.---For the monastery of St. Lawrence at Liège, ibid., 1213.---Bull in favour of Walter, abbot of St. Mary of Chapel-at-the-Planks, ibid., 1214.---Privilege for the monastery of Belleau, ibid., 1215.---For the Premonstratensian monastery, ibid., 1217.---For the monastery of Calmont, of the Premonstratensian Order, ibid., 1221.---Confirms all goods and possessions of the monastery of St. Mary of Soissons, ibid., 1223.---Privilege for the monastery of St. Mary of Vaverley, ibid., 1226.---Bull in favour of the monastery of Tiron, ibid., 1228.---Privilege for the church of St. Mary of Brane, ibid., 1231.---For the monastery of Jandun, ibid., 1233.---For the churches subject to the bishop of Paris, ibid., 1234.---Bull for the nunnery of St. Denis at Montmartre, ibid., 1236.---Privilege for the monastery of St. Martin-in-the-Fields, ibid., 1239.---Bull concerning the dedication of the church of Montmartre, ibid., 1242.---Privilege for the monastery of St. Heribert at Deutz, ibid., 1244.---For the monastery of St. Quentin of the Mount, ibid., 1215.---Bull to Ivo, abbot, and the monks of Redon, confirming their privileges, ibid., 1247.

Privilege for the monastery of St. Martin-in-the-Fields, CLXXX, 1250.---For the church of St. Saviour of Saragossa, ibid., 1252.---For the monastery of St. Mary of Lucelle, ibid., 1254.---For the church of St. Mary of Dieu-le-Lieu, ibid.---For the monastery of Trunchin, ibid., 1259.---For the monastery of St. Mary of the Christian Valley, ibid., 1260.---Receives the monastery of St. Mary of New Castle (Neuenburg) under the protection of the Apostolic See, ibid., 1262.---Bull confirming the church of Libenstadt, ibid., 1263.---Receives under the protection of the Apostolic See the Cistercian monastery of St. Mary of Aldersbach, ibid., 1265.---Privilege for the monastery of St. Mary of Huntingdon, ibid., 1266.---Bull confirming the possessions of the abbey of St. Mary of Bertin’s Court, or Moncel, ibid., 1268.---Privilege for the monastery of Riguia, ibid., 1269.---Declares that Berne Monastery was granted to Cluny by William, count of Mâcon, ibid., 1272.---Bull confirming the goods and immunities of the church of Stivagium, ibid., 1274.---Privilege for the monastery of Yergua, ibid., 1278.---For the monastery of St. Mary of Nienzabas, ibid., 1279.---For the monastery of St. Vitus of Prüfening, ibid., 1280.---Confirms the union of the Savigniac brethren with the Cistercian Order, ibid., 1282.

Privilege for the monastery of St. John of Reomay, ibid., 1285.---Concerning the monastery of St. Mary of Jette, ibid.---Concerning the nunnery of St. Mary of Helder, ibid., 1287.---Concerning Christ Church, London, ibid., 1289.---Concerning the nunnery of the Holy Spirit at the Paraclete, ibid., 1291.---Concerning the monastery of St. Augustine at Saint-Omer, ibid., 1295.---Receives the church of St. Albin at Basel under his protection and confirms each of its possessions by name, ibid., 1297.---Privilege for the monastery of Lake, ibid., 1301.---Undertakes the protection of the monastery of St. Peter in the Black Forest and confirms its goods, ibid., 1302.---Concerning the monastery of Heilsbronn, ibid., 1303.

Privilege for the monastery of St. Mary of Lonnay, CLXXX, 1304.---Undertakes the protection of the monastery of St. Disibod and confirms its goods and privileges, ibid., 1307.---Privilege for the monastery of Bonifaz, ibid.---For the church of the Holy Apostles on Mount Cornelius at Liège, ibid., 1309.---For the monastery of St. Mary of Longpont, ibid., 1311.---Confirms the privileges and goods of the monastery of Benediktbeuern, ibid., 1312.---Privilege for the monastery of Lorsch, ibid., 1314.---Confirms the privileges and possessions of the monastery of Maulbronn, ibid., 1316.---Privilege for the monastery of Helmershausen, ibid., 1317.---Privilege confirming all the goods of the monastery of Niederaltaich, or Lower Altaich, in the diocese of Salzburg, ibid., 1318.---Privilege for the church of St. Mary of Cambrai, ibid., 1321.---Confirms the altars, possessions, and privileges of the abbey of Ename, of the Order of St. Benedict in the diocese of Mechelen, ibid., 1325.---Receives the church of Włocławek into his faith and protection [Col. 0081], and confirms the boundaries of the bishopric and the limits of the diocese of Włocławek established by Giles, bishop of Tusculum, and Bolesław, duke of Poland, ibid., 1328.---Confirms a perpetual prebend for St. Martin in the church of Amiens, ibid., 1331.---Undertakes the protection of the monastery of
