Saints Facundus and Primitivus at Sahagún, and confirms its privileges and possessions, ibid., 1332.---Bull for the abbey of St. Mary of Flabemont, ibid.---Privilege for the nunnery of St. Andrew at Göss, ibid., 1335.---Receives the monastery of St. Giles of Canawella under his protection, ibid., 1336.---Privilege for the monastery of St. Thierry at Reims, ibid.---For the abbey of St. Denis at Paris, ibid., 1339.---For the monastery of St. Remigius at Reims, ibid., 1342.---For the monastery of St. Mary of Basse-Fontaine, ibid., 1343.---Undertakes the protection of the monastery of Thelon, and confirms its Premonstratensian discipline and its goods, ibid., 1345.---Confirms the primacy of Toledo, ibid.---Privilege for the monastery of Bellelay, ibid., 1352.---Undertakes the protection of the monastery of Rüeggisberg and confirms its possessions, ibid., 1354.---Concerning the monastery of Clairvaux at Milan, ibid.---Privilege for the monastery of Toul, ibid., 1356.---Bull for the church of St. Ambrose at Milan, ibid., 1358.---Undertakes the protection of the nunnery of St. Maurice at Milan and confirms its possessions, ibid., 1360.---Concerning the monastery of St. Saviour, ibid., 1361.---Bull for the canonry of St. Antoninus at Florence, ibid.---Confirms all the goods and complete exemption of the monastery of St. Saviour and the martyr Julia, in the diocese of Brescia, of the Cassinese Order, and grants other privileges, ibid., 1363.---Privilege for the church of Blessed Mary at Brescia, ibid., 1366.---Confirms the monastery of St. Mary in the Sand at Wrocław, ibid., 1369.---Privilege for the church of St. Mary of Luni, ibid., 1371.---Bull confirming to the Camaldolese hermitage the gifts of Jerome, bishop of Arezzo, ibid., 1372.---Bull for the nunnery of St. Hilary, situated in the bishopric of Fiesole, ibid., 1374.---Bull for the convent of nuns of St. Martin of Agello, ibid., 1375.---For the abbot of St. Mary of Morrona, ibid., 1377.---For the hermitage of Fonte Avellana, ibid., 1383.---Privilege for the monastery of St. Peter at Modena, ibid., 1384.---For the monastery of St. Peter at Salzburg, ibid., 1387.---Concerning the monastery of St. Lucius of Chur, ibid., 1400.---Bull to Oberto, archbishop of Milan, ibid., 1403.---Concerning the primacy of Toledo, ibid., 1405.---Confirms the canonical discipline of the brethren of St. Laud at Rouen, ibid., 1408.---Privilege for the monastery of St. Martin of Auneau, ibid., 1409.---For the monastery of St. Benedict at Piacenza, ibid., 1411.---Grants to Guibert, provost, and the canons of St. Lawrence of Genoa an extensive confirmation of all goods and rights, including the donation of Count Raymond, ibid.---Privilege for the church of Fontaine-d’Ébray, ibid., 1413.---Confirms the goods, possessions, and privileges of St. Mary of Reno, ibid., 1415.---Undertakes the protection of the monastery of St. Nicholas at Angers, etc., ibid., 1419.---Confirms all goods, donations, and exemptions of the monastery of St. Quirinus at Tegernsee, which is declared subject to the ordinary bishop in spiritual matters, ibid., 1425.---Confirms the privileges and immunities of the canonry of St. Mary of Mont-Bel, ibid., 1428.---Privilege for the church of canons of Blessed Mary at Raitenbuch, in the diocese of Freising, ibid., 1429.---Enumerates the possessions of the abbey of Lobbes, of the Order of St. Benedict in the diocese of Liège, and confirms and enlarges its privileges, ibid., 1431.---Privilege for the monastery of St. Mary at Compiègne, ibid., 1435.---Confirms the possessions of the church of Monopoli, ibid., 1437.---Confirms the privileges and possessions of the monastery of St. Saviour and St. Boniface at Fulda, ibid., 1442.---Concerning the abbey of St. Saviour of Majella, 1444.---Bull for the bishops of Orléans, ibid., 1449.---Privilege for the monastery of the Holy Trinity and St. Michael of Melet, ibid., 1452.---For the Church of Beauvais, ibid., 1454, 1458.---Privilege for the monastery of Michaelstein, ibid., 1460.---Bull for Guarinus, abbot of St. John in the Valley, ibid., 1462.---For Theobald, abbot of St. Caranus, ibid., 1463.---Confirmation of privileges granted to the Order of St. Benedict by various supreme pontiffs, ibid., 1464.---Bull for the monastery of St. Quiricus of the Roses, ibid., 1466.---Confirms the metropolitan rights of Robert, archbishop of Acerenza, and grants him the pallium, ibid., 1467.---Undertakes the protection of the nunnery of St. Cyriacus at Girona, etc., ibid., 1469.---Confirms the privileges of the hospital of St. Blaise, ibid., 1470.---Confirms the goods and privileges of the nunnery of St. Peter Major at Florence, ibid., 1471.---Privilege for the church of Isola, ibid., 1473.---Confirms the possessions of the monastery of St. Mary at Pongartenberg and receives it under his protection, ibid., 1476.---Concerning the nunnery of St. Zacharias at Venice, ibid., 1479.---Privilege for [Col. 0082] the canons of Pistoia, ibid., 1480.---Protective bull issued for the monastery of Esrum, ibid., 1482.---Confirmation of numerous rights and privileges long previously granted to the archbishop, clergy, and canons of the metropolitan church of Cologne, ibid., 1486.---Bull for the monastery of Welschendorf, ibid., 1495.---Privilege for the monastery of Brem, ibid., 1504.---Receives the monastery of Heidenheim under his protection and grants it various privileges, ibid., 1507.---Confirmation of all goods and liberties of the monastery of Rohr, of Canons Regular of St. Augustine in the diocese of Regensburg, ibid., 1511.---Privilege for the church of Coventry, ibid., 1513.---For the monastery of Silviniac, ibid., 1515.---For the church of Treviso, ibid., 1520.---Confirms certain possessions of the monastery of Heilsbronn, ibid., 1522.---Privilege for the church of Trier, ibid., 1525.---For the monastery of Himmerod, ibid., 1527.---For the monastery of Wadegossen, ibid., 1529.---For the abbey of Springiersbach, ibid., 1532.---Confirmation that the advocatial office of Lower Altaich Abbey was transferred from the Empire to the bishop of Bamberg, ibid., 1536.---Bull for St. John of Sens, ibid., 1538.---Confirmation of the Cistercian constitutions, ibid., 1541.---Bull for the canonry of Blessed Mary at Fano, ibid., 1546.---For the monastery of St. John in the Valley of Ture, ibid., 1548.---Privilege concerning all properties of the monastery of St. Mary of Bozlav, ibid., 1551.---Privilege against the archdeacons of Paris, in support of episcopal authority, ibid., 1554.---For the monastery of Saints Lawrence and Hilary, ibid., 1555.---Bull for the church of Constance, ibid., 1557.---Receives into apostolic protection the church of St. Rumold at Mechelen, formerly collegiate and now metropolitan, with all its possessions and tithes, ibid., 1550.---Concerning the abbey of St. Cornelius at Ninove, ibid., 1561.---Privilege for the church of St. Lawrence of Genoa, ibid., 1562.---For the monastery of St. Sylvester on Monte Suavi, ibid., 1567.---For the church of St. Mary of Kapenberg, ibid., 1568.---Confirms Ringelheim Abbey to the church of Hildesheim, ibid., 1570.---Bull for the nunnery of St. Saviour at Évreux, ibid., 1572.---Privilege for the church of Arras, ibid., 1575.---Undertakes the protection of the church of Verden and confirms its possessions and rights, ibid., 1584.---Confirms the primacy of Toledo, ibid., 1585.---Concerning the monastery of Ellwangen, ibid., 1587.---Privilege for the monastery of Cantave, ibid.---For the monastery of Bonneval, ibid., 1588.---Bull by which the monastery of Sarlat, founded by princes Pippin and Charles, is received under the protection of St. Peter, 1591.---Privilege for the church of St. Mary at Asti, ibid., 1594.---For the nunnery of Othmarsheim, ibid., 1597.---For the monastery of Tournus, ibid., 1600.---For the abbey of Conques, ibid., 1601.---For the monastery of St. Benedict of the Saxon Mount of Lateran, ibid., 1603.---Confirms a spurious diploma which King Conrad III is said to have granted to the Church of Utrecht, ibid., 1607.---Confirms the goods and privileges of the monastery of Hildesheim, ibid., 1609.---Bull confirming the Premonstratensian institute at Röttgen and the possessions of that monastery, ibid., 1611.

EVERARD, bishop of Tournai.---Grants various privileges to the chapel of Zantvoorde, CLXXIV, 1580, 1581.

FORMOSUS, pope.---Grants the monks of St. Theuderic immunity and a firm and stable legal right to their goods, CXXIX, 837.---Bull for the church of Girona, ibid., 841.---To Berno, abbot of Gigny: concerning the privileges of that monastery, ibid., 845.

FREDERICK, archbishop of Cologne.---Confirms for the abbot of Corvey the tithes from demesne holdings in his bishopric, formerly granted in a solemn council in the time of Emperor Arnulf, CLXVI, 1352.---Diploma for the monastery of Groffschalt, ibid., 1353.

FREDERICK, emperor.---Charter for the monastery of Baume, CLXXXIX, 1070.

GAUFRIDUS, bishop of Châlons.---Charter of the foundation of the abbey of Monastery in Aragon, CLXXIII, 1395.---Charter by which he confirms gifts made to the monastery of Trois-Fontaines, ibid., 1396.---Privilege for the monastery of St. Peter, ibid., 1398.---Establishes his anniversary commemoration in the Parisian church of St. Martin-in-the-Fields, ibid.---Foundation in the abbey of Mont-Maur, ibid., 1399.

GELASIUS II, pope.---Places Oldegarius, bishop of Barcelona, over the Church of Tarragona and grants him the pallium, CLXIII, 489.---To Pontius, abbot of Cluny: a Cluniac privilege, ibid., 492.---Grants Bernard, abbot of the monastery of St. Sophia at Benevento, a privilege concerning the drawing of water from the river Calore, ibid., 493.---To Walter, archbishop of Ravenna: after he had renounced the schism, confirms his election and grants him the pallium [Col. 0083] with other rights, ibid., 495.---Approves and renews the customs of the canons of Lucca, ibid., 497.---Confirms the rights and liberties of the Canons Regular of St. Frigdianus at Lucca, ibid., 499.---Undertakes the protection of the monastery of St. Manilian, situated on the island of Montecristo, and confirms its possessions and rights, ibid., 500.---Assures the canons of Lucca that, in confirming the privileges of St. Frigdianus’s canons, he has not diminished their rights, ibid., 501.---Bull enumerating and confirming the possessions of Nobilac, ibid., 502.---Confirms the privileges of Bernard, primate of Toledo, ibid., 503.---Bull for the abbey of Lagrasse, ibid., 504.---To the Christian army besieging the city of Saragossa: grants an indulgence to all who contribute anything to it, ibid., 508.---To Pontius, abbot of Cluny: confirms the privileges of the monastery of Cluny, ibid., 509.---Bull for the monastery of Caunes, in the diocese of Narbonne, ibid., 511.---Privilege for the monastery of St. Andrew at Avignon, ibid., 412.

GHISELA, sister of Charlemagne.---Charter by which she grants to the monastery of Saint-Denis many estates received from her parents, XCVII, 984.

GERVASIUS, archbishop of Reims.---Charter of the foundation or restoration of twelve canons in the church of Saints Timothy and Apollinaris, CXLIII, 1401.---Charter for the foundation of the abbey of St. Denis at Reims, ibid., 1402.

GREGORY (St.) II.---Recognizes Tatwine, archbishop of Canterbury, as primate of all England and orders that he be recognized, LXXXIX, 525.---Grants immunity and other privileges to the monastery of St. Maximin at Trier, ibid., 529.

GREGORY IV, pope.---Privilege granted to Abbot Rabanus, CXXIX, 991.---Confirms the goods and privileges of the monastery of St. Justina at Padua, ibid., 993.---Concerning the rank and privileges of the monastery of Fleury, ibid., 995.

GREGORY V, pope.---Extensive privileges for Winizone Abbey and the church of Cambrai, CXXXVII, 901, 904.---Confirms to Abbot Werinfrid its possessions and the right to elect an abbot, first from Stavelot and then from the monastery of Malmedy, ibid., 906.---Privileges for the monastery of St. Martin at Tours and for the church of Ravenna, ibid., 907, 909.---The right of Otto, abbot of Fulda, to celebrate Mass wearing dalmatic and sandals is confirmed, ibid., 912.---Bull for the monastery of Subiaco, ibid., 915.---Privilege for the Church of Piacenza, to which he subjects Montefeltro, ibid., 919.---Confirms the privileges of the abbey of St. Ambrose, ibid., 920.---Letter to Gerbert, bishop of Ravenna, by which he sends him the pallium, adorns the Church of Ravenna with many privileges, and increases it by many gifts, ibid., 921.---Privileges for the monasteries of St. Genesius in the diocese of Bisuldun, of Cluny, and for the church of Montmajour, ibid., 924–932.---Bull for the election of Arnulf as bishop of Ausona, ibid., 928.---Bull confirming the rights of the monastery of Petershausen in the diocese of Constance, ibid., 935.

GREGORY VI, pope.---Bull for Farfa Abbey and its abbot, CXLII, 573.---Gives the church of St. Domninus to the canons of the church of Florence, ibid., 575.---Bull for the monastery of St. Quentin of the Mount, ibid.

GREGORY VII, pope.---Privilege for the Camaldolese hermitage, CXLVIII, 616; and for the monastery of Saints Peter and Hubert, ibid., 653.---Bull for the monastery of Padua, ibid., 659.---Privileges for the monasteries of Cluny, Poitiers, and Gigny, ibid., 661, 663.---Confirms the possessions of the monastery of St. Peter at Condom, ibid., 668.---Receives the monastery of Fonte Avellana under his protection, ibid., 669.---Bull for the church of St. Aubert at Cambrai, ibid., 675.---Undertakes the protection of the Pisan monastery of St. Michael and confirms its goods and rights, ibid., 681.---Privilege for the monastery of St. Saviour of Septimania, ibid., 682.---For the monastery of Holy Cross at Quimperlé, ibid., 684.---For the monastery of St. Benignus at Dijon, ibid., 685.---For the Cassinese monastery, ibid., 888.---For the monastery of St. Zeno at Pisa, ibid., 698.---Confirms all privileges of the church of Palermo, ibid., 702.---Privilege for the church of St. Quentin, ibid., 704.---For the church of St. Sophia at Benevento, ibid., 1710.---Privilege confirming the goods and immunities of the monastery of Hirsau, which is received under the protection of the Apostolic See, ibid., 714.---Bull for the monastery of St. Peter at Juncelles, ibid., 717.---Privilege for the monastery of St. Benedict, ibid., 718.---Confirms the privileges of the church of St. Audomar in Artois, ibid., 717.---Privilege for the church of St. Paul at Rome, ibid.---Privilege for the church of St. Audomar, ibid., 728.---Privilege for the monastery of Vendôme, ibid., 729.---Confirmation of the primacy of the church of Vienne and grant of privileges, ibid., 751.

[Col. 0084] GREGORY VIII, pope.---Undertakes the protection of the monastery of Lucelle and confirms its possessions and rights, CCII, 1543.---Privilege for the monastery of La Charité at Foulain, ibid., 1546.---Confirms the Order of Calatrava and its possessions, ibid., 1548.---Commends Lanfranc, bishop-elect, ibid., 1549.---Exempts the canons of the Venetian church of St. Saviour from payment of tithes, ibid., 1552.---Undertakes the protection of the Venetian church of St. Saviour and confirms its privileges, ibid., 1553.---Privilege for the church of St. Apollinaris, ibid., 1555.---Confirms the privilege of the abbot of Tegernsee, established by Otto, bishop of Freising, ibid., 1560.---Confirms the possessions and privileges of the canons of the church of Genoa, ibid., 1564.---Declares the church of St. Christina of Clano to belong to the monastery of St. Mary of Agnano, ibid.

GUARINUS, bishop of Amiens.---Charter for the monastery of Cluny granting two altars, CLXXXIX, 1065.

GUIDO, count of Flanders.---Diploma concerning all minor tithes of the whole parish of Aldenburg, etc., CLXXIV, 1585.

GUIDO OF CHÂTILLON, archbishop of Reims.---Privilege granted to Odila, abbess of the nunnery of St. Peter, CXLII, 1405.---Confirms Manasses’s gift of certain lands, ibid., 1408.

WILLIAM, abbot of St. Benignus at Dijon.---Privilege for the monastery of Fruttuaria, CXLI, 871.

WILLIAM, archbishop of Besançon.---Confirms to Cluny the possessions of Haute-Pierre, CLXVI, 247.

HATO, bishop of Troyes.---Gift of the churches of Barbonne, etc., to the monastery of Cluny, CLXXXIX, 1066.

HEDDO, bishop of Strasbourg.---Testament by which he founds and endows the monastery of Ettenheim, XCVI, 1547.

HEDENUS, illustrious man.---Charter by which he makes gifts to Willibrord, bishop of Utrecht, CXXXIX, 535.

HENRY I, king of the Franks.---Confirms to the monastery of St. Saviour at Montreuil the gifts made to that place by his grandfather Hugh and his father Robert, CLI, 1225.---Plea for the monastery of St. Medard against Robert of Clichy, ibid., 1027.---Grants the canons of Chartres the free fiscal estate of Unigrad, ibid., 1028.---Privilege for the monastery of St. Thierry near Reims. Assisted by Abbot Albert in the capture of Châteauneuf, he frees that monastery from the yoke of advocates and the vexations of archdeacons, ibid., 1029.---Privilege for the monastery of La Chaise-Dieu, ibid., 1031.---Charter for the monastery of St. Victor at Nevers: the abbey of St. Victor at Nevers, rescued from lay control, is restored, ibid., 1032.---Charter concerning freedom restored to a certain Arnald, ibid., 1034.---Charter for the monastery of St. Peter, ibid., 1036.---Gives the churches of Saints Stephen, Julian, Severinus, and Bacchus to the canons of Paris, ibid., 1038.---Grants to the Church of Paris the small abbey of St. Germanus at Laie, ibid., 1039.

HENRY I, emperor.---Concerning the royal rights granted to Blessed Peter, XCVIII, 625.

HENRY II (St.), Emperor Augustus.---Gives Abbot Godehard of Niederaltaich a plot situated at Regensburg, CXL, 239.---Gives the monastery of Tegernsee a plot situated at Regensburg, ibid., 240.---Gives to the Old Chapel, restored by himself as a royal chapel, the estate of Duveninga belonging to his own right, with its appurtenances, ibid., 240.---Gives the bishop of Brixen a plot situated at Regensburg, ibid., 241.---A grant of *mundiburdium*—royal protection—to the Lower Monastery, ibid., 242.---Gives to the collegiate church at the Old Chapel in Regensburg the estate of Welchina in the district of Nordgau, ibid., 243.---Gives the bishop of Brixen the estate of Teigni near Regensburg, ibid., 244.---Writ by which he assigns to Burchard, bishop of Worms, all the property which Duke Otto held in that city, ibid., 245.

Privilege granted to Lady Godesdihu, abbess of Herford monastery, CXL, 246.---For New Corvey, ibid., 247.---For the church of Paderborn, ibid., 248, 249.---Grants Nonantola Abbey to Sigifred, bishop of Parma, ibid., 250.---Privilege for the church of Hamburg, ibid.---Diploma for the nunnery of Möllenbeck, by which he confirms privileges granted to it by Emperors Arnulf and Otto II and gives it the unrestricted power to elect its abbess, ibid., 251.---Confirms the possessions of the Benedictine monastery of St. Bavo at Ghent, ibid., 252.---Diploma granting Count Adalbero the ban over wild beasts, ibid., 254.---Privilege granted to Abbess Frederema, ibid., 255.---Diploma granted to the monastery of virgins at Keminade, ibid., 256.---Confirms and increases the privileges and possessions of the church of Como, [Col. 0085] ibid., 257.---Diploma by which he grants the estate of Pipinesdorf to the church of Worms, ibid., 258.---Gives to the Old Chapel a certain estate of his own right in Nordgau and everything he possessed in the two estates of Durnin and Mantalahi, ibid., 260.---Gives the Lower Monastery an estate in the courts of Regensburg, that is, in Regensburger Burgfrieden, ibid.---The monastery of Steinen, transferred from Duellio, is endowed by Henry II and subjected to the church of Bamberg, ibid., 261.---Confirms the foundation of the college of canons in the church of Holy Cross at Liège, made by Notger, bishop of Liège, ibid., 264.---Gives certain estates to the monastery of Altaich, ibid., 265.---Renews for the monastery of St. Maximin the immunities and privileges granted by his predecessors, ibid., 266.---Confirms and increases the privileges and possessions of the church of Como, ibid., 267.---Writ by which he confirms to the Church of Worms all its possessions and adds others, ibid., 268.---Confirms to Notger, bishop of Liège, and his successors the abbeys and collegiate churches of Lobbes, St. Hubert, Brogne, Gembloux, Fosses, Malonne, etc., ibid., 269.---Receives Landulf, bishop of Cremona, under his *mundiburdium*, ibid., 271.---Gives the place called Kircheim to Steinen monastery, ibid.---Diploma by which he gives the county of Cambrai to the metropolitan Church of Cambrai and to Bishop Herluin and his successors, ibid., 273.---Letters concerning the bishopric of Bamberg established by him, ibid.---Makes a benefaction to the college of noble canonesses at Thorn on the Meuse, ibid., 275.---Gives Kitzingen Abbey to the archbishopric of Bamberg, ibid.

A certain foundation made by him, CXL, 276.---Gives a place of his own property called Plering for the support of the canons of Bamberg, ibid., 277.---Gives to the church of Bamberg, established by himself, as its own possession his proprietary abbey, or Old Chapel, ibid., 278.---Writ by which he assigns to the Church of Worms everything which Count Becelin held as a benefice, ibid.---Diploma by which he transfers Meiningen and Walldorf to the Church of Würzburg in exchange for other goods in the district of Ratenzgau, assigned to the new bishopric of Bamberg, ibid., 279.---Privilege for the Church of Vicenza, ibid., 280.---Gives Bishop Balderic of Liège and Count Balderic the ban over wild animals in the woods they possessed, ibid., 281.---Gives Niederaltaich monastery the parish church at Mandraching, with its tithes and a holding there, etc., ibid., 282.---Gives Prüfening monastery near Regensburg a royal holding in the estate of Genstall, ibid., 283.---Gives the church of Bamberg the place of Litchtowa in the district of Nordgau, ibid., 284.---Writ for the church of Cremona and the Abbey of St. Apollinaris at Classe, ibid., 286.---Privileges granted to Abbot Godehard, ibid., 287, 288.---Grants many estates to the church of Nortwald, situated in a wilderness, ibid., 288.---Gives the nunnery of Obermünster, built by himself from its foundations and consecrated in his presence, a court called Salach belonging to his own right, ibid., 289.---Gives the estate of Clarissa to the church of Bamberg, ibid., 290.---Privilege for the church of Altaich, ibid., 291.---Diploma issued for the monastery of Tegernsee, ibid., 292.---Diploma by which he adds the whole county in the district of Lobdengau to the other dominions of the Church of Worms, ibid., 293.---Privilege for the church of Paderborn, ibid.---Pious gifts of King Henry himself and the conveyance of Zunderenhart Forest and of Lupence March, ibid., 294, 295, 296.---Diploma confirming Flerins Abbey, a Benedictine house in the diocese of Liège, ibid., 298.---Gives the church of Bamberg the place of Irnsing in the district of Kelesgau and the county of Wittelsbach, ibid., 299.---Privilege for the monastery of St. Benedict of Monte Cassino, ibid., 300.---Confirms the possessions and privileges of the church of Bergamo, badly treated by Bishop Reginfred, ibid., 302.---Grants the court of Berneshuson to the church of Paderborn, ibid., 303.---Confirms the privileges and possessions of that church of Paderborn, ibid., 304.---Confirms to Peter, bishop and abbot of St. Michael at Porcariana, his goods and rights, ibid., 305.---Diploma for the monastery of St. Saviour at Fontenay-Tan, ibid., 306.---Confirms the privileges of the Mantuan *arimanni*, ibid., 307.---Confirms and enlarges the privileges of the church of Hamburg, ibid., 309.---Confirms the privileges of the church of Treviso, ibid., 310.---Restores to the bishop of Novara the rights of his church taken away by Margrave Arduin, ibid., 311.---Confirms and enlarges the possessions of the church of Savona, ibid., 313, 314.---Privilege for the monastery of Saints Peter, Lawrence, and Columbanus, ibid., 314.---Letters by which he delivers Schwarzach Abbey for possession to Werenhar, bishop of Strasbourg, and his successors, ibid., 317.---Gives the Abbey of St. Michael certain estates outside the city of Bamberg, [Col. 0086] ibid., 320.---Confirms the possessions of the Abbey of St. Vitonus, ibid., 321.---Confirmation of the rights and privileges of the convent of holy virgins of St. Saviour at Lucca, ibid., 322.---Secures Count Bernard of Parma in possession of the estate of Neromiana, ibid., 323.---Gives the court of Honstede to the church of Paderborn, ibid., 325.---Gives the church of Bamberg the two places Schwarzenfeld and Wellendorf in Nordgau, ibid., 326.---Grants Bishop Alberic of Como the court or estate of Barzanorum, ibid., 327.---Grants certain estates to the church of Paderborn, ibid., 328, 329, 330, 331, 332, 339.

Diploma for the Abbey of St. Peter of Piro, CXL, 335.---Foundation of the collegiate church of Prüm, ibid., 337.---Grants to Poppo and the church of Trier the court of Confluentes with all appurtenances, ibid., 338.---Founds and endows the collegiate body of canons of St. Adelbert at Aachen, ibid., 340.---Confirms the possessions of the Abbey of St. Ghislain in Hainaut, ibid., 341.---Gives the place of Berga, formerly belonging to the Old Chapel, to the Church of Bamberg, ibid., 342.---Diploma by which he grants the monastery of Tegernsee two royal holdings situated at Liupana, ibid., 343.---Privilege for two holdings situated near Liupana, ibid., 344.---Privilege for the church of Mimigernaford, ibid., 345.---Gives the church of Paderborn Sceldice Abbey and the court of Hammonstedi, etc., ibid., 346, 350, 356.---By his diploma confirms to Farfa Abbey of St. Mary goods newly acquired by the monks themselves, ibid., 347.---Grants certain estates to the abbot of Altaich, ibid., 349.---Confirms all goods of the monastery of St. Emmeram generally, ibid., 357, 358.---Gives the Upper Monastery two lands near Regensburg, ibid., 359.---Diploma granted to Amatus, archbishop of Salerno, by which he confirms all his rights, ibid., 360.---Confirms to Romuald, founder of the Camaldolese hermits, the abbey of St. Benedict in the Alps, situated at Bifulcum, ibid., 362.---Privilege for the monastery of St. Sophia at Benevento, ibid., 363.---Gives the church of Bamberg the estate of Hormunze, which he had received from Archbishop Poppo, ibid., 366.---Confirms to Echternach monastery the right of coinage, ibid., 367.---Diploma for Moyenmoutier Abbey, ibid., 371.---Confirms the privileges of the church of Bergamo, ibid., 374.---Confirms the privileges of Murbach monastery and its right to elect an abbot, ibid., 375.---Gives the estate of Steini to the church of Paderborn, ibid., 377.---Privilege for the church of Paderborn, ibid., 378, 379.---Confirms and enlarges the privileges and possessions of the church of Novara, ibid., 382.

HENRY III, emperor.---Privilege for Corvey monastery and Herford nunnery, CLI, 1085, 1089, 1096.---Confirms the possessions and immunities of Stavelot monastery, ibid., 1091.---Privilege for the monastery of St. Peter at Minden, ibid., 1094.---Confirmation of the rights and privileges of the Church of Mantua, ibid., 1097.---Diploma by which he confirms all goods of the Veronese monastery of St. Zeno, ibid., 1100.---Confirms the privileges of the canons of Padua and of their church, ibid., 1102.---For the canons of St. Saviour, ibid., 1103.---Grants Bishop Bernard of Padua the right to mint coinage, ibid., 1107.---Diploma for St. Maximin: through the intervention of Pope Leo IX, he restores to St. Maximin monastery the court of Prichinas and confirms several estates for the brethren’s use, ibid., 1110.---Confirms to Brunwilre monastery a gift made by Richeza, queen of Poland, ibid., 1111, 1113.---Diploma for St. Maximin monastery: against the advocates, he sets limits to their legal authority and privileges, ibid., 1115.---Diploma which exempts the Volterran clergy from the jurisdiction of the counts and confirms to the church of Volterra all its rights and privileges, ibid., 1117.---Likewise for the church of Vercelli, ibid., 1118.---Confirms rights and immunities to the Mantuan *arimanni*, ibid., 1120.---Concerning the canons of the Church of Cremona, ibid., 1121.---Privilege granted to the people of Ferrara, ibid., 1122.---Confirms the privileges and possessions of Prüm monastery, ibid., 1123.---Concerning Stavelot monastery, ibid., 1160.

HENRY IV, Emperor.—Privilege for the Church of Hamburg, CLI, 1139.—For the churches of St. Peter at Minden and Paderborn, and for the monastery of Stavelot, he confirms the privileges of ancient kings, prohibits the oppressions of advocates, and orders that the two monasteries, Stavelot and Malmedy, shall have one abbot only, ibid., 1143.—Privileges for the Church of Osnabrück, ibid., 1144, 1146.—Confirmation of the privileges and rights of the bishop of Passau and his church, ibid., 1149.—Privilege granted to Abbot Peter for the monastery of St. Eugenius in the county of Siena, ibid., 1150.—Diploma by which he confirms and enlarges all rights and privileges of Farfa Abbey, ibid., 1153.—The same for the monastery of St. Zeno at Verona, ibid., 1159, 1162.—Gift [Col. 0087] of the castles of New Campitello and Scorciarolo, made by Emperor Henry IV to Cono, bishop of Mantua, and his church, ibid., 1163.—Confirmatory diploma of all the rights of the Church of Pavia, ibid., 1164.—Decree for the protection of certain property belonging to the monks of St. Justina at Padua, CLI, 1164.

HILDEGARD, Queen.—Gift for the monastery of St. Arnulf, XCVIII, 972.

HONORIUS I, Pope.—Privilege granted to Bobbio Abbey, LXXX, 483.

HONORIUS II, Pope.—He takes the canons of the Church of St. Vincent at Bergamo under his protection, and confirms their possessions and rights, CLXVI, 1217.—Concerning the monastery of Rheinau, ibid., 1219.—Confirmation concerning the abbey and election of an abbot at Saalfeld, according to the institution made by Hanno of Cologne and Siegfried, archbishop of Mainz; incorporation concerning the parish of Neuhofen and Crolup; and that no one shall found or consecrate a church within the territory or jurisdiction of the lord abbot, nor shall dogs be fed or stipends given to hunters, ibid., 1220.—Privileges for the Camaldolese congregation and for Cluny Abbey, ibid., 1223, 1225, 1228, 1229.—He takes the Church of Montefeltro under the protection of the Holy See, ibid., 1252.—Privilege for the collegiate church of Porto; and the ancient privileges of the abbey of St. Walburga are renewed and enlarged, ibid., 1235.—He takes the monastery of St. Paul of Argon under his patronage and confirms its property, ibid., 1237.—He confirms the original foundation of the monastery of St. Martin at Ahuas, ibid.—Concerning the foundation of the cell of St. Mary at Breisach, ibid., 1239.—He confirms the possessions and privileges of the monastery of St. Ulrich at Neresheim, ibid., 1240.—Concerning Savigny Abbey, ibid., 1241.—Concerning the Church of York, ibid., 1242.—Concerning the Church of Ravenna, ibid., 1243.—Concerning the Church of Lincoln, ibid., 1245.—Privilege confirming the possessions and property of the monastery of St. Thierry at Reims, ibid., 1247.—He confirms the discipline and possessions of the brethren of St. Mary of Prémontré, ibid., 1249.—Confirmation of the foundation of the church at Cappenberg, ibid., 1251.—Privileges for the Church of St. Mary at Piacenza, ibid., 1253.—He receives the monastery of St. Blaise into apostolic protection and confirms its free advocacy, ibid., 1254.—Concerning the monastery of Wiblingen, ibid., 1257.—He restores to Roger, archbishop of Pisa, the right of consecrating Corsican bishops and grants him the pallium, ibid., 1261.—He secures Cluny Abbey to Abbot Peter, ibid., 1265.—Privilege for the nunnery of Fontevraud, ibid., 1268.—He confirms the discipline, possessions, and privileges of the monastery of Sts. Ulrich and Afra at Kreuzlingen, ibid., 1270.—Privilege for the abbey of St. Peter at Chartres concerning several churches confirmed by him, ibid., 1273.

Bull, or diploma, by which the foundation of Sponheim Abbey is confirmed, CLXVI, 1274.—Concerning the property of the canons of Faenza, ibid., 1277.—He confirms the privileges and possessions of the Church of Trier, and grants Archbishop Mainer the use of the pallium and the processional cross; and, at the appointed stations of the church, permission to ride with a white *naccus* [uncertain term], ibid., 1278.—He informs the people of Tyre that he has bestowed the pallium upon William, elected archbishop of Tyre and consecrated by the patriarch of Jerusalem, ibid., 1280.—Privilege for the Church of the Holy Sepulchre at Jerusalem, ibid., 1281.—He takes Flèreffe Abbey under the protection of the Apostolic See and confirms its possessions, ibid., 1284.—To Louis VI, king of the Franks: he receives Henry, the king’s son and a cleric, under his protection, ibid., 1286.—Bull confirming the church and property of Steinfeld, ibid., 1288.—He receives under the protection of the Apostolic See the hospital-house and church of St. Mary in the diocese of Ceneda, ibid., 1289.—He confirms the regular canons established in the monastery of Agaune, ibid., 1292.—Privilege for the Church of St. Peter at Bologna, ibid., 1293.—Bull for Vendôme Abbey, ibid., 1294.—He receives the monastery of St. Mary of Curatio under protection; and to those who visit the monastery on certain days he remits one hundred and fifty years of imposed penances, ibid., 1298.—Privileges for the monastery of St. Mary at Amelungsborn and for the Church of St. Martin at Tours, ibid., 1301.—He commends to Alfonso, king of the Spains, his legate Hubert, cardinal-priest, ibid., 1302.—He takes the monastery of St. Peter in the Black Forest under protection and confirms its privileges, ibid., 1304.—Concerning the church of Hadmersleben, ibid., 1305.—Privilege for the Church of Meaux, ibid., 1306.—For the monastery of St. George at Prüfening, and for the Church of St. Margaret at Bamberg, ibid., 1307, 1308.—Confirmation of the foundation of the church at Denkendorf, ibid., 1309.—He confirms an ancient law of the late Emperor Henry that clerics should not be required to take an oath, ibid., 1311.—Confirmation [Col. 0088] of the foundation of the collegiate church of Beuron; likewise, grant of abbatial blessing and investiture with the pastoral staff, ibid., 1312.—He confirms the liberty of Altach Abbey, ibid., 1314.

INNOCENT II, Pope.—Diplomas for Cluny Abbey, CLXXXIX, 1062, 1064, 1065.

HORMISDAS, Pope.—He appoints Sallustius vicar of the Apostolic See throughout the provinces of Baetica and Lusitania, LXIII, 425.—He commends Emperor Justin’s concern for achieving peace and urges perseverance in what has been begun, ibid., 428.—He praises Justin’s zeal for ecclesiastical peace, ibid., 465.—He delegates to Epiphanius, bishop of Constantinople, the vicariate authority of the Apostolic See in receiving back the lapsed, ibid., 515.

HUGH, Saint, bishop of Lincoln.—Charter reciting and confirming donors’ grants, CLIII, 1113.—Charter reciting and confirming donors’ grants to the monastery of St. Oswald of Bardney, ibid., 1118.—Charter confirming gifts for the Church of St. Andrew at Northampton, ibid., 1120.—Confirmation concerning the church of Walden, ibid., 1122.—Confirmation of the churches of Thorneberg and Dodeford for the monks of Luffield Abbey, ibid.—Charter confirming Ralph of Aby’s donation for the construction of an abbey at Granefeid, ibid., 1122.

HUGH, Archbishop of Lyons.—Letter concerning the church of St. Faith of Castellet, given to Conques Abbey, CLVII, 509.—Letter to Hugh, archbishop of Besançon, for the monks of St. Benignus at Dijon, ibid., 516.—Charter of the absolution of Fulk, count of Anjou, ibid., 517.—He gives the Church of St. Desiderius at Brescia to Cluny, subject to rents, ibid., 518.—To the abbot of Sens, on behalf of the abbot of St. Peter-the-Living, ibid., 522.—Gift of the church of St. Germanus, ibid., 527.—Charter granting the church of St. John of Bruilloles to Savigny Abbey, ibid.

INNOCENT III, Pope.—Confirmation concerning certain churches granted, with the chapter’s consent, to the provostship of the Church of Kalocsa, CCXIV, 25.—Concerning confirmation of the sentence pronounced by legates of the Roman curia against Markward, ibid., 31.—Concerning the grant and confirmation of the monastery of Abola, belonging to the Roman Church, ibid., 37.—Concerning confirmation of the privilege granted by the bishop of Chartres to the priests of the deanery of Sparton, ibid., 40.—Concerning confirmation of the constitution made between the archpriest and canons of Perugia, ibid., 41.—Concerning confirmation of the primacy of the provinces of Torres, Cagliari, and Arborea, ibid., 49.—Concerning relaxation of the sentence which a legate of the Roman Church had pronounced against the bishop and church of Zamora, ibid., 51.—He confirms Adelmus’s election as bishop of Poitiers, ibid., 65.—He confers a certain prebend in the Church of Antwerp, ibid., 78.—He confirms the foundation and privileges of the Hospital of the Holy Spirit, ibid., 85.—He confirms the treaty between Philip, king of France, and the count of Flanders, ibid., 117.—He confirms and approves the statutes of St. Vedast’s Abbey and that abbey’s ancient and praiseworthy customs, ibid., 122.—He approves the ancient and praiseworthy customs of the convent of Vézelay and grants it new privileges, ibid.—Concerning the immunity and privileges of the monastery of Blessed Mary at Vézelay, ibid., 131, 132.—Confirmation of a certain constitution concerning the revenues of Ivo’s benefice, ibid., 138.—He receives Robert, abbot of St. Germanus at Paris, and his brethren under apostolic protection, confirming their old privileges with many additions, ibid., 151.—He confirms the rights and privileges of St. Denis Abbey, ibid., 154.—He confirms the sentence pronounced by the cardinal of St. Mary in the case of P. and James, cleric of Pavia, ibid., 160.—The convent of St. Germanus at Auxerre is permitted to receive holy chrism and oil, and consecrations, from another Catholic bishop if the bishop of Auxerre refuses to impart them freely, ibid., 103.—Property granted to the monastery of the Holy Trinity at Cervifroid, to be devoted to pious uses, is confirmed by apostolic authority, ibid., 215.—He confirms to the consuls, judges, and people of Benevento their statute concerning the palace of judges and notaries, ibid., 218.—The privileges granted to the bishop of Ultrasilvana by Pope Gregory are confirmed, ibid., 228.—Concerning the confirmation of the order, privileges, and rule of life of St. Osyth of Chuc, ibid., 240.—He confirms for Charo, archbishop of Monreale, and his successors the privileges granted by their predecessors, ibid., 275.—He confirms for Bishop Alfonso and the chapter of Ourense their statute concerning the number of canons, ibid., 293.

Concerning the privilege and exemption of the canons of Borgo San Donnino, that they may not be harassed by the bishop of Parma, CCXIV, 316.—Concerning the privileges and immunity of the church of St. Nicholas, ibid., 317.—He confirms a certain decree of the king of England, ibid., 353.—For Peter, bishop of Oloron, he confirms a statute establishing six prebends, ibid., 354.—For the elect of Uppsala: how the pallium is to be used, ibid.—He receives the noblemen Uguith and Guido, marquises, together with their subjects, under apostolic protection, ibid., 359.—To the nobleman of Spalagran: he is permitted to enter a monastery and the Order of St. Benedict, ibid.—He permits the archbishop of Siponto to convert a collegiate church into a monastery of monks, ibid., 376.—He confirms the privileges and gifts of Sore Abbey, ibid., 399.—He receives the consuls and people of Todi under apostolic protection and confirms their ancient privileges, ibid., 400.—He receives the kingdom of Jerusalem under apostolic protection, ibid., 417.—He receives Sancho, king of Portugal, and his kingdom with all its property under apostolic protection, ibid., 419.—The bishop of Périgueux is granted authority to visit monasteries, establish churches, and correct abuses, ibid., 421.—For the clerics of St. Paul of Castro Cervario, he confirms the sentence pronounced in their favour concerning the right of baptismal font, ibid., 432.—For Richard, abbot, and the chapter of Compiègne: their jurisdiction and privileges are confirmed, ibid., 433.—The establishment of prebends made in the Church of Durham is confirmed, ibid., 427.—He receives the provost of St. John of Cinciterio and his brethren under apostolic protection, ibid., 439.—He receives the monastery of St. Peter at Corbie under his protection, ibid., 450.—By apostolic authority he confirms the purchase of certain property by the brethren of the Knights Templar, ibid., 467.—He confirms the agreement formerly concluded between the commander and brethren of a house of the Knights Templar and the provost and chapter of Maguelonne, ibid., 467.—He grants Fulk, abbot of Corbie, the use of a ring, ibid., 478.—For the canons of St. Lawrence at Spello, he confirms the cardinal’s sentence concerning the priory of St. Lawrence, ibid., 499.—He confirms the privileges and property of the monastery of Francheval, ibid., 501.—Concerning Boscodon Abbey, ibid., 504.—He receives the monks and house of the Holy Trinity at Cervifroid under apostolic protection, ibid.—He entrusts to the archbishop of Palermo the care and restoration of the monastery at Palermo, ibid., 521.—The bishop of Passau is granted authority to absolve arsonists, ibid., 526.—For the chapter of Saintes, the constitution concerning the number of forty canons is confirmed, ibid., 545.

Concerning confirmation of privileges granted to Donatus, bishop of Alès, and his successors, CCXIV, 548.—For the abbey of St. Mary of Casanova, ibid., 550.—For Dereford Abbey, ibid., 564.—For the Church of Cork, ibid., 565.—For the abbey of St. Bertin, ibid., 577.

Baldwin, count of Flanders, and his wife Mary are received under apostolic protection, CCXIV, 585.—He receives Calatrava Abbey under his apostolic protection, ibid., 590.—The statutes made by the bishop of Oxford in his church are confirmed, ibid., 604.—The dean of Toledo is received under the protection of Blessed Peter and the Apostolic See, ibid., 606.—The monastery of St. Michael is received under the protection of the Apostolic See, ibid., 607.—Privileges are confirmed for the monastery of St. Peter of the Isle, ibid., 610.—For the Church of Sées, ibid., 615.—For the abbey of St. Peter at Gubbio, ibid., 618.

The privileges of the Church of Marseilles are confirmed, CCXIV, 640.—Concerning the monastery of the Holy Cross, ibid., 645.—Concerning the monastery of St. Mary of Canneto, ibid., 650.—Concerning the Church of Blessed Mary of the Rock, ibid., 651.—Concerning the monastery of Sts. Sergius and Bacchus, ibid.—Concerning the monastery of St. Mary of Aquileia, ibid., 664.—Concerning the monastery of the Holy Cross of Waltham, ibid., 665.—The privileges of the archbishop of Wells are confirmed, ibid., 672.—Concerning Waltham Abbey, ibid., 674, 675.—He confirms tithes given by the king of Braga to the church, ibid., 691.—The privileges of the clerics of St. Chrysogonus are confirmed, ibid., 706.—He confirms to Andrew, archdeacon of Acheruntia, the archdeaconry with every right, ibid., 711.—He receives the count of Lecce under apostolic protection, ibid., 712.—He confirms the privileges of the abbey of St. Mary of Ferraria, ibid., 837.—For Theobald, bishop of Amiens, he confirms a certain statute and ordinance, ibid., 847.—He confirms the ancient privileges of the abbey of St. Peter at Gubbio, ibid., 852.—William of Bieria, priest, is received under apostolic protection, ibid., 858.—The privileges of Mariadura Abbey are confirmed, ibid., 859.—He receives William, lord of Montpellier, under the protection of the Apostolic See, ibid., 861.—For the prior and chapter of Sigüenza: concerning confirmation of certain revenues, ibid., 943.—The privileges of the Church of St. Mary of Chirberi are confirmed, ibid., 944.—He receives Aymon, lord of Cicala, under his protection, ibid., 945.—The privileges of Grandmont Abbey are confirmed, ibid.—To the archbishop of Sens: concerning the absolution of the bishop of Nevers, ibid., 261.—The election of the archbishop of Mainz is confirmed, ibid., 964, 969.—To the bishop of Chalon and the abbot of Cîteaux: concerning absolution of the abbot of St. Seine from his vow to cross the sea [Col. 0090] to the Holy Land, ibid., 970.—The legation to the East is confirmed for the cardinal-priest of the title of St. Praxedes, ibid., 980.—For the abbot and convent of Dol, the agreement made with the lord of Château-Raoul is confirmed, ibid., 1048.—For the bishop of Viterbo: confirmation of the endowment of the Church of St. Mary of Polenzano from the castle of Bagnaia, made to it by the consuls of Viterbo, ibid., 1087.—He receives the monastery of Sts. Peter and Paul and St. Augustine under the protection of Blessed Peter and confirms its property and privileges, ibid., 1101.—Concerning the chapter of Amalfi, ibid., 1104.—The privileges of Jort Abbey are confirmed, ibid., 1135.—The privileges of the monastery of Sts. Peter and Paul at Canterbury are confirmed, ibid., 1185.

He grants to the monastery by the cave of Blessed Benedict six pounds of coin from the annual rent of the castle of Porciano, CCXV, 9.—He receives the monastery of St. Lupus at Troyes under the protection of Blessed Peter and confirms its rights and privileges, ibid., 11.—He approves the agreement concluded between the bishop of Ourense and the archbishop of Compostela, ibid.—He receives the Church of Ourense under the protection of the Apostolic See and confirms its rights and privileges, ibid., 18.—Concerning the Church of Pisa, ibid., 24.—Concerning the monastery of St. Mary at Faenza, ibid., 25.—By apostolic authority he confirms the sentence pronounced by J., master of the schools of Orléans, delegated for this purpose by the pope, in the case concerning the election of the prior of Graciac, ibid., 34.—He receives the landgrave of Thuringia under apostolic protection, ibid., 46.—He confirms the church of St. Albinus to Le Bec Abbey, ibid.—He establishes the cathedral church of Acheruntia at Matera and joins it to the Church of Acheruntia, ibid., 57.—He confirms for the archbishop of Ragusa benefices in the bishopric of Carlisle, ibid., 58.—He receives the Church of Huesca under the protection of Blessed Peter and enumerates and confirms the property belonging to it, ibid., 78.—He confirms the election of the archdeacon of Merseburg as bishop, ibid., 90.

He confirms certain privileges for the hospitals of the Holy Spirit at Magabonne, ibid., 113.—He receives the house of the Holy Trinity at Cervifroid under his protection, ibid., 134.—He receives under protection Master Gualfred, cleric of St. Maurice of Tarbudiato, ibid., 140.—He confers temporal jurisdiction in Villa Magna upon the monastery of Villamagna, ibid.—He commends the Church of Tyre to the king of Jerusalem, ibid., 148.—He confirms tithes to the Church of Tyre, ibid., 149.—He confirms the possessions and privileges of the monastery of Flora, ibid., 151.—He confirms the union made between Caraceto Abbey and the Cistercian Order, ibid., 189.—He receives the Cistercians under his protection and enumerates their property, ibid.—He receives the monastery of St. Columba of Hay under the protection of the Apostolic See, and its possessions are enumerated, ibid., 193.—He confirms to the bishop of Palestrina the scholastership of the Church of Mainz, ibid., 205.—He confirms the privileges of Corbie Abbey, ibid.—He grants the abbot of Corbie Abbey the faculty of using a ring, ibid.—He confirms the archdeacon of Vicenza, ibid., 225.—He receives the Church of the Holy Cross at Coimbra under the protection of Blessed Peter, and its property is enumerated, ibid., 232.—He receives Clorets Abbey under his protection, ibid., 240.—By apostolic authority he confirms to Michael, subdeacon of the church of Castris, possession of a benefice, ibid., 258.

Privilege by which Leo, legate of the Apostolic See, is granted authority to anoint Kaloyan, king of the Bulgarians, as king, CCXV, 277.—He establishes the archbishop of Trnovo as primate of all Bulgaria and Vlachia, and sends him such a privilege, ibid., 280.—He sends the pallium to Anastasius, archbishop of Belesbud, ibid., 292.—For the archbishop of Trnovo, ibid., 294.—He receives the prior and brethren of the Hospital of Thuregan under his protection, ibid., 300.—For the prioress and nuns of Ruesperra, ibid., 302.—By apostolic authority he confirms the transfer of the episcopal see of Luni to Sarzana, ibid., 306.

He receives the Church of the Holy Cross of Stampis under his protection, CCXV, 312.—Concerning the Church of St. Stephen at Fano, ibid., 315.—Concerning the Church of Rimini, ibid., 321.—By apostolic authority he confirms for Thomas de Disce, canon of Wells, the prebend conferred upon him by the archbishop of York, ibid., 332.—By apostolic authority he confirms the privileges granted to the king of Bohemia by emperors and recently confirmed by Otto, ibid., 339.—He receives the master and brethren of the Hospital of Bekekeq under his protection, ibid., 314.—By apostolic authority he confirms for the chapter of St. Cecilia the sentence rendered in their favour in a certain case against the Church of St. Lawrence at Pozzuoli, ibid., 353.—He receives Peter of Paris, chaplain at the bridge of Lincoln, under the protection of Blessed Peter, ibid., 362.—He receives the monastery of St. Andrew of the Rock under protection, and its possessions are enumerated, ibid., [Col. 0091] 368.—To the chapter of Vicenza: by apostolic authority he confirms the provostship of Vicenza to his subdeacon Nicholas, ibid., 382.—He receives the Church of Furcone under his protection and confirms its possessions and privileges, CCXV, 396.—He receives Charles, canon of Aquileia, under his protection, ibid., 431.

He receives the Church of Lethglenn under his protection, CCXV, 432.—Concerning the convent of the Hospital of Rivicenaria, ibid., 435.—Concerning the monastery of St. Mary of Botrano, ibid., 439.—Concerning Montmajour Abbey, ibid., 466.—Concerning the Church of Feltre, ibid., 504.

He grants Richard, abbot of Compiègne, the use of mitre and ring, ibid., 504.—He receives the brethren of the Hospital of St. James of Colle Bertanni under his protection, ibid., 509.—He confirms the patriarch of Constantinople, ibid., 512.—He grants the abbot of Cluny authority to correct what needs correction in abbeys belonging to Cluny Abbey, according to God and the Rule of Blessed Benedict, ibid., 526.—He receives the prior and brethren of Val-des-Choux under the protection of Blessed Peter, ibid., 531.—He confirms the possessions and privileges of the monastery of St. Mary of Charity, ibid., 537.—He receives Winchester Abbey under his protection, ibid., 561.—He grants Thomas, patriarch of Constantinople, authority to absolve from censures incurred through striking a cleric, and to anoint the emperor of Constantinople, ibid., 576.—He receives the monastery of St. Peter at Chalon under his protection, etc., ibid., 590.—He renews and confirms the ancient privileges for the abbess and nuns of Gandersheim, ibid., 598.—He receives the lord of Guirchia under the protection of Blessed Peter, ibid., 616.—He receives under protection the church founded by Alferada, ibid.—The archbishop of Sens is permitted to visit the province of Sens and correct abuses, ibid., 618.—He receives the hospital-house of St. Rainerius into his jurisdiction and protection, ibid., 629.—The archbishop of Reims has his privileges confirmed, among which is particularly noted that he alone may anoint and crown the king of the Franks, ibid., 640.

He receives the hospital-house of the Holy Trinity of Vernolio under his protection, CCXV, 662.—Concerning the monastery of St. Julian of Perario, ibid., 668.—Concerning the Church of Agen, ibid., 684.—He permits the archbishop of Bourges to absolve his servants and the clerics of his church from violent laying on of hands, ibid., 726.—He grants the archdeacon of Vienne, elected bishop of Viviers, authority to retain other ecclesiastical benefices besides the archdeaconry of Vienne, ibid., 727.—A certain agreement between C., cardinal-priest, and the clerics of St. Lawrence in Lucina is confirmed, ibid., 739.—He receives Vendôme Abbey under his protection, and its possessions are enumerated, ibid., 747.—The patriarch of Jerusalem is permitted to use the pallium in any province, ibid., 752.—He grants immunities and privileges to the Church of Fermo, ibid., 767.—He confirms certain institutions of the archbishop of Lund, ibid., 774.—He confirms the ancient privileges and grants of the Church of Nidaros, ibid., 798.—An ancient privilege is renewed for Pultari Abbey, ibid., 850.—Certain property given to the Cistercian convent of Cupro is confirmed, ibid., 870.—He confirms certain property to the Church of Stendal, ibid., 882.—He receives the monastery of St. Rufus under his protection, ibid., 885.—Concerning the Church of St. Mary of Monte de Gardia, ibid., 898.—Concerning the monastery of St. Andrew, ibid., 901.—The privileges and statutes of the Church of Pavia are confirmed, ibid., 905.—That the kings of Aragon may be crowned by the archbishop of Tarragona, ibid., 915.—He receives the monastery of Sts. Innocents and Anastasius at Gandersheim under the protection of the Apostolic See, ibid., 919.—He receives the hospital-house of Neufchâtel at Driencourt under his protection, ibid., 944.—All the property of the leprous brethren of Vailiac is confirmed, ibid., 1019.—The gift of Satalia made to the Knights Templar by the Venetians is confirmed, ibid., 1019.—The bishop of Samaria has confirmed for him the grant concerning Mount Holy, ibid., 1030.—He receives the clerics of the island of Negroponte under his protection, ibid.—The sentence pronounced for the convent of Fossanova concerning certain possessions against Saracenus is confirmed, ibid., 1053.—He receives the duke of Cracow under his protection, ibid., 1067.—The possessions and property of the Church of Lucca are confirmed, ibid., 1068.—He receives Kening Abbey under the protection of Blessed Peter, ibid., 1073.—He receives the Church of Methoni under his protection, ibid., 1079.—He confirms the election made for the archbishop of Magdeburg, ibid., 1093.—He receives the duke of Saxony under the protection of the Apostolic See, ibid., 1106.—He receives Radingia Abbey of the Cluniac Order under his protection and confirms its privileges and rights, ibid., 1115.—The Church of Blessed Lawrence at Jovisvilla is received [Col. 0092] under the protection of the Apostolic See, with all its property, liberties, immunities, and privileges, ibid., 1122.—Concerning Radingia Abbey, ibid., 1123.—Privileges are granted to the nuns’ monastery of Seesen, and its liberties and immunities are confirmed, ibid., 1155.

Several similar items still remain in volume CCXV, and in volumes CCXVI and CCXVII; enough has now been said concerning this pope.

IRMINA, Abbess.—Charter by which she grants to Willibrord, bishop of Utrecht, whatever she possesses in the village of Stancheim, CXXXIX, 537.

JOHN IV, Pope.—Concerning the celebration of a purely Catholic Easter and the need diligently to guard against the reviving Pelagian heresy, LXXX, 601.—That monks may appoint priests for their own churches, ibid., 608.

JOHN VIII, Pope.—He asserts certain estates for the Church of Ravenna, CXXVI, 653.—The privileges of the Roman Church are extinguished only by prescription of one hundred years, ibid., 654.—He again declares Fulda Abbey, together with all its cells, churches, tithes, estates, and other appurtenances, exempt and free, ibid., 657.—He confirms for the monks of St. Vedast at Arras all contained in the diploma of Emperor Charles, ibid., 658.—Privilege for Ansegisus, archbishop of Sens, granting him his vicarial authority in Gaul and Germany, ibid., 660.—He confirms the division of the monks of St. Medard at Soissons, ibid., 660.—The Church of Orense in Galicia is made metropolitan, ibid., 663.—By pontifical authority he ratifies every royal and episcopal privilege of the monks of Tournus, adding exemption from the jurisdiction of every bishop whatsoever, ibid., 686.—He approves the gift made to them of the monastery of St. Pourçain, ibid., 687.—He commends Wigbod, bishop of Parma, to Emperor Charles the Bald, ibid., 699.—He sends Emperor Charles the Bald a palm branch, etc., 714.—Privilege granted to the monastery and hospice of Piacenza, 737.—He grants the bishop of Pavia the use of archiepiscopal insignia, together with authority to summon the archbishops of Ravenna and Milan to a synod, ibid., 739.—He grants the pallium to Theotmar, archbishop of Juvavum, etc., ibid., 745.—He confirms the privileges of the Church of Bered in England, ibid.—He confirms property formerly granted to Tournus Abbey, ibid., 772.—Letter to Rostagnus, archbishop of Arles, granting him his vicarial authority and use of the pallium, 775, 777.

Privilege for the monastery of St. Giles, CXXVI, 792.—For the Church of Poitiers, that none may invade its property, etc., ibid., 796.—Granted for Fleury Abbey at the synod of Troyes, ibid., 797.

He grants Wala, bishop of Metz, a pallium to be worn on specified days, CXXVI, 798.—He confirms the privileges granted to the Church of Tours, ibid., 800.—Privilege for Vézelay Abbey, confirming immunities formerly granted to it, ibid., 803.—For the monastery of St. Marcellus, ibid., 805.—For Piacenza Abbey, ibid., 821.

He urges King Carloman to have Conspectus created bishop in the Church of Vercelli, CXXVI, 840.—To Branimir: he receives him as returning to the bosom of the Roman Church and grants him the apostolic blessing he had requested, ibid., 841.—He confirms the ordination of Joseph, bishop of Asti, who had previously been made bishop of the Church of Vercelli contrary to the canons, ibid., 920.—To the clergy of Milan: he receives Haderic under the protection of the Apostolic See and excommunicates all who have caused trouble to him or his churches, ibid., 926.—He entrusts the visitation and care of the Church of Faenza, deprived of a pastor, to John, bishop of Forlì, until a new pastor is appointed over it, ibid., 934.—Constitution concerning the right of cardinals, ibid., 942.—Privilege for Monte Cassino Abbey, ibid., 950.—An exhortation that King Charles should keep King Carloman firm in love for the Roman Church, ibid., 958.—Letter to the clergy and people of Autun: he grants them the privilege of setting over themselves one of their own whom clergy and people have proclaimed, notwithstanding the contrary choice of kings or princes, ibid., 964.

JOHN X, Pope.—Privilege granted to Abbot Haico, confirming the privileges of the monastery of the Saviour at Fulda, CXXXII, 800.—He confirms the possessions and privileges of the Church of Autun, ibid., 801.—He grants anew to Solomon, bishop of Constance and abbot of St. Gall, the privilege of immunity and free election formerly given to that monastery by emperors and kings, ibid., 803.—Privilege granted to Paul, bishop of Adria, ibid., 804.—Privilege granted to Honesty, archbishop of Ravenna, ibid., 805.—He confirms possessions given by William, count of Auvergne, to the monks of St. Laumer, who had been driven out by pagans, ibid., 809.—He confirms the possessions of the Church of Narbonne, 811.—He commends Cluny Abbey and orders restoration to it of the property of Gigny Abbey given by Abbot Berno, which Abbot Wido had taken away, ibid., 812.—He sends the pallium to Wenni, archbishop of Hamburg, and confirms the Hamburg privileges, ibid., 813.

JOHN XI, Pope.—He confirms Saint Odo as abbot in the government of Cluny Abbey, as well as that monastery’s exemption from every lordship. He establishes that the election of an abbot after Odo’s death shall be free and made without consultation with anyone. He also confirms the Roman monastery granted to Cluny by Rudolf, king of Burgundy. Moreover, he gives authority to receive monasteries offered for reform; restores tithes of Cluniac chapels taken away by bishops; and likewise confirms its own coinage, as Rudolf, king of the Franks, had granted. He permits brethren who wish to improve their manner of life to move temporarily from other monasteries to Cluny. Further, he determines that Cluny Abbey belongs to the Holy Apostolic See for protection and support, and orders that, as a token of that protection, ten solidi be paid at Rome every five years, CXXXII, 1055.—He confirms Cluny Abbey with all the things and possessions which it has and shall acquire in future; and, among other matters, orders that the monastery called Carus Locus, in the district of Mâcon, shall remain subject to Cluny Abbey, ibid., 1058.—Privilege for Vézelay Abbey, ibid., 1059.—He secures to the Church of Autun the right freely to elect its bishop, 1061.—Privilege for the monastery of St. Mary and St. Martin at Poitiers, ibid., 1062.

JOHN XII, Pope.—He confirms the privileges and possessions of the monasteries of St. Mary at Humolaria and St. Vitonus, CXXXIII, 1015–1018.—He grants use of the pallium to Henry, archbishop of Trier, ibid., 1019, 1029.—He confirms the possessions and rights of the monasteries of Subiaco, St. Saviour at Fulda, Sts. Stephen, Dionysius, Silvester, St. Peter at Bivora, Volturno, etc., ibid., 1020–1042.

JOHN XIII, pope.—Confirms the immunity of the canons of Bologna, CXXXV, 951.—Bull for the establishment of the archbishopric of Magdeburg, ibid.—Privilege for the Church of Ferrara, ibid., 956.—Takes the nunnery of Gandersheim under his protection and confirms its possessions and rights, ibid., 959.—Bull for the monasteries of St. Maximinus of Trier and of St. John the Evangelist of Meissen, ibid., 960, 961.—Privilege for the monastery of Dol, ibid., 965.—Bull by which he grants Adalbert, archbishop of Magdeburg, primacy among all the prelates of Germany, and establishes him in honor equal to the chief primates of Gaul, ibid., 966.—Bull to the same, granting to him and his successors the consecration of all bishops between the Elbe and the Saale, together with the right to the pallium, ibid., 967.—Privilege for the monastery of St. Michael of Coxano, ibid., 969.—Bull for the convent of Quedlinburg, ibid., 972.—Privilege for the Church of Trier, ibid., 974.—Grants Archbishop Theoderic of Trier the use of the pallium, ibid., 976.—Privilege for the monastery of Fulda, ibid., 979.—Privilege for the monastery of St. Vincent at Metz, ibid., 980.—Raises the Church of Ausona to archiepiscopal rank, ibid., 983.—States that he has united the Church of Tarragona to that of Ausona, consecrated Atto as archbishop, and bestowed the pallium upon him, ibid., 984.—Privilege for the monastery of St. Mary of Tangmarsfeld, ibid., 986.—Privilege for the monastery of Cluny, ibid., 990.—Confirms the decree of Adalbero, who had installed monks in the abbey of Mouzon in place of canons, ibid., 991.—Privilege of the monastery of St. Remigius, ibid., 992.—Privilege for the monastery of St. Saviour at Pavia, ibid., 993.—Places under protection, but not under the jurisdiction, of the bishop of Pavia the monastery of St. Saviour at Pavia, founded and endowed by the Empress Adelaide, ibid., 995.—Privileges for the Church of Arles, ibid., 998.

JOHN XV, pope.—Confirms all possessions of the monastery of Golden Heaven at Pavia, and grants Abbot Peter the use of the dalmatic, sandals, stockings, and gloves, and the right to carry a little bell in the chapel while travelling, etc., CXXXVII, 827.—Receives under apostolic protection and endows with various privileges the Church of Noyon and the monasteries of St. Gregory, Corbie, St. Nazarius of Lorsch, and Amiens, ibid., 828–835.—Concerning the Church of Hamburg and the monasteries of St. Peter of Roda and Brewnow, ibid., 839–847.—Bestows the pallium on Grimoald, archbishop of Salerno, and establishes him as metropolitan of the bishoprics of Paestum, Acerenza, Nola, etc., ibid., 848.—Receives the monastery of Fulda under the protection of the Apostolic See [Col. 0094] and frees it from the jurisdiction of any church whatsoever, ibid., 849.

JOHN XVIII, pope.—Confirms the privileges and possessions of the monastery of St. Florentius at Saumur, CXXXIX, 1471.—Privilege for the Church of St. Mary at Iserg, ibid., 1485.—Grants privileges to the Church of SS. Cosmas and Damian at the Golden Mica, ibid., 1481.—Privilege for the Church of Paderborn, ibid., 1482.—Confirms a gift made by Bishop Renaud to the canons of Paris, ibid., 1483.—Privilege for the monastery of St. Benignus at Dijon, ibid., 1485.—Confirms the possessions of the canons of the Church of Pisa, ibid., 1486.—Diploma confirming the bishopric of Bamberg, ibid., 1487.—Confirmation of the privileges and metropolitan right of the Holy Church of Toulouse, ibid., 1489.—Confirms the privileges of the monastery of Belleloc, etc., ibid., 1491.—Concerning the monastery of St. Victor at Marseilles, ibid., 1492.

JOHN XIX, pope.—Privilege for the Church of Porto, CXLI, 1115.—Grants the pallium to Archbishop Canusinus of Besançon and confirms his rights, ibid., 1123.—Confirms the possessions of the Church of Silva Candida, ibid., 1125.—Invests Peter, bishop of Silva Candida, upon receipt of the staff, with the entire territory of all the churches of Galeria, ibid., 1132.—Declares that he confirms all monasteries and places belonging to the monastery of Cluny and granted to it by Christian faithful, kings, etc. He further forbids any bishop or priest to come to Cluny, for the consecration of a church, the ordination of priests or deacons, or the celebration of Masses, unless invited by the abbot of Cluny; but the monks of Cluny may receive whatever grade of ordination they wish, wherever it pleases their abbot, etc., ibid., 1135.—Confirms the property and rights of the Church of Tivoli, ibid., 1139.—Grants Bishop Peter of Girona the privilege of using the pallium, ibid., 1143.—Letter to Robert, king of the Franks, concerning the immunity of the monastery of Cluny, ibid., 1145, 1146.—Confirms the privileges of the monastery of Fulda, ibid., 1147.

JOSLENUS, bishop of Soissons.—Charter for the monastery of La Sauve-Majeure, CLXXXVI, 1495.

JUSTINIAN, emperor.—Letter to Pope John V confirming the Sixth Synod of Constantinople, XCVI, 425.

JUSTIN, emperor.—Informs Pope Hormisdas that he has been elected emperor, LXIII, 426.—At the request of the Council of Constantinople, asks Pope Hormisdas to deign to send legates to Constantinople to bring peace to the Eastern Church and receive back those who had fallen away, ibid., 427.—For the peace and unity of the Eastern Church, asks Hormisdas, if he is unwilling himself to go to Constantinople, to send legates, ibid., 430.

JORDAN, bishop of Limoges.—Diploma granting many things to the chapter of Limoges, CXLII, 1351.—Diploma concerning peace concluded with William, count of Poitou, ibid., 1351.

CANUTE, king.—Confirms the agreement concerning fishing in the Clona, made by Chancellor Andrew and others between the canons of the Paraclete and the royal settlers, CCIX, 754.

LEO III (Saint), pope.—Concerning the privilege of the chapel at Eresburg, CII, 1028.—Sends the pallium to Athelard, archbishop of Canterbury, and recognizes his primacy over all England, ibid., 1032.—Grants a privilege to the Benedictine nunnery of Horre near Trier, ibid., 1067.—Confirms the transfer of the episcopal see of Regensburg from the monastery of St. Emmeram to the Church of St. Stephen, and promulgates the latter’s complete exemption, ibid., 1069.—Privilege for the monastery of St. Benedict at Kupersam, ibid., 1070.

LEO III, pope.—Privilege for the monastery of Saint-Denis, CXXIX, 967.—Diploma for the Church of St. Martin at Tours, ibid., 971.

LEO IV, pope.—Judgment for the bishop of Siena against the bishop of Arezzo, in a dispute concerning various churches or parishes, CXV, 658.—Confirms the privileges of a certain church, ibid., 665.

LEO VII, pope.—Confirms the privileges of St. Saviour’s monastery of Fulda, CXXXII, 1065.—Confirms the property and privileges of the monastery of Subiaco, devastated by the Saracens, ibid., 1067.—Secures for St. Odo, abbot of Cluny, and his successors possession of the estate of Escutiola, ibid., 1068.—Concerning the estate of Savinias, ibid., 1069.—Sends the pallium to Gerard, archbishop of Lorch, ibid., 1071.—At the request of Abbot Odo, confirms that the abbey of Cluny, with all things pertaining to it, is free from every lordship of any person; and forbids its ever to be entrusted to anyone, whether canon, layman, or even monk-abbot unless he lives according to the rule. He also secures freedom in the election of the abbot himself, ibid., 1074.—Confirms the discipline of the monastery of St. Benedict at Fleury, restored by Abbot Odo and Hugh, king of the Franks, together with its possessions and privileges, ibid., 1075.—Commends the monastery of St. Mary and St. Peter of Ripoll to certain bishops, CXXXIII, 1080.—Sends the pallium to Adaldag, bishop of Hamburg, ibid., 1083.

LEO VIII, antipope.—Privilege concerning investitures, CXXXIV, 991.—Privilege for the monastery of Montmajour, ibid., 994.—Cession of the donations of the Roman Church, ibid., 996.

LEO, bishop of Toul, soon Pope LEO IX.—Confirms the possessions of the abbey of St. Aper, CXLIII, 583.—Consecrates the oratory of the estate of Bertiniacum, ibid., 585.—Confirms the foundation of the priory of Dagulin, ibid., 587.

LEO IX, pope.—Confirms the property, rights, and privileges of the monastery of Farfa, CXLIII, 591.—Concerning the monastery of St. Saviour of Septimianum, ibid., 597.—Concerning the Church of Porto, ibid., 598.—Concerning the Church of Verona, ibid., 606.—Concerning the monastery of Fulda, ibid., 609.—Concerning the nunnery of St. Mary in Porto, ibid., 614.—Concerning the abbey of St. Denis, ibid., 620.—Concerning the monastery of Lorsch, ibid., 624.—Concerning the monastery of St. Mary at Verdun, ibid., 630.—Concerning the monastery of St. Mary in Gradibus, in the diocese of Arezzo, ibid., 649.—Concerning the monastery of St. Saviour on Mount Amiata, ibid., 650.—Concerning the monastery of St. Mansuetus, ibid., 654.—Concerning the monastery of SS. Bertarius and Atalenus, ibid., 661.—Concerning the Church of SS. Martin and Agericus, ibid., 667.—Concerning the Church of Besançon, ibid., 668.—Concerning the monastery of St. Maximinus at Trier, ibid., 669.—Concerning the Church of Lucca, ibid., 671.—Concerning the Church of Toul, ibid., 672.—Concerning the Church of the Holy Trinity at Pescara, ibid., 674.—Concerning the Church of Salerno, ibid., 676.—Concerning the monastery of St. Mary on Gorgona, ibid., 677.—Concerning the monastery of Subiaco, ibid., 678.—Concerning the abbey of Farfa, ibid.—Concerning the monastery of St. Peter at Perugia, ibid., 681.—Concerning the monastery of St. Mary of Pomposa, ibid., 683.—Concerning the monastery of Casa Dei, ibid., 686.—Concerning the abbey of Altorf, ibid., 689.—Concerning the monastery of Monte Cassino, ibid., 690.—Concerning the monastery of Holy Wisdom at Benevento, ibid., 692.—Concerning the Church of Ascoli, ibid., 693.—Concerning the Church of Bamberg, ibid., 697.—Concerning the Church of Olivolo, ibid., 704.—Concerning the nunnery of St. Lawrence in Alsace, ibid., 740.

Privileges: for the Church of Trier, CXLIII, 594; for Abbot Richer, 604; for the monastery of St. Remigius Corbinianus, 619; for the canons of the Church of Verdun, 628; for the monastery of Vézelay, 642; for the Church of Carro, 648; for St. Hugh concerning the Church of Raningis, 658; for the canons of Agaune, 665.

Bull for St. Deodatus in the Vosges, CXLIII, 632; for the abbey of Elet, 639; concerning the consecration of the Church of Hohenburg, 663; confirming the privileges and rights of the abbey of Farfa, 678; granting the pallium to Stephen, bishop of Le Puy, 681; and for the Church of St. Arnulf, 781.

Secures for Eberhard, archbishop of Trier, the cell of the Four Crowned Martyrs, CXLIII, 597.—Subjects the monastery of Holy Cross in Rome to Richer, abbot of Monte Cassino, and his successors, ibid., 605.—Confirms the privileges of the monastery of Cluny, ibid., 607.—Confirms to Cedulf, treasurer of the Church of Stavelot, all possessions granted as the endowment of the altar, etc., ibid., 618.—Confirms the foundation and advocacy of the monastery of Holy Cross at Werden, ibid., 637.—Approves the privileges granted by his predecessors to the monastery of Corbie, ibid., 641.—Commends the Roman monastery to Henry, emperor of the Romans and king of Burgundy, etc., ibid., 653.—Releases Edward, king of the English, from his vow to go to Rome because of the disturbed state of the kingdom; and directs him to distribute among the poor the money allocated for the journey and expend it upon founding a new monastery of Blessed Peter or restoring an old one, ibid., 674.—Grants Stephen, bishop of Le Puy, and his successors the use of the pallium, on condition that they be ordained by the Roman pontiff, ibid., 681.—Confirms the privileges of the metropolitan Church of Cologne; grants Archbishop Hermann and his successors the title of chancellor of the Holy Roman Church and cardinal of St. John at the Latin Gate, etc., ibid., 687.—Grants Archbishop Liuthbald of Mainz the use of the pallium, ibid., 694.—Sends Bishop Hartwig of Bamberg the pallium, to be used three times a year, ibid., 700.—Confirms the privileges of the Church of Hamburg and grants Archbishop Adalbert the use of the pallium and mitre, ibid., 701.—Grants a ship for the use of the monastery of Monte Cassino, with its master and crew, free and exempt from every toll and payment, ibid., 731.—Confirms Dominic, formerly a monk, as bishop of Valva, having himself made him bishop, ibid., 734.—Grants to the Vatican basilica of St. Peter a tenth part of the offerings, ibid., 736.—Confirms the foundation [Col. 0096] of the abbey of St. John the Baptist at Florence, ibid., 742.—Concerning the abbey of St. Mary near Saintes, ibid., 743.

LEODEGARIUS, archbishop of Vienne.—In a full synod grants the Church of St. Ferreolus to St. Victor, CXLIII, 1403.—Charter by which he gives the Church of St. Symphorianus to the abbey of St. Ferreolus, ibid., 1406.

LEOTALD, count of Mâcon.—Donation made to the monastery of Cluny, CXXXIII, 841.

LOTHAIR I, emperor.—Privilege for the monastery of Novalesa, CIV, 1151.—Privilege for the monastery of Prüm, ibid., 1158.—Grants many properties to the monastery of Nonantola, ibid., 1161.—Diploma for the monastery of Verona, ibid., 1223.—Writ for the Church of Arezzo, ibid., 1232.—Writ for the monastery of St. Ambrose at Milan, ibid., 1268.—Diploma for the monastery of Lucerne, ibid., 1308.

LUCIUS II, pope.—Privilege for the monastery of St. Columbanus at Bobbio, CLXXIX, 823.—Privilege confirming all the property and rights of the Holy Church of Ferrara, which is declared to be and remain, with all its appurtenances, under the perpetual right of the Apostolic See, ibid., 825.—Privilege for the monastery of St. Peter at Perugia, ibid., 828.—Privilege for the nunnery of the Holy Trinity of the Paraclete, ibid., 850.—Privilege for the Church of Cremona, ibid., 831.—Privilege for the monastery of St. John of Parma, of the Cistercian order, ibid., 838.—Privilege for the Church of Olivolo and for the monastery of Admont, ibid., 833, 837.—Privilege for the nunnery of Remiremont, ibid., 839.—Takes certain churches of the monastery of Marseilles under his protection and confirms the agreement made by Abbot Peter with Adhemar, bishop of Rodez, ibid., 843.—Confirms the privileges of Patriarch Henry of Grado and the possessions of his church, ibid., 845.—Confirms the possessions and diocesan boundaries of the Church of Regina, ibid., 847.—Privileges for the monasteries of St. Trudpert and St. Zeno, ibid., 850.—Bull for the monastery of Pontlevoy, ibid., 852.—Privilege for the Church of SS. Peter and Ursus at Aosta, ibid., 854.—Privilege for the hermitage of Fonte Avellana, ibid., 856.—Confirms the judgment issued by Innocent II in the dispute between the canons of St. Vincent and St. Alexander of Bergamo, ibid., 857.—General apostolic confirmation of the possessions of the Church of Lichfield, saving the canonical right of the bishop of Coventry, ibid., 861.—Secures certain churches to Roger, bishop of Coventry, and the Church of Lichfield, ibid., 862.—Bull confirming all the rights and privileges of the monastery of St. Mary of Châtillon, ibid., 862.—Privilege for the nunnery of Fontevraud, ibid., 864.—Privilege for the Church of Tours, ibid., 866.—Privilege for the Church of Bologna, ibid.—Takes the Church of St. Mary of Ardennes under protection and confirms its property, ibid., 869.—Confirms the primacy of the Church of Toledo, ibid., 871.—Privilege for the monastery of St. Bartholomew at Neuburg, ibid., 873.—Bull confirming Urban II’s judgment concerning the subjection of the Church of Dol to the Church of Tours, ibid., 875.—To the bishops of Saint-Brieuc and Tréguier: absolves them from the obedience promised to the bishop and Church of Dol, ibid., 977.—Bull for the Church of St. Martin at Tours, ibid., 878.

Privileges for the Premonstratensian order and the Church of St. Martin at Laon, CLXXIX, 880, 882.—For the Churches of St. Peter at Faenza and Rimini, ibid., 884.—Secures to the monastery of Cluny the manor of Lecdecumba, ibid., 887.—Cluniac privilege, ibid., 888.—For the monastery of St. Bertin at Sithiu, ibid., 891.—For the monastery of Faremoutiers, ibid., 892.—Takes the Church of St. Peter at Faenza under protection and confirms the possessions and privileges of its canons, ibid., 894.—Concerning the monastery of Tournus, ibid., 896.—Privilege for the monastery of St. Mary of Fontvive, ibid., 900.—For the Church of the Holy Sepulchre at Jerusalem, ibid., 903.—Takes the monastery of St. Mary of Ebron under protection, confirming its possessions and privileges, ibid., 905.

Bull confirming the monastery of St. Mary at Regensburg, CLXXIX, 907.—Takes the monastery of Stavelot under his protection and confirms its privileges, ibid., 909.—Concerning the monastery of All Saints, ibid., 911.—Bull for the abbey of St. Apollinaris at Classe, ibid., 912.—Privilege for the Church of St. Mary at Ilbenstadt, ibid., 914.—Privilege concerning churches subject to the bishop of Paris and concerning the exemption, granted by the Most Christian King Louis, of the deceased bishop’s household goods, ibid., 915.—Takes the monastery of Savigny under his protection and confirms its possessions, ibid., 917.—Privilege for the abbey of St. Martin of the Fields, ibid., 918.—Commends the monks of Savigny, ibid., 920.—Privilege for the Church of Blessed Mary of Rheno, ibid.—Privilege for the monastery of St. Magnus at Regensburg, [Col. 0097] ibid., 922.—Bull for the Church of St. Augustine at Canterbury, ibid., 925.—Grants certain privileges to William, patriarch of Jerusalem, ibid., 927, 929.—Privilege for the monastery of Bamberg, ibid., 933.

LUCIUS III, pope.—Takes the monastery of St. Peter in Chains at Ravenna under protection and confirms its property and rights, CCI, 1071.—Concerning the monastery of St. Mary of Gallomont,
