### III.—Christ’s faithful have been accustomed to perform good works, namely fasts, almsgiving, and so forth, which benefit both the dead and themselves after death, Tertullian, I, 926; II, 737

An offering is made for the dead, St. Cyprian, IV, 399.---The merits of martyrs and the works of the righteous benefit the dead detained in purgatory, ibid., 480. St. Ambrose considers that the soul of his deceased sister should be commended to the Lord not by tears but by offerings, XVI, 1099.---Offerings are made for the dead, St. Augustine, XXXIII, 92.---Works of mercy toward the dead are prescribed, id., XXXV, 1350.---The spirits of the dead are aided by the prayers of the Church, the saving sacrifice, and almsgiving, id., CXXXVIII, 936, 937.---Sacrifices of the altar and almsgiving are performed for the dead, id., XL, 158, 283.---Works of piety for the dead who are very good are thanksgivings; for those who are not very bad, propitiations, ibid., 284.---Sacrifices of the altar, prayers, and almsgiving are offered for the dead, ibid., 609.---The dead are helped by prayers and other pious works, ibid., 1320, 1329.---Offerings are customarily made for the dead, Cassian, XLIX, 529–531.---Offerings are made for the dead, St. Gregory of Tours, LXXI, 875–877.---The offering for the dead was instituted, St. Germanus, LXXII, 289.---Donations were made for the performance of offerings for the dead, ibid., 435, 436.---Donations offered for the dead were received at the offertories, ibid., 223.---The dead receive refreshment through the prayers of those who fast and through sacrifice, ibid., 262–264.---Those who withhold offerings for the dead are excommunicated, St. Isidore of Seville, LXXXIV, 259.---Let us send little gifts of charity after our beloved dead, Alcuin. To pray, fast, give alms, and celebrate Masses for the faithful dead is good and salutary for them, Alcuin, C, 321, 322, 473, 474; CI, 488.---Almsgiving is performed in the Church for the dead, ibid., 1279.---It must not be denied that the souls of the dead can be relieved by the piety of their living relatives when the sacrifice of the Mediator is offered for them or almsgiving is performed in the Church.---When sacrifices, whether of the altar or of any almsgiving, are offered for baptized dead persons, they are propitiations for those who are not very bad, Amalarius, CV, 1162, 1163.---There must be no doubt that the dead are aided by the prayers of the holy Church, the saving sacrifice, and almsgiving [lacuna], Jonas of Orléans, CVI, 262.---It is the duty of Christians to bring aid to the spirits of the dead through prayers and almsgiving, ibid., 264, 265.---Those detained in purgatory are released from punishments by the prayers, almsgiving, fasts, and tears [lacuna] of friends, Haymo, CXVIII, 936, 937.---For those who fell while fighting faithfully in battle, offerings of almsgiving, prayers, and the sacred victim ought confidently to be made.---Hincmar, CXXV, 844.---There are dead persons who, released from punishments by the devout prayers, almsgiving, fasts, tears, and offerings of the saving victim of faithful friends, attain the repose of the blessed, ibid., 912.---Those who deny offerings for the dead to churches are immediately to be excommunicated, Isidore Mercator, CXXX, 348.---Let one who defrauds the Church of offerings for the dead be expelled from the Church, ibid., 342, 397.---Those who retain offerings for the dead and delay in handing them over to churches are to be expelled from the Church as unbelievers, Regino of Prüm, CXXXII, 355; Burchard, CXL, 701.---We ought not to grieve for the dead, but rather render them the offices of piety, id., CXL, 1008, 1009.---I cede an estate to the Church for my parents, living and dead, St. Odilo, CXLII, 834.---Those who reject prayers, offerings, and sacrifices for the dead are reproved, St. Peter Damian, CXLIV, 337.---A certain woman tries to redeem the soul of her deceased husband by almsgiving, id., CXLV, 568.---A monk of Fulda, having refused a prebend or alms for the benefit of a dead person, was divinely beaten with scourges, Othlo, CXLVI, 371.---The prayers, almsgiving, fasts, and especially the celebration of Masses of the living aid many dead persons, so that they may be released even before the Day of Judgment, ibid., 382.---For the soul of an excommunicated brother, the office and almsgiving are ordered to be performed immediately, as though he had died that very day, Adam, CXLVI, 685, 785.---It is not permitted to offer oblations for deceased impious persons, St. Anselm, CXLIX, 566.---Offices and almsgiving are performed for the dead [lacuna], Hugh, CLIV, 347.---Before Lord Basolus, Drogo of Estraines gave something to St. Mansuetus for his own soul and the souls of his forebears, Pibo, CLVII, 434.

For the salvation of their souls, they conveyed a certain estate, Sigebert, CLX, 629.---For the salvation and absolution of a dead person, a tithe of cultivated lands is given, ibid., 652.---For the dead we solemnly make supplication by sacrifices of the altar, prayers, and almsgiving, St. Ivo, CLXI, 191.---Those who either deny offerings for the dead to churches or return them with difficulty are excommunicated as murderers of the needy, ibid., 248.---That which the neighbors and friends of the dead freely wish to give for their name and redemption ought to be accepted, ibid., 249.---The soul of the dead must be assisted by every means of the Christian religion, ibid., 1240.---Sacrifices both of the altar and of almsgiving are offered for all baptized dead persons, Hugh of St. Victor, CLXXV, 594, 595.---“I shall rise to aid the dead; I shall plead with groanings, implore with sighs, intercede with prayers, and make satisfaction by sacrifice,” St. Bernard, CLXXXII, 654.---On offering sacrifice for the dead and on almsgiving to be performed for them, Peter the Venerable, CLXXXIX, 893.---Against those who say that the almsgiving, fasts, solemnities of Mass, or other prayers of the living do not benefit the faithful departed, Bernard, CCIV, 828.---How greatly the offering of the faithful benefits the spirits of the dead, ibid., 832.---The most valiant man Judas sent drachmas to Jerusalem so that a sacrifice might be offered for the sins of the dead, Alan of Lille, CCX, 376.---Whoever dies in the unity of the Church shares in all the benefits which are performed for one dead person, Peter of Poitiers, CCXI, 1272.---Almsgiving, prayers, fasts, and sacrifices are made with a view to the dead, Sicard, CCXIII, 430.

### IV.—It has been believed with constant faith in the Catholic Church that the offerings of priests, prayers of the righteous, almsgiving of loved ones, fasts of friends, and other such good works benefit souls detained in purgatory, Tertullian, II, 737

## CHAPTER V.—ON THE RELATIONS BETWEEN THE CHURCH SUFFERING AND THE CHURCH TRIUMPHANT

The merits of martyrs and works of the righteous benefit the dead detained in purgatory, St. Cyprian, IV, 480.---The intercession of the saints benefits the dead, St. Leo the Great, LV, 136, 137.---The invocation of holy martyrs frees us from the punishment of purgatory, St. Gregory of Tours, LXXII, 800.---At the Assumption feast of the Virgin, she frees countless persons from the punishments of purgatory, St. Peter Damian, CXLV, 586. “Holy Mother of God, and all holy companies of seraphim and cherubim, intercede for us and for all faithful living and dead,” ibid., 930.---The intercession of the saints is effective for the dead, St. Bernard, CLXXXII, 1497.---Saints are to be invoked for the dead, id., CLXXXIII, 1097, 1098.---By prayers and other good offices of the friends of the dead, the saints assist their souls, Alan of Lille, CCX, 376.

See the Index on the Cult of Saints.

## CHAPTER VI.—WHAT IS THE CONDITION OF THE DEAD IN RELATION TO THE LIVING?

The souls of the dead know and are concerned about what happens among the living, St. Augustine, XXXVII, 1437.---The dead can know what is done here, either by God’s revelation or in another way, id., XL, 605, 799. The dead themselves can be sent to the living, ibid., 606.---Visitations by the dead predicting events, confirmed by their fulfillment, id., XXXIII, 697, 698.---Many dead persons have been seen entering houses just as they used to do, ibid., 697.---Many testify that in places where bodies are buried, and especially in basilicas, disturbances and prayers occur at night, ibid.---A certain holy priest is a witness of such a vision, [Col. 0256] ibid., 696.---From the Gospel it is inferred that the dead have some concern for us, St. Augustine, XXXVII, 1437; XL, 799.---A deceased wife is represented as concerned for her husband, id., 1075.---Dead persons seen by the living ask for burial, id., XL, 600.---The souls of the dead sometimes appear to human beings, id., XL, 1026.---The purgatory of certain saints was revealed to Isaac, disciple of Blessed Gunther, Othlo, CXLXI, 368. A dead person appears in order to console certain living persons, St. Stephen, CLXVI, 1367.---A dead person appears to someone sleeping, William, CXXIX, 1077.---While sleeping in bed, a certain person saw one of the canons of St. Mary’s, who had died many years before, appearing to him, Hermann, CLXXX, 67.---Whatever we do for our brethren, living or dead, we shall receive from them in reciprocal return, ibid., 79.---The torments of the dead increase because of the torments of the living whom they loved, Robert Pullus, CLXXXVI, 769.

[Col. 0255]

# CXXXI. INDEX ON THE CULT AND VENERATION SHOWN TOWARD THE DEAD, DEMONSTRATING THE TRADITION FROM THE HISTORY, LITURGY, AND MONUMENTS OF THE LATIN CHURCH

## NOTICE

Having examined throughout this volume all the matters concerning the immortality of the soul, purgatory, the cult and veneration of the saints, and likewise prayer, which are set forth in various indexes as transmitted and proclaimed by the Holy Fathers, you will now, pious reader, find with goodwill—and perhaps find it pleasing to peruse—whatever is reported in the whole *Patrology* concerning the offices paid to the dead.

It may manifestly and unquestionably be concluded from these materials that the bodies of Christians were not only honored with sacred rites, as temples of the Holy Spirit and as destined for the future resurrection, but that the errors of heretics are also refuted by that testimony.

For it is clearer than the sun: first, that the funeral rites of deceased Christians, whatever the rites of the Gentile nations, far surpassed them in sincere religion and fitting veneration; second, that in every preceding age not only prayers and mourning, but also the use of sacraments, lights, and the sacrifice of the Mass, were instituted in all churches, just as the same suffrages still flourish and endure in the Catholic Church. This is a new and not insignificant argument for the honor of this holy Church.

We have assigned to the present index a fourfold division of subjects: historical; testimonial, which also reproduces very many words of the Holy Fathers; liturgical; and monumental, in which we thought fit to report not everything, but at least some of the material concerning tombs and epitaphs.

[Col. 0265]

CXXXII. INDEX TO ANTICHRIST, INDICATING TO THE READER, ACCORDING TO THE JUDGMENTS OF THE HOLY FATHERS, VARIOUS SIGNS FORETELLING, ACCOMPANYING, AND FOLLOWING HIS COMING, TOGETHER WITH HIS FINAL END.

PART ONE.—Signs foretelling the coming of Antichrist.

I.—Prophecies of the Old Testament. Tertullian, II, 117; St. Cyprian, IV, 779; St. Ambrose, XIV, 684; Rufinus, XXI, 321; St. Augustine, XXXIV, 788; XLI, 695; Alcuin, C, 564, 1292; CI, 1296; St. Bruno of Asti, CLXIV, 438, 884; Rupert, abbot, CLXVII, 556; Venerable Godfrey, CLXXIV, 55, 56; Garner, abbot, CXCIII, 87.

II.—Prophecies of the New Testament. St. Augustine, XXXII, 908; XLI, 645; St. Gregory the Great, LXXVI, 650; Alcuin, CI, 1294, 1296.

III.—Figures and types—Abimelech: Rabanus Maurus, CVIII, 1172; St. Peter Damian, CXLV, 392, 470; Peter Lombard, CXCI, 501.—Antiochus: St. Cyprian, IV, 412, 669; St. Jerome, XXV, 568; St. Gregory the Great, LXXVI, 651; Rupert, abbot, CLXIX, 1069; Peter Lombard, CXCIII, 104.—Arius and every Arian: St. Hilary of Poitiers, X, 191; St. Ambrose, XV, 1808.—Auxentius: St. Hilary, X, 616.—Baal-peor: Rupert, abbot, CLXVII, 908, 909.—Emperor Constantius: St. Hilary, X, 581.—Doeg: Cassiodorus, LXX, 373; Rupert, abbot, CLXVII, 1107.—Heretics and sinners: St. Augustine, XXXIV, 1999; XLI, 679, 686, 687; St. Gregory the Great, LXXVI, 486.—The he-goat: Rupert, abbot, CLXVII, 819.—Nero: St. Augustine, XLI, 686.—Rhamnus: Rabanus Maurus, CVIII, 1171, 1172.—Sabellius: St. Ambrose, XV, 1808.

IV.—The time of Antichrist’s coming.—The time of Antichrist’s persecution is unknown, St. Augustine, XLI, 616.—Antichrist’s reign before the Day of Judgment, St. Augustine, XXXIV, 1998; St. Cyprian, IV, 358, 400.—He will rage at the end of the world, but for a short time, St. Gregory the Great, LXXXVI, 449.—Antichrist will rule at the end of the world, ibid., 520.—The belief that Antichrist would come in the time of Emperor Severus is refuted as an error in the historian’s chronology, St. Jerome, XXIII, 315.—The time of Antichrist foretold by St. Paul, St. Hilary, X, 611, 612.—The question is customarily asked: “When will this be?” It is altogether untimely, St. Augustine, XLI, 616.—“If it were useful for us to know this, from whom better would it be stated than from God Himself, the Teacher, to His questioning disciples?” ibid.—However the mystery of iniquity may be understood—by one person in one way, by another in another way—how long it will operate is hidden, St. Augustine, XXXIII, 908.—“The mystery of iniquity is already at work; only let him who restrains it now continue to restrain it, until he is removed from the midst; and then that lawless one will be revealed,” ibid.—Antichrist will come first, and then the Day of Judgment will come, id., XXXIV, 1998.—“But some will say: How is it the last time? How is it the last hour? Certainly Antichrist will come first, and then the Day of Judgment will come,” ibid.—“He will rule at the end of the world: ‘Can you bring forth Lucifer in his time, and make the evening-star rise over the children of the earth?’” St. Gregory the Great, [Col. 0266] LXXVI, 520.—With the end of the ages now impending, Lactantius, VI, 788.

The time of Antichrist has not yet arrived, Alcuin, CI, 1295.---Although we see that the Roman empire has already for the most part been destroyed, nevertheless, as long as the kings of the Franks endure, who ought to hold the Roman empire, the dignity of the Roman empire will not utterly perish, because it will stand in its kings, ibid.---Our teachers hand down that one of the kings of the Franks will hold the Roman empire in its entirety, and he will exist in the last times, ibid.---He will be the greatest and the last of all kings; after he has faithfully governed his kingdom, he will finally come to Jerusalem and lay down his sceptre and crown on the Mount of Olives. This will be the end and consummation of the Roman and Christian empire, ibid.---As we have in the Sibylline verses, in the time of the aforesaid king—whose name will be C—the king of the Romans of the whole empire, of great stature, handsome in appearance, radiant in countenance, and well-proportioned in every feature of his limbs, there will be great riches and the earth will yield its fruit; after this time Antichrist will come, ibid., 1296.---Then the most filthy nations will rise up from the north, which King Alexander enclosed in Gog and Magog; these are twenty-two kingdoms, whose number is as the sand of the sea. This time will precede the coming of Antichrist, ibid.---When the king of the Romans hears this, having summoned an army, he will defeat them; he will always have before his eyes the writing which says: “Let the king of the Romans claim for himself every kingdom of the earth,” ibid.---In the time preceding Antichrist, the last king of the Romans will devastate all islands and cities, destroy every temple of idols, summon all pagans to baptism, and the cross of Christ will be set up in every temple, ibid.---The Jews will then turn to the Lord. “In those days Judah will be saved, and Israel will dwell securely,” ibid.---After one hundred and twelve years of his reign have been fulfilled, the last king of the Romans will come to Jerusalem and there, as has been said, laying aside his diadem, will leave the kingdom of Christians to God the Father and to His Son Christ Jesus, ibid.---The last king of the Romans will have a glorious tomb, and this will immediately precede the coming of Antichrist, ibid.---Unless the Roman empire has first been laid waste and Antichrist has come beforehand, Christ will not come; for He is to come in order to destroy Antichrist, Rabanus Maurus, CXII, 569, 573.---Not to mention those who now exist, or who will yet exist until the end of the age, among whom Antichrist will certainly be, Hincmar, CXXV, 276; Blessed Lanfranc, CL, 342.---The time of Antichrist’s revelation or manifestation, ibid., 344.---When the Roman empire has been destroyed, “only this remains,” that he who holds now should hold, ibid., 343.---The Roman empire, or the faith, or nothing concerns us except holding the faith until he is taken out of the way; until the Roman empire is destroyed, or Antichrist is born, or he who holds the faith holds it until he dies. And then this lawless one will be revealed, [Col. 0267] ibid., 344.---The coming of Antichrist at the end of the age is again described, St. Bruno, CLXV, 270, 273.---For when he recounts his own matters, which are signified in holy Church when that dragon, who is now held shut up in the abyss, is brought out of the pit of the abyss, Rupert, CLXVIII, 1086.---“For unless the falling-away comes first and the man of sin, the son of perdition, is revealed,” Hervey of Bourg-Dieu, CLXXXI, 1391, 1394.

## V. Cause of Antichrist’s Coming

The kingdom of Antichrist will come because of the sins of the peoples, St. Gregory the Great, LXXVI, 343.---“He makes a hypocritical man reign because of the sins of the people,” ibid.---Those who are subject to evil prelates should ascribe it to their own fault: Antichrist will reign because of the sins of the peoples, ibid.---Judaea refused to have a king reign over her, and therefore, as her deserts required, received a hypocrite, ibid.

## PART II. Signs Accompanying the Coming of Antichrist

### I. Distinguishing Characteristics of Antichrist

Antichrist, a false prophet, St. Augustine, XLI, 679.---Antichrist, an apostate according to Blessed Paul, ibid., 685.---Some suspect Nero’s resurrection and that he will be Antichrist, ibid., 686.---Others think Nero was not killed, but removed from sight, ibid.---Antichrist, a sinful man, St. Gregory the Great, LXXVI, 486.---Antichrist, a vessel of perdition—that is, the devil having entered into a human being—ibid., LXXV, 1952.---Antichrist, a man assumed by the devil, ibid., 1117; LXXVI, 649, 651, 700.---Antichrist, a little king, ibid., LXXV, 1090.---Antichrist, a vessel of the devil, ibid., LXXVI, 716.---Antichrist, a damned man, ibid., 428.---Antichrist, the devil’s cave, ibid., LXXV, 1117 and 1118.---Antichrist is signified by evening, LXXVI, 519, 520.---Antichrist, the devil’s sword, ibid., 726.---Antichrist, the tail of Behemoth, ibid., 649.---Antichrist, a serpent and a horned viper (*cerastes*), ibid., 596.---Description of Antichrist raising his hand against God, ibid., 1009.---Daniel and Paul teach that Antichrist will rise against the Prince of princes and will be broken without human hand, ibid., LXXVI, 652.---Antichrist exalted by pride, ibid., 486.---The lofty arm: the proud elevation of Antichrist, ibid.---The warning of the coming judgment is mocked by him, ibid., 730.---Antichrist, said to bite the hoofs of the horse, ibid., 507.---Antichrist’s savagery extends to cruelty, ibid., 449.---He is more to be feared because of the signs he will perform than because of the punishments he inflicts on martyrs, ibid., 650.---Antichrist tortures with scourges and flashes forth with signs, ibid.---He will overcome some by force and deceive others by counterfeit powers, ibid.

Antichrist, head of the reprobate, ibid., LXXV, 1090.---Antichrist, exalting himself above everything called God or worshipped, ibid., LXXVI, 487.---Antichrist falsely claims to be Christ, St. Jerome, XXII, 423.---Antichrist’s covering is counterfeit power, ibid., 553.---Antichrist, an eagle because of pride, ibid., XXV, 568.---Many among us suppose that Nero Domitius will be Antichrist, ibid.---Antichrist, a man, St. Hilary, X, 298.---Antichrist, the man of sin, son of the devil, ibid., IX, 1075; Tertullian, II, 889.---Antichrist: son of the devil, portion of sin, defender of the law, St. Hilary, IX, 1056.---Antichrist, the abomination of desolation, ibid., 1054.---Antichrist will strike great terror into the Church, ibid., 1001, 1002.---Antichrist, denying that the Son possesses one divinity with the Father, ibid., X, 616.---Antichrist, the boundary-setting serpent, St. Cyprian, IV, 280.---Some think that what the holy Apostle said, “For already the mystery of iniquity is at work,” was intended to mean Nero, whose deeds already appeared like those of Antichrist; hence some suspect that Nero himself will rise again and be Antichrist, St. Augustine, XLI, 686.---Others think that Nero lives concealed in the vigor of the very age in which he was when he was believed to have perished, until he is revealed in his own time and restored to his kingdom, ibid.---Another king will arise from Syria, begotten by an evil spirit, the overthrower and destroyer of the human race. That king will indeed himself be most foul, but a prophet of lies, Lactantius, VI, 793.---Amid those evils, he shows plainly enough that an impious king will arise who will crush, torture, harass, and kill the remnants of that tyrant, and that this king will be Antichrist, ibid., 1008 and 1009.---The opinion of those asserting that Antichrist will be none other than the devil must be avoided; St. Jerome condemns them, ibid.---All Antichrist’s deeds and sayings are sins, Cassiodorus, LXX, 90.---For he will have no equal in crimes, ibid.---Because he will be a wicked persuader: those whom he cannot pervert by terror, he will at least attempt to turn aside by harmful rewards. Countless sins will undoubtedly appear in one whose entire life is called transgression. He adds, “and is not found,” ibid., 91.---All his paths are defiled, ibid., 87.

[Col. 0268] He is called Antichrist because he will be contrary to Christ in all things. Christ came humble; he will come proud, Alcuin, CI, 1291.---Not of a virgin alone, nor of a bishop and a nun, as others madly teach, but of a most unclean harlot and a most cruel villain, ibid., 1292.---Antichrist will be conceived, begotten, and born in sin, ibid.---At the very beginning of his formation, the devil, the head of pride, teacher of error, fullness of malice, will enter at the same time into his mother’s womb, ibid.---He is the king over all the children of pride, whose power will always be with him, ibid.---The devil will descend into the mother of Antichrist, ibid., 1293.---Antichrist: a man and the fountain of all sinners, ibid., 1295.---The son of perdition, the son of the devil—not by nature, but by imitation, because he will fulfill the devil’s will in every respect—ibid.---The fullness of diabolical power and of every malicious capacity will dwell in him; in him will be hidden all treasures of malice and iniquity, ibid.

What else will Antichrist say except that Jesus was not the Christ, but that he himself is what Jesus was falsely believed to be? St. Agobard, CIV, 94.---In this one blasphemy Antichrist surpasses the Jews: that he presumes to call himself Christ, ibid.---With God permitting and ordaining, the devil will prepare for himself a most suitable vessel, namely that damned and lost man, the head of the lost, ibid., 280.---Antichrist himself is king over all the children of pride, ibid., 281.---From this synagogue, in the last times, the most wicked son—that is, Antichrist—will be begotten, Rabanus Maurus, CVIII, 1171.---He, Antichrist, will be the son of the lost, that is, of the sinful synagogue, ibid.---Antichrist, who is said to be coming, whom else will he call himself but Christ God? Paschasius Radbertus, CXX, 798.---Since transgression is expressed by the number eleven, the author of transgression himself is judged to be the eleventh horn of this beast; thus it is said of Antichrist in St. Gregory’s *Moralia*, Book XXXI, Hincmar, CXXV, 276.---For a mere man is begotten, but he grows monstrously, advancing even to an allied power of angelic strength, ibid.---What is the tail of this Behemoth but that final manifestation of the ancient enemy, when he enters into his own vessel, that lost man who is especially called Antichrist? ibid.---He is called Antichrist because he is opposed to Christ, ibid., 281.---Antichrist will not seek God in order that his cruel sins may be forgiven, St. Bruno of Würzburg, CXLII, 73.---Of Antichrist it is said that all his paths are defiled, that is, his thoughts and deeds are foul, ibid. and following, 209.---The way of Antichrist, St. Peter Damian, CXLV, 287.---While new evils are always added to old, what else is happening except that the way of Antichrist is undoubtedly being paved, so that when he comes into the world far beyond the end of the age, he may enter freely without obstacle? ibid.---Since his way is certainly nothing else but our scandals, the same cause ought to restrain our footsteps which promises him that he may come with unimpeded steps, ibid.---The coming of Antichrist is arranged according to Satan’s working, or Satan will work in him, Blessed Lanfranc, CL, 344.---Antichrist will come in his own name, exalting himself, because he will come to preach not as sent by God but by his own pride, St. Bruno, CLXV, 492.---The conduct of Antichrist, Rupert, CLXVIII, 1030.---Reproof and description of Antichrist, ibid., 1187.---Job says: “His heart will be hardened like a stone,” because it will never be softened by any conversion of repentance, ibid., 1192.---Antichrist, a lying spirit, ibid., CLXIX, 537.---Why Antichrist is called a beast, ibid., 1063.---The conception of Antichrist, ibid.---The place of his birth, ibid., 1067.---Where Antichrist will be born, Hugh of St. Victor, CLXXV, 591.---What Antichrist’s wickedness will be, ibid., 593.---Whether Antichrist will be a mere man, ibid., 591.---The life of Antichrist, Peter Lombard, CXCI, 139–148.---Description of Antichrist, ibid., 501.---Antichrist called a dragon, Rev. Garnerius, CXCIII, 124.---Antichrist called a serpent, ibid., 126.---Called a little king, ibid., 127.---A lurking lion, ibid., 108, 109.

### II. Distinguishing Characteristics of Antichrist’s Disciples

Arius or Sabellius—indeed, all heretics—are Antichrists or his disciples, St. Ambrose, XV, 1808.---Heretics are called Antichrists insofar as they are his followers, St. Augustine, XLI, 686, 687.---Many Antichrists are in the Church: evil Christians opposed to Christ, ibid., XXXIV, 1999.---Antichrists are those who confess Christ with their mouths but differ from Christ in their conduct, ibid., 2001, 2002.---The love of faithlessness is the dwelling-place of Antichrist, St. Gregory the Great, LXXIX, 66.---Antichrist’s temptations are not absent even in the Church’s peace, ibid., LXXVI, 486.---His preachers are the mouth of Antichrist, ibid., 710.---His preachers burn with malice and shine by a simulation of virtue, ibid.---All wicked persons are disciples of Antichrist, [Col. 0269] ibid., LXXV, 1009.---Antichrist’s disciples are also crafty and double-dealing, ibid., 1023.---Antichrist already lives and rages in his members, ibid., LXXVI, 484, 485.---All wicked persons united to their head are members of Antichrist, ibid.---The business of Antichrist is carried on daily among the wicked, ibid., 486.---Men devoted to the earth are justly subjected to him, ibid., 1620.---Antichrist already has many witnesses, ibid., 653.---Who are Antichrist’s bones, and who his flesh, ibid., 654.---“This is Antichrist, who denies the Father and the Son.” From these words it is most clearly declared that the Jews are not only liars but also Antichrists, St. Agobard, CIV, 94.---Above all, by denying that Jesus, born of the Virgin Mary, is Christ, they have claimed for themselves alike the name and the speech of Antichrist, ibid.---In this the Jews equal Antichrist in wickedness, that they dare deny that Jesus was Christ, ibid.---If there are already many Antichrists, what else could they be called together with their head than pseudo-Christs? Paschasius Radbertus, CXX, 798.---Every word foreign to truth and alien to faith—what else do we call it than Antichrist? ibid.---And therefore, because this one word is true, if anything else is said against Christ, the person who bears it in his heart is rightly himself called Antichrist, ibid.---Bede calls heretics Antichrists, but also those who destroy by perverse arts the Catholic faith which they confess, Hincmar, CXXV, 281.---All these bear witness, as it were, to the great Antichrist who is to come at the end of the age, as to their own head, ibid.---None but Antichrists go out from Judas, the chief Antichrist, throughout all the time until that greatest Antichrist comes. For it is written: “The devil put it into Judas’s heart that he should betray him, and Satan entered into him,” ibid.

Judas was called the son of perdition, as is also the greatest Antichrist, ibid.---“The mystery of iniquity is already at work,” that is, secretly through its members, Blessed Lanfranc, CL, 343.---Everyone opposed to the word of Christ is Antichrist, St. Ivo, CLXI, 785.---Members of Antichrist, ibid., 1009–1012.---He will make the Jews especially his followers and heralds, St. Bruno, CLXIV, 438.---All who perform Antichrist’s works are Antichrists, ibid., 624.---His body, that is, all wicked persons of whom he is the head, is like cast shields, Rupert, CLXVIII, 1192.---His disciples will bear the sign of Antichrist, Rupert, CLXIX, 1077.---Antichrist’s counsellors are called the eyelids of dawn, Garnerius, CXCIII, 264.---Antichrist’s more wicked and powerful servants are represented by bones, ibid., 214.---Antichrist wishes those whom he compels, by entreaty or threats, to serve him to be marked on their foreheads with his character, Philip of Harvengt, CCIII, 825.---His crimes, ibid.---He wishes that none among his apostates be permitted to have any intercourse of human society unless he is fortified by a certain seal of apostasy, ibid.

### III. Effects of Antichrist’s Coming

First effect: a deceptive operation wrought falsely by Antichrist, St. Augustine, XLI, 687.---Second effect: Antichrist’s tribulation, a fire of testing, ibid.---Third effect: a great disturbance is imminent because of Antichrist’s signs, St. Gregory the Great, LXXVI, 709 and 710.---Fourth effect: the elect will be troubled and stagger when they see Antichrist’s prodigies, ibid., 712.---Fifth effect: the Jews’ faith in Antichrist, St. Ambrose, XIV, 1100.---Sixth effect: all the elect rebuke him, when they despise him and resist his wickedness by strength of mind, St. Gregory the Great, on Job 21, LXXV, 1117.---Seventh effect: the strength of the saints appears as straw against Leviathan and Antichrist, ibid., LXXVI, 728.---Eighth effect: Antichrist’s snares through false miracles, ibid., on Job 40, LXXVI, 704.---Ninth effect: for then iniquity will rage so unrestrainedly against the righteous that even the hearts of the elect will be struck with no small terror, ibid., on Job 19, LXXV, 1053.---Tenth effect: therefore let us consider what that temptation of the human mind will be when the devout martyr subjects his body to torments, yet before his eyes the torturer performs miracles, ibid., on Job 40, LXXVI, 650.---Eleventh effect: lamps come forth from his mouth, because they set the minds of hearers ablaze with love of faithlessness; and where they seem to shine by wisdom, there without doubt they burn up by wickedness, ibid., 710.---Twelfth effect: his preachers burn with malice and shine through a simulation of virtue, ibid.---Thirteenth effect: smoke is said to proceed from his nostrils because, from the snares of his miracles, a dark uncertainty is produced for a time even in the hearts of the elect, ibid., on Job 40, LXXVI, 712.---Fourteenth effect: for then every soul is like a boiling pot, enduring the assaults of its thoughts as though they were the foam of burning waves; the fire of zeal agitates them, while temporal oppression itself holds them within, as in a pot shut up inside, [Col. 0270] ibid., 713.---Fifteenth effect: when John recounted the signs of this beast, he added: “So that he makes fire come down from heaven” (Rev. 13:13), ibid.---Sixteenth effect: “Strength will dwell in his neck.” What is signified by the neck of this Leviathan except the extension of pride? ibid., 718.---Seventeenth effect: prophecy in the Church is hidden, the grace of healings is taken away, words of doctrine fall silent, and miraculous wonders are removed, ibid., 721.---Eighteenth effect: neither spear nor breastplate will be able to stand, so that, if heavenly help is absent, the sharpness of preachers may be blunted and their long-suffering and patience destroyed, ibid., 727.---Nineteenth effect: it is openly shown that, in long desiring God’s likeness, he wished to raise himself up, as though beside God, ibid., on Job 38, LXXVI, 487.---Twentieth effect: whenever you hear that those called Christs are named not from the Lord Jesus Christ but from someone else, ibid., St. Jerome, XXII, 182.---Twenty-first effect: and in the end let not the Jews, who will receive Antichrist in place of Christ, rejoice in Christ, St. Jerome, XXIII, 1051.---Twenty-second effect: at the consummation of the world, Antichrist will perform such signs and portents that, as iniquity increases, the love of many will grow cold, ibid., Commentary on Isaiah, ch. 14, XXIV, 212.---Twenty-third effect: Antichrist, received by the Jews, will stand in the place of sanctification, so that where God was invoked by the prayers of saints, there he, received by unbelievers, may be venerated with God’s honour, ibid., Commentary on Matthew, ch. 25, IX, 1054.---Twenty-fourth effect: the terror which he will strike into the Church, ibid., 1001, 1002.---Twenty-fifth effect: when Antichrist’s ministers transform themselves into an angel of light, Christ Himself is effaced from nearly everyone’s perception and consciousness, ibid., *Against Auxentius*, X, 611, 612.---Twenty-sixth effect: because false prophets will promise, as it were, present help in Christ to persons under great oppression, they will falsely say that Christ is present and found in many places, in order to lead the afflicted and oppressed into Antichrist’s service, ibid., Commentary on Matthew, IX, 1055.---Twenty-seventh effect: “And therefore God will send them [the Jews] an operation of error, so that they may believe a lie, and that all may be judged who did not believe the truth but consented to iniquity” (2 Thess. 2:3, 11), in Psalm CV, no. 37, St. Augustine, XXXVI, 1418.---Twenty-eighth effect: toil and pain, by which false doctrines are marked beneath his tongue, St. Gregory the Great, LXXVI, 704.

### IV. Antichrist’s Cunning, Simulations, and Snares

Then desolation will draw near, because many, having fallen away from true religion, will depart through error, St. Ambrose, XV, 1808.---Let the one who understands not be deceived into believing false things in preference to true ones, after the manner of the Jews, who denied the true Christ; whence it will follow that they believe him who is false to be true, ibid., 1809.---Therefore the signs of faithlessness, through which the days are shortened and diminished, must be guarded against, ibid., XIV, 1001.---“The devil who deceived them was cast into the lake of fire and sulphur,” St. Augustine, XLI, 679.---But also “into a friend,” that is, as a friend, ibid., 685.---Antichrist will work falsely, ibid., 687.---Antichrist will lie in wait secretly, like a lion in his den; he calls him a lion in his den, one in whom force and deceit will operate, ibid., XXXVI, 127, 128.---Antichrist will fulfill all the wickedness and impiety which all false prophets began, ibid., 126, 127.

The love of faithlessness is the dwelling-place of Antichrist, who contradicts faith in the Redeemer, St. Gregory the Great, LXXIX, 66.---To preach his falsehood, he will choose men who are crafty, double-dealing, and possessed of the knowledge of this world, ibid., LXXV, 1023.---Fickle minds marvel at and follow him in his prodigies; thus it is aptly said of him: “He was sweet to the gravel-beds of Cocytus,” ibid., 119.---Whoever receives within himself the counsels of the asp to be nourished, by his deeds becomes a member of the wicked head and grows into the body of Antichrist, ibid., 1090.---Who else is understood by the name of the beast except the ancient enemy, who fiercely assaulted the first man through deception? ibid., LXXVI, 428.---But when this beast, after the coming of the Redeemer, [lacuna] invades that damned man who is called Antichrist, what else does it do but enter its hiding-place, in order to dwell in its own cave? ibid.---What it means that deceit is directed in the hand of Antichrist: “Deceit will be directed in his hand,” ibid.---Deceit is directed in Antichrist’s hand because, in whatever he proposes to carry out temporally against the good, no adversity hinders him, ibid., 368.---Antichrist’s snares through false miracles, ibid., 704.---Because of perverse doctrines, toil and pain are beneath his tongue, ibid., 616.---Because of the appearance of miracles he sits in ambush; but because of the glory of worldly power, he sits in secret places with the rich, ibid., 704.---He employs at once the fraud of miracles [Col. 0271] and earthly power, and is said to sit in secret places and there with the rich, ibid.---Antichrist’s path shines with miracles, and whether he comes forth in person or through his ministers, he flashes with lying signs, ibid., 116.---Toil and pain, by which false doctrines are marked beneath his tongue, ibid., 704.---The flame of his mouth is the very instigation of secret speech, ibid., 716.---He directs words of evil persuasion toward the mind of each individual, ibid.---What comes forth from his mouth is flame, because the mind burns in desires when it is incited by his suggestions, ibid.---He will overcome some by force and deceive others through feigned powers, ibid., 650.---Smoke comes from Leviathan’s nostrils because, through his lying prodigies, the mist of fear confounds even the eyes of good minds, ibid., 712.---Raising himself against God, he is exalted both by a simulation of holiness and by the swelling of power, ibid., 718.---Antichrist is a *regulus*, for the *regulus* is called king of serpents, ibid., LXXV, 1090.---Antichrist will proceed in his deceit, but during the brief span of this present life that very deceit will prosper, ibid., LXXVI, 529.---Then another must be received, coming in the same name. But he is a man, from whom people will hope for honour for themselves and to whom they will render honour in return, St. Hilary of Poitiers, X, 298.---And that Antichrist is signified by him is not obscure: he glories in the falsehood of a paternal name, ibid.---Scripture composed in Antichrist’s style, ibid., 614.---Whoever believes and joins himself to him will be marked by him like cattle; whoever refuses will either flee to the mountains or be tortured and killed, Lactantius, VI, 794.---Then he will be loosed and go forth, and through that vessel of his he will terribly deceive the nations, Alcuin, CI, 1292.---His miracles will be false, lies, and alien to truth, because by magical art and illusion he will deceive men, just as Simon Magus also deceived the man who, thinking he was killing him, killed a ram in his place, ibid., 1293.---But all these miracles will in every way be false through diabolical incantations; they will appear true to sinners and unbelievers, ibid., 1294.---Deceit and iniquity are beneath his tongue, St. Agobard, CIV, 280.---He lies in wait near the entrances in hidden places, in order to kill the innocent, ibid.---He lies in wait in secret like a lion in his den, ibid.---In the Psalm, “Why do you glory in malice, you who are mighty in iniquity, etc.,” it is shown what this body of the devil and Antichrist is in the present, and what awaits it in the future, ibid., 281.---Antichrist speaks wholly with deceit, St. Bruno of Würzburg, CXLII, 209.---Antichrist’s wickedness is evident from the fact that he will be an evil persuader, so that those whom he cannot pervert by terror he may at least attempt to turn aside by harmful rewards, ibid., 75.---“You have loved all words of ruin, deceitful tongue,” is said of Antichrist, who in confused morals loves iniquity, ibid., 209.---In the estimation of deceivers and in his own simulation he will be a lamb, but in reality a goat—indeed, a beast, or a horn of the beast—in whose pride and credulity he will feast, Rupert, CLXVII, 1801.---Those deceived by Antichrist are not believed likely to return to the faith, Robert Pullus, CLXXXVI, 978.

### V. Antichrist’s Battles against the Saints of God

Martyrs will suffer under Antichrist, St. Gregory the Great, LXXIX, 527.---There is nevertheless one thing that is not repeated in the same way: there it is said “like fragments of pomegranate,” but here “like the rind of pomegranate,” ibid.---I think this signifies nothing except the blood of martyrs who will die under Antichrist, and the unity of faith in which many Jews will be bound together, ibid.---As they endure the shedding of blood in that steadfastness, they will be adorned by the tribulation of faith, like the redness of the rind, ibid.---The dragon’s tail casts stars down to the earth because that final manifestation of Satan, raised up through the boldness of the man he has assumed, by gaining possession of some whom it finds in the Church as though God’s elect, reveals them to be reprobate, ibid., LXXVI, 651.---*Κέρατα* (*kerata*) is Greek; in Latin it means “horns.” This serpent is said to be horned because Antichrist arms himself against the life of the faithful not only with the bite of deadly preaching but also with horns of power, ibid., 596.---“For he stretched out his hand against God, and strengthened himself against the Almighty,” ibid., LXXV, 1009.---“He ran against Him with uplifted neck and armed with a fat neck,” ibid.---“Who will rebuke his way before him?” That is, who will dare rebuke that man, whose very sight almost inspires terror? ibid.---Deceit is directed in Antichrist’s hand because, in whatever he proposes to carry out temporally against the good, no adversity hinders him, ibid., LXXVI, 368.---Through Antichrist the devil will rage more fiercely; he burns only wood, hay, and straw, and tears extinguish his flame, ibid., 716.---The flame going forth from his mouth burns only wood, hay, and straw, ibid.---The strength of the saints appears as straw against Leviathan and Antichrist; yet “he can do nothing against their soul,” ibid., 728.---Jews converted in Antichrist’s time will suffer grievous persecutions, ibid., 921.---The prophet is commanded to be shut up [Col. 0272] in the midst of his house, because in Antichrist’s time the converted people of the Jews will be pressed by harsh persecutions from those nations which have remained in unbelief, ibid., 921.---“But the court which is outside his temple, cast out and do not measure it, because it has been given to the nations, and they will trample the holy city for forty-two months,” ibid.---Then iniquity will rage so unrestrainedly against the righteous, ibid., LXXV, 1053.---“Who will rebuke his way before him?” For who indeed but God, by whose aid the elect are strengthened so that they may resist?---Although his savagery extends to cruelty, heavenly mercy nevertheless constrains it by the shortness of the days, ibid., LXXVI, 449.---“Then there will be great tribulation, such as has not been from the beginning of the world until now, nor ever will be,” ibid., 650.---He is more to be feared because of the signs he will perform than because of the punishments he inflicts on martyrs, ibid.---But it must be carefully considered, when this Behemoth raises his tail like a cedar, in what manner he will then rise forth more terrible than he now displays himself, ibid.---He then moves with such great power that, if possible, he may trouble even the elect members of the Lord, ibid., 709.---When terrible signs are seen, a dark thought gathers in the hearts of the elect, ibid., 712.---How greatly the elect will then boil with zeal: “like a heated and boiling pot,” ibid., 713.---Antichrist will fight against the saints of the Lord, St. Jerome, XXVI, 984.---And finally we may understand as those who will fight under Antichrist against the saints of the Lord those who are gathered for this purpose, that they may perish, ibid.---The abomination of desolation, because by wars and slaughter he will lay waste the earth with sacrilege, St. Hilary, IX, 1054.---The four watches of God over the Church. The terror of Antichrist. Yet amid these things the disciples are delayed by wind and sea, and are tossed by all the movements of the age, while the unclean spirit opposes them, ibid., 1001, 1002.---For he will come to those especially anxious and afflicted. And because, through familiarity with Antichrist, they will be alarmed by every novelty of temptation, they will tremble even at the Lord’s coming, fearing false appearances of things and fictions creeping before their eyes, ibid.---Elijah and Enoch are sent into the world against Antichrist’s assault, Alcuin, CI, 1296.---Against Antichrist’s assault the two great prophets will fortify, instruct, strengthen, and prepare the faithful for battle with divine weapons, ibid.---The killing of Elijah and Enoch by Antichrist, ibid., 1297.---After they have completed their preaching, Antichrist will rise against them and kill them, ibid.---But after three days they, having been slain, will be raised by the Lord. Afterwards, while persecuting the remaining faithful, he will either put them to the sword or make them apostates, ibid.---Elijah with Enoch and all the elect will resist him, St. Ivo, CLXI, 1010.---How great a subversion of Christians will be wrought by Antichrist, St. Bruno of Asti, CLXV, 270, 273.---He will overcome even the prophets and Enoch, and bring them to their end by martyrdom, ibid., 674.---Antichrist will make war, Abbot Rupert, CLXIX, 1029.---After John has described the Church’s manifold warfare, he adds that during this warfare the devil is prepared to inflict harm, yet is restrained by God lest His own people grow sluggish or despair, Richard of St. Victor, CXCVI, 770.

VI. The temple in which he will sit. — It is uncertain in what temple of God Antichrist will sit, St. Augustine, XLI, 685. — It is uncertain whether Antichrist will sit in the ruined temple built by King Solomon, or rather in the Church, ibid. — He will not sit in the temple of any idol or demon; for the Apostle would not call the temple of an idol or demon the temple of God, ibid. — Some wish Antichrist in this passage to be understood not as the prince himself, but in some sense as his entire body, that is, the multitude of persons belonging to him, together with their own prince, ibid. — Some think that it may more correctly be said even in Latin, as it is in Greek, not “that he sits in the temple of God,” but “that he sits into the temple of God,” as though he himself were the temple of God, which is the Church; just as we say *sedet in amicum*, “he sits as a friend,” that is, as though he were a friend, ibid. — Antichrist will be made manifest by these words of Paul; for he says, “that he may be revealed in his own time,” ibid., 908. — Antichrist will reign, or he will come first, and then the day of judgment will come, the same author, XXXIV, 1998. — Antichrist will attain the empty and futile summit of dominion, the same author, XXXVI, 126, 127. — Antichrist will possess force in his rule: “like a lion in his lair”; what is said of the lion refers to force, ibid., 127, 128. — The tabernacle of Antichrist is love of unbelief, by which he opposes faith in the Redeemer. The Jews now remain in it, because, while they lovingly inhabit the abode of their unbelief, they fight against the Redeemer, St. Gregory the Great, LXXIX, 66. — Antichrist is called a “young serpent.” But who is the head of the reprobate except Antichrist? Therefore, what has been warmed will break forth into a young serpent, the same author, LXXV, 1090. — He is permitted to be exalted for a short time, so that, in proportion as he is allowed to glory briefly, he may be punished more severely forever, [Col. 0273] ibid., 1009. — He will be called Antichrist, because he will endeavor to spread his name far and wide; this is now imitated by everyone who strives to extend the glory of his praise through remembrance of an earthly name and rejoices in passing renown, ibid., 1052. — Antichrist endeavors to establish his memory on earth when, in seeking earthly glory, he desires, if possible, to remain forever, ibid., 1053. — He delights for his name to be celebrated in the streets when he spreads the activity of his wickedness far and wide, ibid. — Antichrist will reign because of the sins of the peoples, the same author, LXXVI, 343. — Since Antichrist will also appear after these things, Solomon added this as a fourth point there, saying: “And the fool appeared after he had been raised on high,” ibid., 528. — He himself will be raised on high when he falsely claims to be God, ibid. — The power to carry out the wickedness of Antichrist’s pride will be added to him, ibid., 718. — From the words, “Arise, O Lord; let not man prevail; let the nations be judged before him”: he seems to make mention of Antichrist. For that man of sin will be strengthened to such an extent that he will sit in the temple of God and even call himself God, Rufinus, XXI, 683, 684. — Antichrist will reign in the world before Christ comes a second time to earth to judge all humankind, St. Maximus of Turin, LVII, 225. — He will exalt himself even above all the gods of the nations, because he will make himself greater and stronger than all; and also above everything worshipped, that is, above the Holy Trinity, Alcuin, CI, 1295. — He will exalt himself so that he sits in the temple of God, showing himself as though he were God, ibid. — Coming to Jerusalem, he will circumcise himself and say to the Jews: “I am Christ, promised to you, who have come for your salvation, that I may gather and defend you who are scattered,” ibid., 1296. — Antichrist will grow into such great wickedness that, being the worst of all men, he may display himself and be heard as though he were a god, and rise up against all things, St. Agobard, CIV, 280. — He will exalt himself, so as to boast himself above everything called god or worshipped, ibid. — “There is no power on earth comparable to him, who was made to fear no one. He sees every height,” ibid. — It is said of him: “When the sword seizes him, it will not be able to stand, nor spear, nor breastplate,” ibid., 281. — Antichrist “speaks in his heart: ‘I shall not be moved from generation to generation,’” ibid. — Having gathered the impious to himself, Antichrist will wickedly usurp the kingdom, as Abimelech did, Rabanus Maurus, CVIII, 1171. — The son of perdition, who opposes and exalts himself above everything called God or worshipped, so that he sits in the temple of God, showing himself as though he were God, the same author, CXII, 569, 573. — He will enter houses of prayer and sit there as though he himself were Christ and therefore ought to be worshipped by human beings in the rank of God, ibid. — As it is written, he will reign for a time, times, and half a time; that is, for no more than three and a half years, St. Bruno of Segni, CLXIV, 725. — The Jews, however, will receive Antichrist and worship him as God for a time, the same author, CLXV, 492. — The voice, exaltation, and hatred of Antichrist toward Christians, Peter Lombard, CXCI, 779–782. — The coming dominion of Antichrist, ibid., 139–148. — He will falsely claim to be God, Rev. Garnerius, CXCIII, 87. — Antichrist will have power against the continual sacrifice because of sins, ibid., 193. — How great will be the tyranny of Antichrist, Abbot Wolbero, CXCV, 1063.

VII. Miracles, power, and brief glory of Antichrist. — “The days are shortened where Antichrist is; therefore the signs of unbelief are to be guarded against, by which the days are shortened and diminished,” St. Ambrose, XIV, 1001. — The power of Antichrist will last three years and six months. Although this period is very short, it is rightly uncertain whether it belongs to the thousand years during which he says that the devil is bound and the saints reign with Christ, or whether this small interval is added to those same years and thus lies outside them, St. Augustine, XLI, 678. — Antichrist will perform such great signs that, if possible, he will deceive even the elect, the same author, XXXVI, 126, 127. — He will have force in his rule and deceit in his miracles, ibid., 127, 128. — What else is understood by the lofty arm but the proud height of Antichrist, raised above the reprobate minds of men by the arrogance of temporal glory? St. Gregory the Great, LXXVI, 486. — While he bestows gifts on the perverse, raises them to honors in this world, and displays prodigies to their eyes, fickle minds admire and follow him because of his wonders, the same author, LXXV, 1119. — How brief is the glory of Antichrist and of all the wicked, ibid., 1052. — From that past glory he will be cast down [lacuna] at the end of the world with his followers, ibid., 1053. — The folly of Antichrist, raised on high, will become apparent, the same author, LXXVI, 528. — He mocks the announcement of the future judgment and thereby becomes more cruel, ibid., 728. — “And he will mock the brandished spear”: for the Lord brandishes a spear against Leviathan, threatening him, in his destruction, with a strict sentence, ibid., 730. — The path of Antichrist will shine with miracles, ibid., 737. — He is raised so high by so many signs and prodigies in the display of holiness that his acts cannot be reproved by a human being, the same author, LXXV, 1117. — At the end of the world he will rage, but for a short time, the same author, LXXVI, 449. — He will be feared more for the signs which he performs than for the punishments which he inflicts, ibid., 650. — How great the disturbance caused by Antichrist’s miracles, ibid., 709. — Antichrist employs such great signs and prodigies that by the power of miracles he appears to shine as though with the light of fire, ibid. — Since his agitated head strives to become illustrious through miracles, his sneezing is rightly called “the splendor of fire,” ibid. — The elect will be troubled and stagger when they see Antichrist’s prodigies, ibid., 712. — The power to carry out the wickedness of Antichrist’s pride will be added to him, ibid., 718. — Neither spear nor breastplate will be able to stand, so that, if heavenly help is absent, he will both blunt the sharpness of preachers and destroy the endurance of patience, ibid., 727. — Antichrist will exalt himself above God, ibid., 487. — The Apostle openly shows this: “Exalting himself above everything that is called God or worshipped” (2 Thess. 2:4), because, long ago desiring God’s likeness, he wished to raise himself as though beside God; but as his fault increased in pride, he now exalts himself above everything called and worshipped as God, ibid. — Antichrist will perform many signs, St. Jerome, XXIV, 212. — He will set himself up and call himself God; he will command himself to be worshipped and call himself the Son of God; and authority will be given him to perform signs and prodigies, Lactantius, VI, 794. — Thus David proclaimed in a loud voice: “Arise, O Lord; let not man prevail.” For he is the worst man, whom human nature cannot endure, in whom there will be such cunning or power that the Lord’s strength alone can overcome his wickedness, Cassiodorus, LXX, 86. — His preaching and power will extend from sea to sea, from east to west, and from north to north, Alcuin, CI, 1293. — He will also perform many signs and great and unheard-of miracles, ibid. — He will cause fire to descend terrifyingly from heaven; he will make trees suddenly blossom and grow, or wither, ibid. — He will make the sea turbulent and suddenly calm; he will also cause natures to be changed into various forms, and other marvels besides, innumerable and astounding, ibid. — He will make the dead rise in the sight of human beings, “so that, if possible, even the elect may be led into error,” ibid. — The perfect and the elect will doubt, when they see such great and such extraordinary things, whether or not he is the Christ who, according to the Scriptures, is to come at the end of the world, ibid. — He will rise against the faithful in three ways: by terror, gifts, and miracles, ibid., 1294. — He will give wealth of gold and silver to those who believe in him—for in his time hidden treasures will be revealed—ibid. — Those whom he cannot corrupt by gifts he will overcome by terror; but those whom he cannot conquer by terror he will attempt to seduce by signs and miracles, ibid. — Antichrist will come with every power, with signs and miracles, and with lying wonders, either because he will appear to act but will not truly act, and with every seduction of iniquity for those who perish, because they have not received love of the truth, Blessed Lanfranc, CV, 344. — Therefore God will send them the working of error, Antichrist the worker, so that they may believe the lie, in order that all who have not believed the truth but have consented to iniquity, to the devil, may be judged and condemned, ibid. — What will he do when he comes? He will command the Sabbath to be observed, St. Ivo, bishop of Chartres, CLXI, 265. — For because he pretends to die and rise again, he wishes the Lord’s Day to be held in veneration, ibid. — Doubt will be generated in the hearts of the faithful by Antichrist’s treacherous miracles, Rev. Garnerius, CXLIII, 264, 265.

VIII. The blessedness, or apparent happiness, of Antichrist before human beings. — Antichrist will appear so blessed to human beings that he will even be thought God, St. Augustine, XXXVI, 126. — Antichrist will fulfill all the wickedness and impiety which all false prophets began, ibid., 127. — The path of Antichrist will shine with miracles, St. Gregory the Great, LXXVI, 737. — The power to carry out the wickedness of Antichrist’s pride will be added to him, ibid., 718. — Antichrist will proceed prosperously, ibid., 529. — Antichrist will abound in all the pomps of the age, Cassiodorus, LXX, 575. — He will be rich not only in gold, but also in the multitude of nations and the dominion of lands; he will likewise delight in the display of miracles, boast in the pursuit of perverse honor, and be utterly full of the other vices, all of which seem to be understood under the name Egypt, ibid., 376. — Then, having temporarily obtained the world’s glory, Antichrist will surpass human measure by the height of honor and the power of signs, Hincmar, CXXV, 279. — The proud height of Antichrist signified by the arm, the same author, CXCIII, 193.

IX. Cruel persecutions of Antichrist against God’s elect. — Antichrist, that is, temporal tribulation, is rightly called the sword of the devil, St. Gregory the Great, LXXVI, 726. — Converted Jews will suffer grievous persecutions in the time of Antichrist, ibid., 921. — The prophet is commanded to be shut up within his own house because, in Antichrist’s time, the converted people of the Jews will be hemmed in by harsh persecutions from those nations which remain in unbelief, ibid. — In Antichrist’s final persecution, the light of faith will be taken away from evil Christians: “His light shall be taken away from the wicked,” ibid., 484. — The light of faith will be taken away from those who believe and live wickedly, especially in the time of Antichrist’s persecution, ibid. — Nor does God’s light now illumine those who cloak the malice of their own iniquity with the name of faith, ibid. — Although Antichrist’s savagery expands into cruelty, heavenly mercy nevertheless constrains it by the shortness of the days, ibid., 449. — Antichrist will torture martyrs with torments and shine with signs, ibid., 650. — Let us consider what that temptation of the human mind will be when the devout martyr submits even his body to torments, and yet his torturer performs miracles before his eyes, ibid. — Whose strength would not be shaken from the very depth of his thoughts when the one who tortures with scourges shines with signs? ibid. — Antichrist is the abomination of desolation because he will devastate the earth with the guilt of wars and slaughter, St. Hilary, IX, 1054. — Meanwhile the disciples are tossed about by wind and sea, and by all the agitations of the age, while the unclean spirit opposes them, ibid., 1002; St. Cyprian, IV, 355, 592. — The strength and constancy of the stronger will be endangered, and unless God brings help they will fail, St. Gregory the Great, LXXVI, 727. — Where then will the weak be, if the strong are reckoned as chaff? ibid. — Then he will attempt to overthrow the temple of God and persecute the righteous people; there will be distress and affliction such as never was from the beginning, Lactantius, VI, 794. — The first persecution was violent, when Christians were compelled by proscriptions and tortures to sacrifice. The second was deceitful, carried on through heretics and false brethren. A third remains, to come through Antichrist, because nothing is more dangerous: for it will be both violent and deceitful, Rufinus, XXI, 685. — Antichrist, the Charybdis of blood, Prudentius, LIX, 837. — In his mouth he will have blasphemous cursing when he falsely claims to be the Son of God; bitterness, when he pronounces the penalty of death against those who resist him and commands those who have scorned to worship him as a deity to be brought to punishments, Cassiodorus, LXX, 88. — At first the persecution is only violent; the second, etc. [lacuna]; the last remains, which will be exceedingly violent by the power of a singular kingdom and deceitful through miracles, ibid. — Antichrist persecuting the Church is introduced in this manner: “And I will keep you from the hour of temptation which is to come upon the whole world,” Alcuin, C, 1112. — In Antichrist’s time there will be tribulation such as has not been from the beginning of the age, ibid. — The wounds of bodies will indeed be harsh, but the weapons of adversaries more grievous, ibid. — Those whom he cannot mock with signs, he will cruelly kill before all by a marvelous death after torture, the same author, CI, 1294. — Then there will be tribulation such as has not been on earth from the time when nations began to exist until that time, ibid. — Then every Christian who is found will either deny God or, if he remains in the faith, perish by sword, furnace-fire, serpents, beasts, or any other kind of torment, ibid. — After killing the noble sons—that is, those who, believing in Christ from different nations and languages, have been begotten by God—Antichrist will bring in persecution so as to kill all the saints, Rabanus Maurus, CVIII, 1171. — Antichrist will inflict persecution especially upon Christians, Guibert, CLVI, 700. — It is clear that Antichrist will wage war not against Jews or Gentiles, but, in accordance with the etymology of his name, will assault Christians, ibid. — It describes what devastation he will make in the Church, St. Bruno of Segni, CLXV, 673. — That Antichrist’s persecution will be great: “But woe to those who are pregnant and nursing in those days,” etc., Abbot Rupert, CLXVII, 1802. — Antichrist will bring about great tribulation, the same author, CLXIX, 1064. — He will persecute the Church with the greatest severity, Venerable Godfrey, CLXXIV, 170. — The cruelty of Antichrist, Peter Lombard, CXCI, 139, 148. — The persecution of Antichrist, Robert Pullen, CLXXXVI, 977. — Tribulation to come in the days of Antichrist, and the devilish tyranny to be restrained by Christ’s rule, Richard of St. Victor, CXCVI, 769. — The fury of cruelty will rage more fiercely in Antichrist’s time, ibid. — Holy Church everywhere will suffer the cruelty of persecution through the shedding of blood, ibid. — All who are exalted through eminence in virtues, shaken by the waves of persecution, will separate themselves from the wicked by faith and works, ibid. — There will be a time such as has not been since nations began to exist until that time, ibid., 770.

X. How long will Antichrist’s calamities and temptations endure? — The days are shortened where Antichrist is, St. Ambrose, [Col. 0276] XIV, 1001. — “For the sun will be darkened and the stars will fall,” that is, the righteous of God. “When you see these things, believe that Christ is still delayed”; for where Christ is, faith is brighter; where Antichrist is, the days are shortened, ibid. — Antichrist’s persecution will last three years and six months, St. Augustine, XLI, 678. — This final persecution, which will be brought about by Antichrist, as we have already said—for this is set down earlier both in this book (Rev. 10 and 11) and in the prophet Daniel (Dan. 12)—will last three years and six months, ibid. — Because he is permitted to be exalted for a short time, so that, insofar as he is allowed to glory briefly, he may be punished more severely forever, St. Gregory the Great, LXXV, 1009. — While he endeavors to spread the glory of his praise through remembrance of an earthly name and rejoices in passing renown, ibid., 1052. — May he quickly lose the praise of earthly power and lose every joy in his own name, ibid., 1053. — Antichrist will rage at the end of the world, but for a short time, the same author, LXXVI, 650. — This terrible tribulation will last three and a half years throughout the whole world: “Then the days will be shortened for the sake of the elect,” Alcuin, CI, 1294. — When this Antichrist, the devil’s son and most evil craftsman of all wickedness, has afflicted the entire world for three and a half years, [lacuna] at last God’s judgment will come, ibid., 1297. — Of these things nothing remains to be expected that is not already seen, except Satan’s release and the public trampling of the holy city for forty-two months; this will come through Antichrist, the head of all the wicked, St. Agobard, CIV, 69. — Otherwise, people of that age could know the time of judgment if it followed immediately after the three and a half years from the beginning of Antichrist’s persecution, Hincmar, CXXV, 798. — St. Jerome, explaining Daniel’s statement, says: “Blessed are those who, after Antichrist has been killed, wait beyond 1,220 days—that is, three and a half years plus forty-five days—for the Lord and Savior to come according to his will,” ibid., 280. — His kingdom will last three and a half years, Robert Pullen, CLXXXVI, 979.

PART III. Signs following Antichrist’s kingdom, and the end of the final persecutions.

I. The appearance of the supreme Judge confounds the impious one. — Christ alone will defeat Antichrist, who is exalted by signs and a display of holiness, St. Gregory the Great, LXXV, 1117. — Job saw that at the end of the world Satan, whom Holy Scripture calls Antichrist, rules with such great power [lacuna] that his acts cannot be reproved by a human being, ibid. — “Who will rebuke his face and his way?” For who indeed, except God, by whose help the elect are strengthened so that they may resist? ibid. — What else does this beast do after the Redeemer’s coming but enter into its hiding-place, so that it may remain in its own den? the same author, LXXVI, 428. — To brandish a spear against Leviathan is indeed to prepare eternal death for him by strict punishment, ibid., 730. — Antichrist is to be crushed without a hand, ibid., 710. — According to some, Antichrist is to be consumed on the Mount of Olives, St. Jerome, XXIV, 291. — When they see the abomination of desolation standing in the holy place, this will be a sign of the coming advent; then the return in glory must be understood, St. Hilary, IX, 1054. — He who will fail in the very height of his exaltation through the coming of the true Judge, St. Gregory the Great, LXXVI, 528. — This is the one called Antichrist; but he will falsely claim to be Christ, fight against the true one, and, defeated, flee. He will renew the war repeatedly and be defeated repeatedly, until, in the fourth battle, after all the impious have been overcome, he himself is defeated and captured and at last pays the penalty for his crimes, Lactantius, VI, 797. — The other princes and tyrants also, who have crushed the world, are brought bound with him before the King, who will rebuke and convict them, ibid., 798. — Antichrist will be overthrown by Christ. Christ will thus come again to overthrow Antichrist, so that the world may be freed, the homeland of paradise restored, the world’s freedom made everlasting, and all slavery of the age removed, St. Peter Chrysologus, LII, 613. — And just as night is overthrown when dawn shines, so Antichrist is put to flight when the Savior flashes forth, St. Maximus of Turin, LVII, 225. — When the general disaster has been extinguished, he proceeds to the order of future events: for, after Antichrist has been killed, the eternal kingdom of the Lord will come. For this criminal evil is allowed to run before it on earth, so that the desired kingdom of the Lord may be received more gratefully, Cassiodorus, LXX, 91. — God raises up the Scythians against Antichrist, Rabanus Maurus, CVIII, 1173. — He will be crushed without a hand (Dan. 8:15), whom the Lord will kill with the spirit of his mouth, etc., etc. (2 Thess. 1:8): by the coming of the Judge—not through a battle of angels or a contest of saints—he will be struck with eternal death by the spirit of the mouth alone, Hincmar, CXXV, 280. — Antichrist will fail in his lofty exaltation through the coming of the true Judge, Rev. Garnerius, CXCIII, 193.

[Col. 0277]

II. Jesus Christ, by killing Antichrist with the spirit of his mouth, will put an end to his kingdom and power. — Antichrist will be killed by the spirit of Christ’s mouth, St. Augustine, XXXIII, 908. — “And then that wicked one shall be revealed, whom the Lord Jesus shall kill with the spirit of his mouth,” ibid. — Antichrist, whom the Lord Jesus will kill with the spirit of his mouth, is to be crushed without a hand, St. Gregory the Great, LXXXI, 652. — He will be crushed without a hand, because—not through a battle of angels nor through a contest of saints, but by the coming of the Judge—he will be struck with eternal death by the spirit of the mouth alone, ibid. — We know only this: Jesus will extinguish by his presence that very last persecution which is to come from Antichrist, St. Augustine, XLI, 616. — Without delay, that man, drawing his sword, cut him to pieces; and that Christ fell—the one who ought rather to be called Antichrist—and died; and all who were with him were scattered, Gregory of Tours, LXXI, 557. — The Apostle Paul writes concerning him: “Whom the Lord will kill with the spirit of his mouth and destroy by the brightness of his coming,” Alcuin, CI, 1297. — The splendor of Christ’s coming will be so pre-eminent that, overwhelmed by the brightness of the divine light and befouled all over by excrement discharged from his belly, he will perish through fear, ibid. — The teachers relate, as Pope Gregory says, that the archangel Michael will kill him on the Mount of Olives, in his tent and on his throne, in the place from which the Lord ascended into heaven, ibid., 1298. — If Michael, going before the face of God as he comes to judgment, kills him, it will be not Michael’s own power but God’s power and command, ibid. — The Lord Jesus will indeed kill him with the spirit of his mouth and destroy him by the brightness of his coming, Rabanus Maurus, CVIII, 1171; Blessed Lanfranc, ibid., 343. — Once Antichrist has been killed, the victory of the Word of God will be complete, Rupert, CLXIX, 1497. — The destruction of Antichrist, Peter Lombard, CXCI, 139–148. — Antichrist is to be killed either by Christ or by Michael, Robert Pullen, CLXXXVI, 979.

III. Jesus Christ, by killing Antichrist and uprooting him from the face of the earth, will show how brief his glory and how great his folly were. — A manifest indication of perdition occurs when the result favorably follows the iniquities deliberately pursued, and no opposition hinders what the perverse mind has conceived, St. Gregory the Great, LXLVI [probably LXXVI], 368. — Angel and human being fell because they wished to be like God in power rather than in justice; so too Antichrist’s fall comes through pride, ibid., 486. — Antichrist, raised on high, will appear foolish; in the very height of his exaltation he will fail through the coming of the true Judge, ibid., 528. — Some wish the web spread over all nations to be understood as Antichrist, who is to be consumed on the Mount of Olives, as we also said in the final vision of Daniel, St. Jerome, XXIV, 291. — Forty days for repentance before the judgment are granted to those bewitched and marked [*caracteratis*] by Antichrist, Alcuin, CI, 1298. — We must also believe most firmly that, when Antichrist has been killed, the day of judgment will not come immediately, nor will the Lord come immediately for judgment; rather, as we understand from the book of Daniel, there will be forty days of repentance, etc., ibid. — No one knows how much time afterward will pass when this repentance has been completed, ibid. — It remains within God’s providential ordering, he who will judge the world by fire, at the hour which he fixed before the ages for judgment, ibid. — Teachings of St. Augustine and Jerome concerning the hour of the final judgment after Antichrist’s death, ibid. — St. Augustine, in the Epistle beginning *Nolumus vos ignorare de dormientibus* (“We do not wish you to be ignorant concerning those who sleep”), explains very clearly much concerning the interval between Antichrist’s destruction and the hour of final judgment, ibid. — St. Jerome, in his exposition of the seven trumpets addressed to Evervinus, gives us teachings of great learning concerning the day and hour of the final judgment, ibid.; and so does Blessed Lanfranc, CL, 343.

IV. Antichrist and his followers are destined for final condemnation. — And because, having been given over to the desire of his own heart, he is destined for final condemnation, etc., St. Augustine, XXXVI, 126. — Darkness is Antichrist’s place, into which he will be thrust with the wicked, St. Gregory the Great, LXXV, 1054. — “These are the tabernacles of the wicked man, and this is the place of him who does not know God,” indicating, that is, that he who now exalts himself by not knowing God will then reach his own tabernacles when his own iniquity plunges him into punishments, ibid. — He who, while rejoicing here in the false light of justice, occupied another’s place will at last find his own place: darkness, ibid. — He will rule at the end of the world: “Can you bring forth Lucifer in his time, and make the evening star rise over the children of the earth?” the same author, LXXVI, 520. — “And the devil who deceived them was cast into the lake of fire and sulphur, where are the beast and the false prophet; and they shall be tormented day and night for ages of ages,” St. Augustine, XLI, 679. — He will reproach those tyrants for their crimes, condemn them, and hand them over to punishments deserved, Lactantius, VI, 797. — There is no doubt that the criminal power will perish, since its author is known to deserve condemnation, Cassiodorus, LXX, 91. — After completing his wickedness, Antichrist will at the end receive the recompense of eternal condemnation, Rabanus Maurus, CVIII, 1175. — At the end of the world the devil who deceived the nations is to be cast into the lake of fire and sulphur, where is the beast Antichrist with his wicked members and persecutors, and the false prophets—undoubtedly heretics—and they will be tormented day and night for ages of ages, the same author, CXI, 1147. — The cause of the perdition of Antichrist or of any reprobate person is not from God, Hincmar, CXXV, 465. — It is established that anyone who says, or strives insinuatingly to suggest, that Antichrist or any reprobate has from God the cause of perdition, or perishes by God’s operation, is not Catholic but insane, ibid. — The raising of Antichrist from the dead, as also of other human beings, 282. — If all must rise, then so also must that man Antichrist who comes in his own name, ibid. — If Christ’s passion conferred anything upon the other reprobate, namely the members of Antichrist, it did not deny it to their head either, ibid. — “The sinner will provoke the Lord,” that is, he will stir him to anger by his own unspeakable pride; this is properly understood of Antichrist, St. Bruno of Würzburg, CXLII, 73. — Antichrist provokes the Lord when by his deceit he proclaims himself not only an earthly king but even God of all things; but this will be his ruin, so that, as a false god, he may be punished by fitting flames, ibid. — “Therefore God will destroy you forever; he will pluck you out and remove you from your tent,” ibid., 209. — He who is destroyed forever is consigned to eternal punishments, ibid. — The Jews consenting to Antichrist were his roots; therefore the Psalmist says that the root of this people is to be plucked up with him, ibid. — Neither Antichrist nor his ministers will have a portion in the kingdom of the blessed with the saints of the Lord, ibid. — For those who do Antichrist’s works, God reserves the Father’s pain; condemned together with him, they will suffer the same torments, St. Bruno of Asti, CLXIV, 625. — His works and doctrine will please all the wicked, and whoever believes him will be led to hell together with him, ibid., 626. — The curse of Antichrist: “May his memory perish from the earth,” Rupert, CLXVIII, 1041. — Rebuke and threat against Antichrist and his members, Peter Lombard, CXCI, 501. — The blotting out and derision of Antichrist, ibid.

[Col. 0277]

CXXXIII. INDEX CONCERNING THE RESURRECTION OF THE DEAD, LOGICALLY ARRANGING THE VARIOUS OPINIONS OF THE HOLY FATHERS ON THAT DOGMA.

NOTICE.

In this Index, everything written by the Holy Fathers concerning the resurrection of the dead is reduced to four heads, namely:

I. Errors that have gained currency concerning the resurrection of the dead.  
II. The resurrection of the dead is a dogma of faith.  
III. When and how this resurrection will occur.  
IV. What qualities or changes will occur in bodies, and how these will be unto glory for the righteous but unto confusion for the reprobate.

[INDEX CONCERNING THE RESURRECTION OF THE DEAD.]

I. Errors that have gained currency concerning the resurrection of the dead.

TERTULLIAN. — No philosophy agrees concerning the resurrection of the flesh, [Col. 0278] II, 521.
