(St.-Peter of Flore or Fleur, diocese of Tropea in Lower Calabria), a monastery endowed, and perhaps founded, by a nobleman of Mamistra. Celestine III granted it a privilege in 1196, CCVI, 1183.—Privilege of Innocent III, 1203, CCXV, 151; 1211, CCXVI, 461.

### St. Mary of Floreffe

(Our Lady of Floreffe, near Namur), a monastery of the Premonstratensian order, built in 1121 by Countess Ermesinde, wife of Godfrey, and granted by her to St. Norbert. Honorius II confirmed its possessions in 1128, CLXVI, 1284.—It is mentioned in the Life of St. Norbert, CLXX, 1291.—Privilege of Innocent II, 1138, CLXXIX, 381; of Adrian IV, 1154, CLXXXVIII, 1408.

### Florense, or St. Flour

(St.-Flour), a monastery of the Benedictine order, founded by Stephen, bishop of Clermont, and committed by him to the governance of St. Odilo, abbot of Cluny, in 1034.—It was transformed into an episcopal see in 1317 by Bishop Raymond Vehent, CXLII, 864.

### St. Florentius of Saumur

(St.-Florent-le-Vieil, near Saumur), a monastery of the Benedictine order, which took its beginning from the cell of St. Florentius, disciple of St. Martin. After Florentius’s death, he withdrew to Mont Glonne and lived a solitary life in the fourth century. Later Abbot Frotbert and Louis the Pious built a monastery there in 824, CIV, 1132.—Privilege of John XVIII, confirming its possessions and rights, 1004, CXXXIX, 1477.—Diploma of Baldwin, archbishop of Dol, 1109, CLXVI, 1211.—Letter of Innocent III to the abbot, 1207, CCXV, 1121.—Concerning the controversy of these canons with the monks of St. Julian of Tours, 1210, CCXVI, 246, 247, 866.

### Holy Trinity of Florence

(The Holy Trinity of Florence), a monastery of the Benedictine order. At the request of Abbot Jerome, Pope Lucius III granted it a privilege in 1183, CCI, 1234.—Letter of Innocent III to the abbot concerning a certain affair of the bishop of Pistoia, 1214, CCXVII, 225.

### St. Salvius of Florence

(St.-Salvius of Florence), a monastery of the Vallombrosan order, built in the time of Urban II.—Privilege of Alexander III, 1163, CC, 229; of Urban III, 1187, CCII, 1476; privilege of Clement III, 1189, CCIV, 1416.

### St. Mary of Florence

(St. Mary of Florence), a monastery of the Benedictine order. St. Peter Damian wrote in the eleventh century to one of its monks, named Theuzon, CXLIV, 422.—Writings of this Theuzon, CXLIII, 845.—Privilege of Alexander II, 1070, CXLVI, 1358, 1367.—Privilege of Paschal II, 1107, CLXIII, 227, 265; of Alexander III, 1176, CC, 1069; of Clement III, 1188, CCIV, 1297.

### St. Ambrose of Florence

(St. Ambrose of Florence), a nunnery outside the city, in the place called *Pulchito*, built by Bishop Godfrey shortly before 1141; in that year Innocent II honored it with a privilege, CLXXIX, 543.

### St. Lawrence-in-Bifurco of Florence

(St. Lawrence of Florence), a monastery of the Augustinian order, whose rights and possessions Pope Paschal II confirmed in 1114, CLXIII, 349.—Privilege of Innocent II, 1142, CLXXIX, 625, 654; of Alexander III, 1084; of Clement III, 1188, CCIV, 1371.—Privilege of Celestine III, 1191, CCVI, 876.

### St. John the Baptist of Florence

(Convent of St. John the Baptist), a monastery of the Augustinian order, to which Bishop Speciosus made many gifts; his charter, 724, LXXXVII, 1402.—Privilege of Pope Benedict IX to Provost Roland, 1036, CXLI, 1345.—Letter of Gregory VI to the same community, CXLII, 575; of Clement III, 1188, CCIV, 1337.

### St. Saviour of Florence

(St. Saviour of Florence), a monastery of the Benedictine order, built in the suburb of Florence before 1144, when Celestine II confirmed it by privilege, CLXXIX, 801.

### St. Minias of Florence

A monastery of the Benedictine order, whose rights and possessions Pope Benedict IX received under his protection in 1044, CXLI, 1367.—St. John Gualbert embraced monastic life there before fleeing to the hermitage of Vallombrosa, 1029, CXLVI, 719.—Privilege of Pope Alexander II, 1063, ibid., 1303.—Privilege of Lucius III, 1145, CCI, 1345.

### St. Stephen of the Bridge, Florence

(St. Stephen of the Bridge at Florence), a monastery whose prior Innocent III appointed against the bishop of Lucca, CCXV, 1282.

### St. Felicity of Florence

(Nuns of St. Felicity at Florence), a nunnery honored with privileges by Pope Nicholas II in 1060, CXLIII, 1328.

### St. Peter Major of Florence

(St. Peter Major, Florence), a nunnery built in the suburb and endowed with property by the noblewoman Gisla; Alexander II confirmed it by privilege in 1067, CXLVI, 1330.—Privilege of Eugenius III, 1151, CLXXX, 1471; of Celestine III, 1192, CCVI, 923.

### Sts. Peter and Benedict of Fleury

(Fleury-sur-Loire), a celebrated monastery in the district of Orléans, founded in 667 by Abbot Leodebod and endowed by John of Fleury, with the assistance of King Clovis II and Queen Bathildis, LXXXVIII, 1186.—Diplomas of Louis the Pious, 817, CIV, 1078, 1080, 1264.—On its foundation, CXXIV, 901.—The monk Adrevald flourished in 878, ibid., 899.—Privilege of Gregory IV, CXXIX, 995; of Leo VII, 938, CXXXI, 1075; St. Abbo was elected abbot in 1004, CXXXIX, 375.—Annals of Fleury, ibid., 581; the monk Aimoin flourished in 1008, ibid., 617; Abbot Gauzlin, 1027, CXLI, 759.—Privilege of Pope Alexander II, 1072, CXLVI, 1375.—Privilege of William the Conqueror, 1067, CXLIX, 1371.—The monk Ralph Tortarius flourished in 1115, CLX, 1171; the monk Hugh of St. Mary in 1119, CLXIII, [Col. 1065] 791.—Diploma of Ralph, archbishop of Rheims, granting this monastery the altar of Sorbon (Sorbon, near Rethel, Ardennes), 1119, ibid., 1427.—Privilege of Eugenius III, 1146, CLXXX, 1129; of Alexander III, 1163, CC, 257, 258.—Decree of Innocent III concerning the recovery of alienated property, 1209, CCXVI, 56.—Privilege of the same pope, ibid., 57, 58.

### St. Benedict of Florennes

(St.-Benoît of Florennes, diocese of Liège), a monastery of the Benedictine order, built by Blessed Gerard, bishop of Cambrai.—Diploma of Emperor St. Henry, 1012, CXL, 298.—Privilege of St. Leo IX, 1054, CXLIII, 742.

### St. Mary of Flotin

(Our Lady of Flotin, Gâtinais), a monastery of the Augustinian order, built by William, archbishop of Sens, shortly before 1180, in which year Alexander III confirmed it by privilege, CC, 1299.—Charter of the same William, the founder, ibid.

### St. Mary of Fiume

(St. Mary of Fiume, diocese of Forlì, Papal States), a monastery of the Benedictine order.—Privilege of Pope Celestine III, 1192, CCVI, 943.—Donations of the nobleman John of Ceccano, confirmed by Innocent III in 1208, CCXV, 1450.

### St. James of Foggia

(St. James of Foggia, Capitanata, Naples), a monastery of the Benedictine order, dependent upon the abbey of St. Mary of Pulsano, mentioned in a privilege of Alexander III, 1174, CC, 1097.

### St. Nicholas of Foggia

(St. Nicholas of Foggia), of the same order; it receives the same mention as the preceding entry.

### Folkestone

(Folkestone, county of Kent, England), a monastery originally of nuns, founded from 650 onward, later rebuilt by Nigel de Muneville, and apparently handed over to monks, to whom Innocent III granted a privilege in 1204, CCXV, 369.

### St. Mary of Fontallume

(St. Mary of Fontallume, diocese of Ascoli, March of Ancona), a nunnery of the Cistercian order, built shortly before 1212, in which year Innocent III confirmed it by privilege, CCXVI, 599.

### Fontaines-les-Blanches

(Fontaines-les-Blanches, diocese of Tours), a monastery of the Cistercian order, founded in 1132 between Blois and Tours by Renaud of Château-Renaud, lord of the place. It seems to be the subject of a question in a letter of Adrian IV to the archbishop of Tours, 1154, CLXXXVIII, 1421.

### St. Saviour of Fontana Taone

(St. Saviour of Fontana Taone, Tuscany), a monastery of the Benedictine order, whose possessions and privileges Emperor St. Henry II confirmed in 1014, CXL, 306. It adopted the Rule of St. John Gualbert about 1074, CXLVI, 806.—Privilege of Celestine III, confirming a donation made by the nobleman Avianus, 1195, CCVI, 1103.—Charter of the same Avianus attached to the preceding privilege, ibid.

### St. Mary of Fontenelles

(Our Lady of Fontenelles, diocese of Luçon), a monastery of the Augustinian order, to which St. Bathildis granted much in 684. It was later restored, or rather rebuilt, by William de Mauléon and his wife Beatrice in 1210, LXXXVIII, 870.

### Sts. Peter and Paul of Fontenelles

(Fontenelles-sur-Seine), a monastery of the Benedictine order, also called St. Wandrille after its founder, situated in Normandy on the Seine, on an island near Caudebec. King Theuderic granted a diploma to its abbot Candidus in 673, LXXXVII, 1319; diploma of Childebert III, 704, LXXXVIII, 1101; of Chilperic II, ibid., 1122; of Louis the Pious, 815, CIV, 1025; St. Ansegisus became abbot and died in 833, CV, 744.—Diploma of William the Conqueror, CXLIX, 1370.—St. Wandrille, founder of that monastery, CLVIII, 1195.—Letter of Pope Innocent II, 1131, CLXXIX, 117.—On the foundation of this monastery, CCII, 1314.

### St. Marien of Fontaines

(St.-Marien of Fontaines, near Auxerre), a monastery in the diocese of Auxerre, founded by St. Germanus, where St. Marien tended sheep in 570, CXXXVIII, 226, 233, 234.—Charter of Alan, bishop of Auxerre, 1163, CCI, 1387.—Letter of Innocent III to the abbot, 1205, CCXV, 679.

### St. Mary of Fontaines

(Fontaines-en-Vosges), a monastery built by St. Columbanus in the Vosges, later converted into a priory, 597, LXXXVII, 1019, 1033 note.

### St. Mary of Fontaines

(Notre-Dame des Fontaines, diocese of Meaux), a nunnery whose rights and possessions Innocent II confirmed by privilege in 1133, CLXXI, 170.

### Fontaines [printed: Ontanis]

(Fontaines-les-Dijon, birthplace of St. Bernard), a Cistercian priory called the Feuillants, founded about 1614 in the very house in which the holy doctor had been born. King Louis XIII became its protector, CLXXXV, 1637.—Sold in 1791 and [Col. 1066] demolished; more recently, in 1841, its church was restored by the distinguished Renault, vicar-general of Dijon, 1640.—Diploma of Louis XIII, 1643.—Likewise that of Queen Anne, wife of the same king, 1638, ibid., 1661.—Other letters and privileges of the same persons, 1653.—Privilege of Innocent X, attaching indulgences to this place, 1655.

### Fontenay-les-Beauvais

(Fontenay-les-Beauvais), a monastery of the Benedictine order in the district of Beauvais, mentioned in the testament of Abbot Ansegisus, 833, CV, 745.

### St. Mary of Fontenay

(Our Lady of Fontenay, Côte-d’Or), a monastery of the Cistercian order, built in 1119 by Renaud, lord of Montbard; his charter, CLXXXV, 1461.—Charter of Verricus of Châtillon, ibid., 1462.—Diploma of Stephen, bishop of Autun, 1136, ibid., 1463.—Charter of Theobald of Salives, ibid., 1464.—Donations of Andrew of Montbard, ibid., 1466, 1567.—Of Bernard of Montbard, ibid., 1468.—Of Guy, canon, ibid., 1469.—Of Count Odo of Issoudun, ibid., 1471.—Donation of Countess Matilda of Grignon, ibid.—Count Oliver of Grignon confirms his father’s gifts, ibid., 1472.—Gifts of various persons, ibid., 1473. Donation of John of Montbard, ibid., 1474.—Of Blanche, widow of Hervé of Sombernon, ibid., 1475.—Her donation was confirmed by William, abbot of Flavigny, ibid.

### Fontenay

(Fontenay, diocese of Bayeux), a monastery of the Benedictine order, built by St. Evremond, abbot, and mentioned in the testament of St. Ansegisus, 833, CV, 744.—On this monastery, CCII, 1319.—Letter of Innocent III, 1203, CCXV, 256.

### Fonte Avellana

See **Avellanense**.

### Fontaine-André

(Fontaine-André, near Neuchâtel, Switzerland), a monastery of the Premonstratensian order, founded by the count of Neuchâtel in 1144. Blessed Amadeus, bishop of Lausanne, confirmed its possessions, CLXXXVIII, 1290.

### St. Mary of Fontcaude

(Our Lady of Fontcaude, Hérault), a monastery of the Premonstratensian order, built shortly before 1164, in which year Alexander III annexed it to the monastery of Valle-Crosa, CC, 308, 394.—Abbot Bernard flourished in 1190, CCIV, 793.

### Fontevraud

(Fontevraud, between Tours and Poitiers), a celebrated monastery founded in 1107 by Blessed Robert of Arbrissel. Men and women of every condition served God there separately, under the rule of an abbess, according to the Rule of this holy founder, CLXII, 1048.—Diploma of St. Robert, commending his monastery of Fontevraud to Peter, bishop of Poitiers, ibid., 1085.—Charter of foundation by the same Robert, ibid., 1077.—Charter of confirmation by Peter, bishop of Poitiers, 1106, ibid., 1089, 1091.—Various donations from various persons to the aforesaid monastery, ibid., 1097 and following.—Privilege of Paschal II, 1106, CLXIII, 164, 296, 419.—Decree of Gelasius II, ibid., 504.—Of Pope Calixtus II, 1119, ibid., 1121.—Privilege of Honorius II, 1126, CLXVI, 1268.—Of Innocent II, 1131, CLXXIX, 72, 116, 118, 304, 320, 634, 635.—Privilege of Lucius II, 1144, ibid., 864, 924.—Decree of Eugenius III concerning the gift of a certain church by the abbot of Conques, 1145, CLXXX, 1036.—Privilege of the same pope, ibid., 1037.—Decree concerning the election of Matilda, the second abbess, ibid., 1396, 1400, 1413.—Privilege of Alexander III, 1163, CC, 197, 334, 518.

### St. Mary of Fontfroide

(Our Lady of Fontfroide, former diocese of Narbonne, Aude), a monastery of the Cistercian order, originating from the monastery of Grandselve and built by Viscount Aimeric in 1097.—Letters of Innocent III against the archbishop of Narbonne, 1203, CCXV, 355, 358, 683, 1024, 1080.—Letter of the same pope against the men of Montpellier, 1212, CCXVI, 811.

### Fontaine-Géhard

(Fontaine-Géhard, diocese of Le Mans), a priory of the Benedictine order dependent on Marmoutier.—Privilege by which Innocent III confirmed that monastery, 1211, CCXVI, 449.

### St. Mary of Fontmorigny

(Our Lady of Fontmorigny, diocese of Bourges), a monastery of the Cistercian order, built in 1148.—Mentioned by Herbert de Turribus, CLXXXV, 1349.—On the foundation of this monastery, CCII, 1312.—Donation of Henry II, king of England, about 1170, CCVII, 1162.

### St. Mary of Fontevivo

(St. Mary of Fontevivo, diocese of Parma), a monastery of the Augustinian order, founded by Lanfranc, bishop of Parma, shortly before 1144, in which year Pope Lucius II honored it with a privilege, CLXXIX, 900.

### Footel

See **Malanoa**.

### Forbach

(Forbach, in the county of Leiningen, Bavaria), a monastery of the Benedictine order, built by Counts Ecbert and Udalric before 1139, when Innocent II confirmed its property and privileges, CLXXIX, 415.

[Col. 1067]

### Fourmies

(Fourmies, near Avesnes, Nord), a monastery of the Benedictine order, built in 1115 by Baldwin, or Baldric, bishop of Noyon and Tournai, CLXVI, 891.

### Forojuliense

See **Sextense**, **Saltense**, **Vallis Civitatis**.

### St. Rufillus of Forlimpopoli

(St.-Ruffile of Forlimpopoli, Papal States), a monastery of the Benedictine order, to which privileges were granted by Benedict VII, 980, CXXXVII, 336; and Alexander III, 1180, CC, 1308.

### St. Gervasius of Fos

(St.-Gervais of Fos, former diocese of Arles, Bouches-du-Rhône), an ancient monastery wholly ruined by corrupt morals.—Judgment of Innocent III concerning its reform, 1198, CCXIV, 440.

### Sts. Hippolytus and Cassian of Fosciano

(St.-Hippolytus of Fosciano, duchy of Benevento), a Benedictine monastery whose possessions and privileges Alexander III confirmed in 1166, CC, 502.

### Fossanova

(Fossanova, near Piperno, Papal States), a monastery whose agreement with the people of Piperno Innocent III confirmed in 1206, CCXV, 976, 982.—A certain possession confirmed by the same pope, ibid., 1053, 1306.—Privilege of the same pope, 1365, 1435; 1211, CCXVI, 401.

### St. Maurus of Fossés

(Abbey of Fossés-Saint-Maur, near Charenton, diocese of Paris), a celebrated monastery of the Benedictine order, founded in 640 by King Clovis II and St. Blidegisil under the invocation of St. Mary and the holy Apostles Peter and Paul, LXXXVII, 685. Its name was changed to St. Maurus when it received the relics of that holy martyr.—Diploma of Chilperic II, 717, LXXXIII, 1126.—Charter of foundation by Blidegisil, 640, ibid., 1157.—Diplomas of Louis the Pious, 816, CIV, 1044, 1055.—Donations of Burchard and Renaud, confirmed by King Robert, 998, CXLI, 947.—The monk Odo flourished there in 1057, CXLIII, 846.—Charter of Stephen, bishop of Paris, 1134, CLXXIII, 1424.—Privilege of Innocent II, 1136, CLXXIX, 268.—Charter of Abbot Roger, 1165, ibid., 908.—Privilege of Innocent III, 1207, CCXV, 1330.

### Sts. Gervasius and Protasius of Fossés

(Sts. Gervasius and Protasius of Fossés, diocese of Arles), a monastery of the Benedictine order, founded before 923, when Manasses, bishop of Arles, ceded it to Drogo, bishop of Marseille; it later passed to Cluny.—Privilege of Pope Innocent II, 1130, CLXXIX, 62.

### St. Fursey of La Fosse

(La Fosse in Hainaut), a monastery of the Benedictine order, founded in the diocese of Cambrai about 455 by Sts. Foillan and Ultan, brothers of St. Fursey the abbot, who were natives of Ireland. St. Fursey was buried there, XCV, 148.

### Pont-Rompu

(Convent of Pont-Rompu, diocese of Lincoln, England), a monastery whose abbot Innocent III addressed in 1195, CCVI, 1250.

### Franquevaux

(Franquevaux, diocese of Nîmes), a monastery of the Cistercian order, originating from Morimond and built in 1143 by Pons William and the counts of St.-Gilles.—Privilege of Innocent III, 1198, CCXIV, 501.

### St. Mary Magdalene of Frankenthal

(St. Mary Magdalene of Frankenthal, diocese of Worms), a monastery of the Augustinian order, founded in 1133 by Buggo, bishop of Worms.—Privilege of Pope Innocent II in the same year, CLXXIX, 198.

### St. Antoninus of Frédelas

(St. Antoninus of Frédelay or Frédelas, former diocese of Pamiers), a monastery of the Benedictine order, built before 961 and granted by Roger, count of Foix, to Blessed Hugh, abbot of Cluny, about 1094, in order that he might restore its morals and discipline, CLIX, 940.

### St. Frideswide

(St. Frideswide’s at Oxford, England), a nunnery of the Benedictine order, founded about 750 by Didanus, count of Oxford. Innocent III wrote to its superior in 1208, CCXV, 1504.

**OF ST. FREMER** (Saint-Ferme, former diocese of Bazas), a monastery of the Order of St. Benedict, subject to the abbey of St. Florent. — Letter of Pope Innocent II to the Archbishop of Auch concerning the restoration of this monastery to its lawful possessors, 1143, CLXXIX, 631. — Privilege of Eugenius III, 1146, CLXXX, 1130.

**OF ST. BLAISE OF FRIEDLAND** (Saint-Blaise de Friedland, near Northeim, duchy of Brunswick), a monastery of the Order of St. Benedict, built by Otto the Great, duke of Saxony, in 1050; having been destroyed by fire, it was rebuilt by Count Sigfrid of Bunmeneburg in 1128. — Privilege of Lucius II, 1144, CLXXIX, 931. — Of Eugenius III, CLXXX, 1142.

**OF ST. PETER OF FRITZLAR** (Fritzlar in Hesse), a monastery of the Order of St. Benedict, built by St. Boniface in [Col. 1068] the diocese of Mainz about 748, LXXXIX, 647. — Wigbert was appointed first abbot, CXIX, 684.

**OF ST. FRIGDIANUS OF LUCCA** (Saint-Frigdien of Lucca), a monastery of the Order of St. Augustine, apparently founded by Faulo; its foundation was confirmed by Felix, bishop of Lucca, in 685, LXXXVII, 1347. — Charter of Bishop Walprand, 1405. — Privilege of Alexander II, 1068, CXLVI, 1346. — Of Paschal II, 1104, CLXIII, 131, 192, 193, 236, 253, 392. — The same pope confirms the excommunication pronounced by the bishop against the priest Ubertus, ibid., 394, 416, 430. — Letter of Gelasius II, 1118, ibid., 487; privilege of the same pope, 1118, ibid., 499, 501. — Letter of Pope Calixtus II, ibid., 1096, 1146, 1303, 1312. — Privilege, 1321; of Honorius II, 1127, CLXVI, 1270, 1279, 1310. — Privileges of Innocent II, 1132, CLXXIX, 136, 160, 220, 221, 303, 335, 509, 639, 646, 657. — Privileges of Eugenius III, 1145, CLXXX, 1020, 1205, 1256, 1257, 1404, 1427. — Of Anastasius IV, 1153, CLXXXVIII, 1025. — Letter of Alexander III, 1171, CC, 716, 1048. — Of Lucius III, 1181, CCI, 1082. — Letter of Innocent III concerning the election of a bishop, 1202, CCXIV, 1150, 1166, 1173. — 1203, CCXV, 57, 127, 304.

**HOSPITAL OF THE HOLY SPIRIT OF FREISACH** (Freysach, archdiocese of Salzburg, Lower Carinthia), to which Innocent III confirmed tithes, 1213, CCXVI, 645.

**OF ST. STEPHEN OF FREISING** (Saint-Étienne de Freising, Bavaria), a monastery of the Order of St. Benedict, founded by Otto, bishop of Freising, and confirmed by privilege of Eugenius III, 1145, CLXXX, 1066.

**OF FRITZLAR.** See above, **OF FRITZLAR**.

**OF ST. BENIGNUS OF FRUCTUARIA** (Saint-Bénigne du Fruitier, former diocese of Ivrea in Piedmont), a monastery of the Order of St. Benedict, founded by Blessed William, abbot, between the rivers Orco and Malone in subalpine Gaul and in the diocese of Ivrea; he governed it for some time, 1024, CXLI, 838. — Privilege of Lambert, bishop of Langres, 841. — Privilege of St. William for the same monastery, CXLI, 871. — Diploma of King Robert, 1023, ibid., 965. — Privileges of Alexander II, 1063, CXLVI, 1288, 1356. — Of Paschal II, 1110, CLXIII, 268. — Of Anastasius IV, 1154, CLXXXVIII, 1051.

**OF ST. MARY OF COLD MOUNT** (Notre-Dame de Froimont, diocese of Beauvais, Oise), a monastery of the Cistercian Order, built in 1134 and endowed in 1190 and 1218 by the noblemen of Bulles and by the count and countess of Clermont. The monk Helinandus brought distinction to this monastery in 1212, CCXII, 477.

**OF FRUTINO.** See **ST. NICHOLAS**.

**OF ST. SAVIOUR OF FULDA** (Saint-Sauveur de Fulda, Hesse-Cassel), a most celebrated monastery of the Order of St. Benedict, built in the Buchonia forest in 747 by St. Boniface, archbishop of Mainz, LXXI, 238, note; LXXXIX, 1257; CVII, 9, 80. — Diploma of King Pippin, 762, XCVI, 1536, 1563. — Donations of Charlemagne, 774, XCVII, 1051, 1052, 1057, 1063, 1076. — Likewise, diplomas of Louis the Pious, 816, CIV, 1056, 1110. — St. Sturm was the first abbot, and St. Eigil the fourth, CV, 422. — The celebrated school of Fulda, ibid., 423. — Diploma of Benedict III, 761, ibid. — Of Pope Nicholas I, CXIX, 770. — Of John VIII, CXXVI, 657; of Stephen V, CXXIX, 813. — Of Gregory IV, ibid., 991. — Of Leo IV, ibid., 999. — Of Benedict III, ibid., 1010. — Of Nicholas I, ibid., 1011. — Of Benedict IV, CXXXI, 43. — Of John, 917, CXXXII, 799. — Of Leo VII, 936, ibid., 1066. — Of Marinus II, CXXXIII, 865. — Of Agapetus II, ibid., 889, 897. — Of John XII, ibid., 1026. — Of John XIII, CXXXV, 979. — Of John XV, CXXXVII, 849. — Of Gregory V, ibid., 912. — Of Sylvester II, 999, CXXXIX, 272. — Of Benedict VIII, ibid., 1033. — Charter of St. Henry II, emperor, 1012, CXL, 294, 295, 296, 350, 354, 381. — Privilege of John XIX, 1031, CXLI, 1147. — Of Clement II, CXLII, 577, 579. — Of St. Leo IX, CXLIII, 609. — Of Victor II, 1057, ibid., 824. — Of Pope Alexander II, CXLVI, 1301, 1409. — Privilege of Calixtus II, 1122, CLXIII, 1244. — Of Innocent II, 1131, CLXXIX, 85, 187, 327. — Abbot Sturmius is canonized, 450. — Privilege of the same pope, ibid., 602. — Letters of Eugenius III to the people of Fulda, CLXXX, 1334, 1442. — Privilege of Pope Anastasius IV, 1154, CLXXXVIII, 1177. — Of Adrian IV, 1150, ibid., 1591.

**OF ST. PATERNIANUS OF FOLIGNO** (Saint-Paternien of Foligno in Umbria, Papal States), a monastery to which Innocent III subjected the church of St. Christina, 1206, CCXV, 1038.

**OF ST. MARY OF FEUILLANTS** (Notre-Dame-des-Feuillants, diocese of Rieux, Haute-Garonne), a monastery of the Cistercian Order, descended from Morimond, in 1145; it later became celebrated because of the reform introduced by Abbot Jean de la Barrière, confirmed by Pope Sixtus V in 1586. This monastery is mentioned, CLXXXV, 1635. — Privilege of Urban III, 1187, CCII, 1546.

**OF FEUILLANTS** (Abbey of Feuillants, established in the March of Treviso), a monastery of the Cistercian Order, commended by Pope Lucius III to the nobles of that province, 1185, CCI, 1318.

**OF FULRAD’S VILLERS** (Villers, Meurthe), a monastery founded in Lorraine on his own hereditary estate by Fulrad, abbot of St. Denis, and confirmed by diploma of Charlemagne, 774, CXCVII, 937.

**OF FUNDI** (Fondi, Italy), a monastery of the Order of St. Benedict, founded in Samnium (Papal States) by the blessed Abbot Honoratus. It is mentioned in the *Dialogues* of St. Gregory the Great, sixth century, LXXVII, 153.

**OF ST. WALBURGA OF FURNES** (Furnes, the Netherlands), a monastery of the Order of St. Benedict, founded or notably enlarged by Gertrude, countess of Flanders, in 1105. Privilege of Pope Paschal II, CLXIII, 195. — Privilege of Calixtus II, 1121, ibid., 1204.

**OF ST. NICHOLAS OF FURNES** (Saint-Nicolas of Furnes in Flanders), a nunnery to which Gertrude, countess of Maurienne, made a donation. — Privilege of Urban III confirming this gift, 1187, CCII, 1468.

**OF FURNESS** (Furness in Lancashire, England), a monastery built about 1127, to which Innocent III entrusted a matrimonial case in 1203, CCXV, 192.

**OF ST. FURSEY**, a monastery of the Order of St. Benedict among the East Angles, founded about 670 by St. Furseus, an Irish abbot, and King Sigebert, XCV, 145.

**OF ST. FURSEY.** See **OF FOSSES**.

**OF ST. FUSCIANUS IN THE WOOD** (Saint-Fuscien-aux-Bois, Somme), a monastery of the Order of St. Benedict, not far from Amiens, founded by Count Ingelramnus of Montdidier in 1105. Charter of foundation by Godfrey, bishop of Amiens, CLXII, 739.

**OF FOIGNY** (Foigny, Aisne), a monastery of the Cistercian Order from Clairvaux, founded in 1121 by Bartholomew, bishop of Laon; St. Bernard himself supplied it with monks and placed Raynald over it as abbot, CLVI, 1000. — Privilege of Innocent II, 1131, CLXXIX, 113. — Of Eugenius III, 1147, CLXXX, 1204. — Of Alexander III, 1165, CC, 338. — Of Innocent III, 1200, CCXVII, 62, 90, 111.

**OF STS. GERVASIUS AND PROTASIUS OF GEVAUDAN** (Saint-Gervais-et-Protais of Javoux, diocese of Auch), a monastery of the Order of St. Benedict, founded in 1003 by Stephen, viscount of Gévaudan, and his wife Angelmoda, CXXXIX, 284. — It was subject to the monastery of Cluny, ibid.

**OF ST. GABRIEL.** See **OF CREMONA**.

**OF CÁDIZ** (Cadiz), a monastery founded on the Spanish island of Cádiz by St. Fructuosus, 865, LXXXVII, 1089.

**OF ST. MARY OF GENNES** (Notre-Dame de Gennes-les-Prés, Maine), a monastery of the obedience of Fontevraud, founded in 1106 by Count Fulk and Blessed Father Robert of Arbrissel, CLXII, 1087, 1097.

**OF GALDO**, a monastery whose location is uncertain. Letter of Innocent III permitting these monks to dwell elsewhere because of the injuries inflicted by their neighbours, 1198, CCXIV, 56.

**OF ST. HILARIUS, OR ELLARIUS, OF GALÉATE** (Saint-Hilaire de Galéate, diocese of Populonia in Tuscany), a monastery of the Order of St. Benedict, built by St. Hilary before 754, when Pope Stephen was kindly received there by Abbot Anscausus. Later, in the fifteenth century, it passed to the Camaldolese, CVI, 732. — Letter of Innocent III, 1207, CCXV, 1267.

**OF ST. GALL AT ARBON** (Saint-Gall-sur-Arbonne, Switzerland), a distinguished monastery of the Order of St. Benedict, founded or greatly enlarged among the Swiss by St. Gall, an Irishman by birth, in 646, LXXXVII, 9. — Donation of Aloin, 680, LXXXVIII, 1204. — Charter of Duke Godfrey, ibid., 1253. — Likewise, of Erfroin, ibid., 1268. — Diploma of Louis the Pious, 817, CIV, 1075, 1076, 1077, 1108, 1174. — Of Louis the German, 833, ibid., 1242. — The monk Grimald flourished in 872, CXXI, 795. — Ratpertus, 890, CXXVI, 1055. — Privilege of Pope Sergius III, CXXXI, 971. — The monk Notker, 911, ibid., 994. — Various donations, ibid., 1163. — Privilege of John X, CXXXII, 803. — Of Innocent II, 1139, CLXXIX, 431.

**OF ST. QUENTIN OF GAILLAC** (Saint-Quentin of Gaillac, diocese of Albi), a monastery of the Order of St. Benedict, built before 755, when Pippin, king of the Franks, annexed it to the monastery of Figeac, CXLI, 23. — Perhaps it is the same monastery rebuilt by Raymond Pons, count of Toulouse, in 972.

**OF GALLOMONT, OR MOUNT GALON AND THE VALE OF THE MOUNT OF ST. MARY** (Notre-Dame de Valmont, [Col. 1070] diocese of Rouen), a monastery of the Order of St. Benedict, founded in 1169 by Nicholas de Stoteville. Privilege of Lucius III, 1181, CCI, 1071. — Charter of foundation, ibid.

**OF ST. BARNABAS OF GAMUGNO** (Saint-Barnabé of Gamugno, Tuscany), a monastery of the Camaldolese Order, to whose monks Blessed Peter Damian sent admonitions in the eleventh century, CXXXIX, 422, 432, 434.

**OF GAMONDI** (Gamondi, diocese of Faenza), a monastery whose liberty Celestine III preserved against the wishes of the bishop, who wished to subject it to Acerenza, 1195, CCVI, 1064.

**OF ST. BLANDINUS OF GHENT** (Saint-Blandin of Ghent), a monastery perhaps identical with that of St. Bavo, whose abbot Eginhard was for a time, 830, CIV, 605, 606.

**OF ST. BAVO OF GHENT** (Saint-Bavon of Ghent), a monastery of the Order of St. Benedict, founded by St. Amand in the seventh century. The relics of Saints Marcellinus and Peter were translated there in 826, as Eginhard, abbot of this monastery and eyewitness, relates, CIV, 583. — Diploma of Louis the Pious, 818, CIV, 1092. — Privilege of St. Henry II, emperor, 1003, CXL, 252. — Othelbodus, its thirty-sixth abbot, 1040, CXLI, 1338. — Which saints and what possessions belonged to it, ibid. — Privilege of Adrian IV, 1156, CXXXVIII, 1487.

**OF ST. PETER OF GHENT** (Saint-Pierre of Ghent), a monastery of the Order of St. Benedict, built by St. Amand, whose first abbot was St. Florebertus. St. Livinus, bishop, lodged there in 653, LXXXVII, 338. — See **OF BLANDINUS**. — Privilege of Eugenius III, 1146, CLXXX, 1087. — Letter of Alexander III concerning a certain settlement and other churches of the same place, 1176, CC, 1064. — Privilege of Urban III, 1186, CCII, 1459.

**OF ST. MARY OF GANSWICK** (Notre-Dame de Ganswick, diocese of Mechelen), a monastery of the Order of St. Augustine, to whose abbot Innocent III wrote in 1207, CCXV, 1317.

**NUNNERY OF GANDERSHEIM**, in Saxony, founded by Count Otto in 948 and entrusted to the venerable Abbess Windilgard. According to the author of the *Life of St. Godehard*, it was founded in 852 by Liudolf, duke of Saxony, and his wife Oda; its first abbess was Hathumoda, their own daughter, CXLI, 1177. — Privilege of Pope Agapetus II, CXXXIII, 496. — Of John XIII, 968, CXXXV, 959. — The virgin and nun Hrotsvitha flourished in 999, CXXXVII, 939. — Diploma of Emperor Otto II, by which his niece Gerberga was to be foundress and abbess, ibid., 957. — Poem on the beginnings of this monastery, ibid., 1135. — Privileges of Innocent III, 1205, CCXV, 598, 603, 919, 1398.

**OF ST. GANGOLF OF KRAUFTHAL, OR CLAUSTRIACUM** (Saint-Gangolfe of Kraufthal, Bas-Rhin), a nunnery founded by Folmar the Younger, count of Metz. Innocent II wrote concerning its reform to the abbot of St. George in the Black Forest, 1138, CLXXIX, 347.

**OF ST. MARY OF MOUNT GARDA** (Notre-Dame du Mont-la-Garde, Venetian States), a monastery whose goods and rights Innocent III confirmed by privilege in 1206, CCXV, 898.

**OF ST. MARY OF GARIBERTO** (Notre-Dame of Gariberto, diocese of Piacenza), a monastery of the Order of St. Augustine, taken under his protection by Adrian IV in 1158, CLXXXVIII, 1552.

**OF GARST, OR GARSTEN** (Garst or Garsten, diocese of Passau, Bavaria), a monastery of the Order of St. Augustine, built by the noblemen Ottokar of Styria and Conrad shortly before 1179, when Alexander III granted it a privilege, CC, 1221. — Lucius III, 1185, CCI, 1371. — Letter of Celestine III in favour of this monastery, 1197, CCVI, 1188, 1221.

**OF THE HOLY SEPULCHRE OF GAVARET** (Gavaret, Tarn), a monastery of the Order of St. Benedict, built in the diocese of Auch about 1088 by Peter, viscount, and Girard, abbot of La Sauve-Majeure, CXLVI, 1010.

**OF ST. GAUDENTIUS AT THE FOOT OF THE ALPS** (Saint-Gaudence at the foot of the Alps), a monastery which Anastasius IV asserted by privilege to belong to the Church of Fiesole in Tuscany, 1133, CLXXXVIII, 1016.

**OF ST. GAUGERICUS** (Saint-Géry, near Cambrai), a monastery on a hill near Cambrai, built by St. Gaugericus, bishop, in 600, CV, 746; CXLIX, 124.

**OF GAUGIAC**, a nunnery. See **EPISCOPI-VILLAE**.

**OF STS. GAVINUS AND LUXORIUS**, a nunnery whose abbesses were Cyrica and Gavinia, situated at Torres in Sardinia. It is mentioned by St. Gregory the Great, LXXVII, 933.

**OF ST. MARY OF GEDEWERDE** (Sainte-Marie de Gedewerde, England), a monastery of the Order of St. Augustine, founded by Herbert, bishop of Glasgow, before 1209; Innocent III confirmed it by privilege in 1209, CCXVI, 31.

**OF GILLINGHEIM** (Gillingheim in Thuringia), a monastery of the Order of St. Benedict, whose abbot Arnold succeeded St. Godehard at the monastery of Hersfeld and died in 1031, CXLI, 1171, 1172, note.

**OF ST. SAVIOUR OF GELLONE** (Saint-Sauveur de Gellone, diocese of Lodève, later surnamed Saint-Guilhem-du-Désert), founded by Abbot William, to which Louis the Pious granted a privilege in 807, CIV, 982. — Privileges of Alexander II, 1066, CLXI, 1311, 1314, 1341. — Of Eugenius III, 1146, CLXXX, 1154. — Letter of Innocent III concerning an accusation against the abbot, 1202, CCXIV, 1053.

**OF ST. SAVIOUR AND ST. PETER OF GEMBLOUX** (Saint-Sauveur or Saint-Pierre of Gembloux, Belgium), a most celebrated monastery of the Order of St. Benedict, founded in the diocese of Namur in 982 by Emperor Otto and Abbot Wicbert. — Privilege of Pope Benedict VII, 983, CXXXVII, 345, 546. — The learned monk Sigebert flourished in 1112, CLX, 9. — Likewise Anselm, ibid., 239. — *Life of Blessed Wibert*, by Sigebert, ibid., 391. — *Deeds of the Abbots of Gembloux*, ibid., 595. — Innocent II confirms the election of Abbot Arnulf, 1137, CLXXIX, 341. — Abbot Guibert flourished in 1203, CCXI, 1281. — Decree of Innocent III confirming the elected abbot, 1199, CCXIV, 720. — Privilege of the same pope, 1213, CCXVI, 937.

**OF JAMETS** (Jamets-en-Barrois), a monastery of the Order of St. Benedict, built by St. Philibert and St. Bathildis in 684, LXXXVII, 670.

**OF ST. PETER OF JUMIÈGES**, an illustrious monastery of the Order of St. Benedict, built in Normandy about 655. — Testament of St. Ansegisus, 833, CV, 744. A poem on the foundation, destruction, and restoration of this monastery, CXXXVIII, 394. — Charter of Albert, abbot of Micy, 1004, CXXXIX, 585. — William the Calculator flourished in 1087, CXLIX, 177. — On the foundation and restoration of this monastery, CCII, 1315. — Abbot Alexander flourished in 1200, CCV, 919.

**OF ST. GEMINUS OF VITERBO** (Saint-Gémin of Viterbo), a monastery to whose abbot Innocent III wrote in 1211, CCXVI, 472.

**OF ST. PETER OF GÉNERES** (Saint-Pé de Géneres, diocese of Lescar, Hautes-Pyrénées), a monastery of St. Benedict, founded by King Sancho in 1096. — Asserted to belong to the bishop of Lescar by Pope Paschal II, 1114, CLXIII, 354.

**OF ST. GENEROSUS** (Saint-Généroux), a priory not far from the monastery of St. Jouin de Marnes in the diocese of Poitiers, LXXXVIII, 492.

**OF ST. GENESIUS OF THIERS** (Saint-Genez de Thiers, Auvergne), a monastery of the Order of St. Benedict, founded about 520 by St. Avitus, bishop of Clermont, LXXI, 763, note.

**OF ST. GENESIUS** (Saint-Geniès, in the Florentine countryside, Tuscany), a monastery of the Order of St. Augustine, to which Celestine III granted a privilege in 1195, CCVI, 1085.

**OF GENEVA.** See **ST. VICTOR**.

**OF GENGENBACH** (Gengenbach, former diocese of Strasbourg), a monastery of the Order of St. Benedict, built in 712 by Ruthard, count of Alsace, and enlarged in 742 by Pirmin, bishop of Strasbourg. — Privilege of Innocent II confirming the possessions of this monastery, 1138, CLXXIX, 404.

— Of Innocent III, 1198, CCXVII, 36.

**OF ST. GENGULF.** See **OF TOUL**.

**OF GENOLHAC** (Genolhac, diocese of Périgueux), a monastery built in the sixth century and mentioned by Gregory of Tours. Its abbot was Blessed Cyprian in 585, LXXI, 901.

**OF ST. GENEVIEVE OF PARIS** (Sainte-Geneviève-du-Mont, Paris), an illustrious abbey of the Order of St. Augustine, founded in the sixth century by Clovis and St. Clotilde, first in honour of Saints Peter and Paul. Having been devastated by the Northmen, it was restored by Suger, abbot of St. Denis, who introduced there the canons of St. Victor of Paris, 1160, LXXI, note. — The testament of St. Ansegisus mentions it, 833, CV, 745. — Letter of Innocent II to Stephen, bishop of Paris, that he should exempt the abbey from an interdict, 1143, 620. — Certain monks of St. Martin-des-Champs were established there by Abbot Suger with the assent of Eugenius III, 1148, CLXXX, 1347, 1368, 1379, 1565. — Decree of Adrian IV, 1154, CLXXXVIII, 1361. — Of Alexander III, 1163, CC, 211. — Letter of Clement III to the abbot of St. Genevieve, 1188, CCIV, 1367, 1470. — Abbot Stephen flourished in 1203, CCXI, 205. — Letter of Innocent III to Abbot John, 1202, CCXIV, 1097; CCXV, 31, 586, 1191, 1542, 1565, 1578; CCXVI, 155, 518. — The same pope granted the abbot the use of the mitre, CCXVII, 52, 86, 92.

**OF ST. GEORGE** (Saint-Georges, diocese of Le Mans), a monastery in the district of Le Mans. — Diploma of Charlemagne, 802, XCVII, 993.

[Col. 1072] **OF ST. GEORGE OF MARATO** (Marat, Sicily), a monastery mentioned by St. Gregory the Great in the sixth century, LXXVII, 563.

**OF ST. GEORGE OF THE BLACK FOREST** (Saint-Georges in the Black Forest), a monastery of the Order of St. Benedict in the diocese of Constance, built in 824 and restored at the end of the eleventh century by the nobleman Hesso. Pope Urban II took it under his protection in 1095, CLI, 400. — Privilege of Pope Innocent II, 1139, CLXXIX, 437.

**OF ST. GEORGE.** See **OF BARAL**, **OF LUCCA**, and **OF VENICE**.

**OF GERBACH** (Gerbach or Ingerbach, Thuringia), a monastery of the Order of St. Augustine, founded or greatly enlarged by Henry, bishop of Regensburg. At his request Innocent II confirmed it by privilege in 1142, CLXXIX, 584.

**OF GERBEROY** (Gerberoy, diocese of Beauvais), a monastery of the Order of St. Augustine, to which Anastasius IV granted a privilege in 1153, CLXXXVIII, 1043. — Alexander III, 1163, CC, 215.

**OF ST. JOHN OF GERBSTÄDT** (Saint-Jean de Gerbstädt, county of Mansfeld, Prussia), a nunnery founded by Margrave Conrad; at his request Innocent II adorned it with a privilege in 1137, CLXXIX, 335.

**OF ST. GEREMARUS.** See **OF FLAVY**.

**OF GERRESHEIM** (Gerresheim, diocese of Cologne), a nunnery, concerning the election of whose abbess Innocent III wrote in 1200, CCXIV, 940.

**OF GERNRODE**, a nunnery which, according to the author of the *Life of St. Matilda*, was built by her, CLI, 21. According to Thietmar, however, it was founded by Margrave Gero, ibid., note. See below, **OF GERNRODE**.

**OF ST. GERMANUS OF AUXERRE.** See **OF AUXERRE**.

**OF ST. GERMANUS OF AUXERRE AT PARIS** (Saint-Germain-l’Auxerrois, Paris): this monastery seems to have been built by the same king as the following one and under the invocation of St. Vincent. Destroyed by the Northmen, it was rebuilt by Louis the Pious. It is sometimes called St. Germanus of the Round Church. This monastery is mentioned in Innocent II’s privilege concerning the possessions of the Church of Paris, CLXXIX, 352. Letter of Pope Lucius II concerning the same church, ibid., 915. — Letter of Eugenius III concerning the election of the abbot of St. Germanus, CLXXX, 1294. — Letter of Innocent III to the dean, 1206, CCXV, 980.

**OF ST. GERMANUS OF THE MEADOWS** (Saint-Germain-des-Prés, Paris), a most celebrated monastery of the Order of St. Benedict, founded in 558 by St. Germanus, bishop of Paris, and King Childebert, son of Clovis, under the invocation of St. Vincent, whose relics Childebert had brought from Spain, LXXI, 265, note. — Diploma of Childebert III, 703, LXXXVIII, 1099. — Likewise, of Theuderic IV, 730, ibid., 1146. Charter of Vandemirus and Erchamberta, ibid., 1216. — Charter of Charlemagne, 772, XCVII, 922, 963, 974. — Of Louis the Pious, 817, CIV, 1065, 1175. — The monk Usuard flourished in 838; Aimoin in 888, CXXVI, 1009. — The monk Remigius, 908, CXXXI, 47. — Abbo, 923, CXXXII, 721. — Charter of Abbot William, 1028, CXLI, 835. — Privilege of King Robert, 1002, ibid., 948. — Privilege of Paschal II, 1107, CLXIII, 207. — Of Calixtus II, 1230. — Of Innocent II, 1130, CLXXIX, 65. — Of Anastasius IV, 1153, CLXXXVIII, 1030. — Dedication of the church by Alexander III, then in Gaul, 1163, CC, 208. — Privileges of Alexander III, 1176, ibid., 1052, 1083, 1115, 1255, 1292. — Charter of Robert, abbot of St. Germanus, 1194, CCV, 914. — Privileges granted by Innocent III to Abbot Robert, 1198, CCXIV, 151, 163; 1207, CCXV, 1191. — Letter of the same pope concerning rebuilding the walls of the city of Paris, 1210, CCXVI, 284; 1211, ibid., 488; CCXVII, 15, 26. — Concerning the settlement between the monastery and the bishop of Sens, 28, 51, 64, 125, 145, 169.

**OF ST. GERMANUS AT LAIE** (Saint-Germain-en-Laye, near Paris), a small abbey built by King Robert and later granted by Henry I to the church of St. Mary of Paris, year uncertain, CLI, 1039. — Diploma of Philip I, king of the Franks, 1072, CLIX, 841. — Lucius III, 1181, CCI, 1088.

**OF ST. GERMANUS OF MONTFAUCON.** See **OF MONT**.

**OF ST. GERMANUS** (Saint-Germain on the Sarthe, diocese of Le Mans), a small monastery beyond the Sarthe in the district of Le Mans. — Diploma of Charlemagne, 802, XCVII, 993.

**OF ST. MARY AND ST. CYRIACUS OF GERNRODE, OR GERONDODE** (Sainte-Marie de Gernrode, principality of Anhalt-Bernburg), a celebrated nunnery of the Order of St. Augustine, founded by Gero of Lusatia, landgrave, between 930 and 965; it was later enlarged by Count Rucker of Bilstein. Privilege of Celestine III, 1195, CCVI, 1123. — Privilege of Innocent III, 1207, CCXV, 1199, 1200.

**MONASTERY OF GERNRODE**, for men, built beside the preceding nunnery by the same Gero, and later transferred to the Premonstratensians. The privilege of Celestine III, CCVI, 1123, refers equally to it.

**OF GEROLD.** See **MOUNT GEROLD**.

**OF GERSTEIN** (Gersteyn, diocese of Passau, Lower Bavaria), a monastery whose abbot Innocent III addressed concerning a case involving the monastery of Melk in 1208, CCXVII, 178.

**OF ST. GERVASIUS OF PARIS** (the Almonry of Saint-Gervais, Paris), a house which Alexander III declared to belong to the brethren of the Almonry in 1175, CC, 1031.

**OF STS. GERVASIUS AND PROTASIUS.** See above **OF GEVAUDAN** and **OF FOSSES**.

**OF GIARDI.** See **OF THE FOUNTAIN**.

**OF ST. MARY OF GIF** (Notre-Dame de Gif, Seine-et-Oise, former diocese of Paris), a nunnery of the Order of St. Benedict, founded in 1166 by Maurice de Sully, bishop of Paris. — Privilege of Clement III, 1188, CCIV, 1284. — It was annexed to the nunnery of Val-de-Grâce under Innocent III in 1207, CCXV, 1250.

**OF ST. PETER OF GIGNY, OR GIGNIACUM** (Saint-Pierre de Gigny, diocese of Lyons), a monastery of the Order of St. Benedict, founded by the venerable Abbot Berno in 892. — Privilege of Pope Formosus, CXXIX, 845. — Gregory VII entrusted its government to the abbot of Cluny in 1075, CXLVIII, 667. — Letter of Eugenius III against the monks of Gigny because they were harming the brethren of Mirator, 1152, CLXXX, 1517. — Decree of Anastasius IV concerning the same case, 1153, CLXXXVIII, 1037. — Privilege of Innocent III, 1200, CCXVII, 61.

**OF ST. GILDAS IN THE WOOD** (Saint-Gildas-aux-Bois, diocese of Nantes), a monastery of the Order of St. Benedict, founded in 1026 in a place called Lampadus in the district of Nantes by the noble Armorican Simon, son of Rocabernard; Helgot was its first abbot, CXLI, 1281.

**OF ST. GINESIUS** (Saint-Genèse, diocese of Lucca in Lombardy), a monastery of the Order of St. Augustine, founded shortly before 1205, when Innocent III confirmed it by privilege, CCXVII, 150.

**OF JARROW**, a monastery in England; it was so close to Wearmouth that it seemed to be one with it, XC, 10. See **OF WEARMOUTH**.

**OF GISEBURN** (Gisburn, diocese of York, England), a monastery whose abbot Innocent III entrusted with responsibility for reforming certain monasteries in 1207, CCXV, 1128.

**OF ST. GISLENUS, OR GHISLENUS.** See **OF ST. PETER OF CAMBRAI**.

**OF ST. MARY OF GIF** (Notre-Dame de Gif, near Versailles, Seine-et-Oise), a nunnery founded by Maurice de Sully, bishop of Paris. — Letter of Alexander confirming goods bestowed by the nunnery of Hederensis and by Maurice himself, 1180, CC, 1293.

**OF GIXAL** (Gixal, diocese of Barcelona in Catalonia), a monastery of the Order of St. Benedict, whose rights and possessions Alexander III confirmed in 1163, CC, 245.

**OF ST. MARTIN OF GLANDIÈRES** (Saint-Martin de Glandières or Longueville, diocese of Metz), a monastery of the Order of St. Benedict, built about 587. — Privilege of Innocent III, 1210, CCXVII, 199.

**OF ST. MARY OF GLANFEUILLE** (Notre-Dame de la Chapelle-Glain, later called Saint-Maur de Glanfeuille, diocese of Angers), a monastery of the Order of St. Benedict on the Loire in the district of Angers. Having fallen into ruin through the lapse of time, it was rebuilt by Count Rorico and, by privilege of Louis the Pious, subjected to the abbey of Saint-Maur-des-Fossés in 833, CIV, 1230. — Privilege of Urban II, 1096, CLI, 456. — Bull of the same Urban, by which he removed this monastery from Fossés and restored it to Cluny, 1096, CLI, 489. — Privilege of Anastasius IV, 1153, CLXXXVIII, 1023. — Innocent III joined to it the monks of St. Peter of Les Cultures in 1208, CCXV, 1557. — Privilege of the same pope, 1203, CCXVII, 277.

**OF ST. MARY OF GLASTONBURY** (Notre-Dame de Glastonbury, county of Somerset), a monastery founded in England in the tenth century by St. Dunstan, bishop, and King Edgar. — Privilege of Pope John XIII, 971, CXXXV, 984. — The beginnings of the same monastery, CXXXVIII, 423, 430; CXXXIX, 1435. — Charter of King Edgar, 970, CXXXVIII, 517. — Likewise, of Cnut I, by which the abbot of this monastery was appointed judge of both ecclesiastical and secular causes, CLI, 1188. — Privilege of Calixtus II, 1123, CLXIII, 1295. — Letter of Innocent III concerning this monastery’s dispute with its bishop, 1199, CCXIV, 869. — Letter of Innocent III, 1206, CCXV, 827.

**NUNNERY OF ST. GLODESIND.** See **OF METZ**.

**OF ST. MARY OF GOTTESAU** (Sainte-Marie de Gottesau, Swabia), a monastery of the Order of St. Benedict, built by the nobleman Berthold, count of Hohenburg, shortly before 1123, when Calixtus II, at the request of Abbot Burchard, endowed it with a privilege, [Col. 1074] CLXIII, 1240.

**OF ST. ANDREW OF GOES** (Saint-André de Goes, Upper Styria), a nunnery of the Order of St. Benedict, whose possessions and rights Eugenius III confirmed in 1148, CLXXX, 1335.

**OF ST. LAWRENCE OF GOLDBACH** (Saint-Laurent of Goldbach, Swabia), a monastery of the Order of St. Augustine, whose goods and rights Celestine III confirmed in 1192, CCVI, 913.

**OF ST. MARY OF GORGONA ISLAND** (Convent of St. Mary on Gorgona Island, in the Adriatic Gulf), a monastery situated in the Tyrrhenian Sea, mentioned by Gregory the Great in the sixth century, LXXVII, 514. — St. Leo, pope, confirmed and enlarged its rights and privileges in 1051, CXLIII, 677.

**OF ST. PETER OF GORZE** (Saint-Pierre of Gorze, former diocese of Metz), a monastery of the Order of St. Benedict, founded and endowed in 745 by St. Chrodegang, bishop. Donations of Bishop Angilram, 770, XCVI, 1097, 1098. — Diploma of Charlemagne, 768, XCVII, 913. — Likewise, of Louis the Pious, 815, CIV, 1019. — Of Robert, bishop of Metz, 916, CXXXII, 529. — Abbot John flourished in 978, CXXXVII, 239. — Privilege of Godfrey of Bouillon, later king of Jerusalem, 1096, 395. — Of Bishop Poppo, 1095, CLV, 1653. — Letter of Alexander III in favour of this monastery, 1174, CC, 974.

**OF ST. MARY OF GOSLAR** (Sainte-Marie de Goslar, Saxony), a monastery of the Order of St. Augustine in the diocese of Minden, not far from Hildesheim, built by Bishop Theoderic in the eleventh century, CXLI, 1218. — Privilege of St. Leo IX, 1049, CXLIII, 931; of Victor II, CXLIII, 822. — Letter of Anastasius IV to the bishop of Halberstadt in favour of this monastery, CLXXXVIII, 1076; of Adrian IV, 1154, ibid., 1420.

**OF GOTLAND** (Gotland in Livonia, Prussia), a monastery whose abbot was entrusted with the care of the brethren of the Order of the Temple who were being established there in 1213, CCXVI, 918.

**OF ST. MARY OF GÖTTWEIG** (Notre-Dame of Göttweig or Kettwein in Crimea), a monastery of the Order of St. Benedict, built in 1083 by Blessed Hartmann, bishop of Passau, who was also its abbot. — Privileges of Urban II, 1088, 1099, CLI, 519. — Privileges of Paschal II, 1104, CLXIII, 129, 432.

**OF ST. JOHN OF GREZ** (Saint-Jean de Grez, diocese of Tours), a priory of the Order of St. Augustine. Letter of Innocent II concerning the election of the prior, 1203, CCXV, 34.

**OF GRADIZ** (Gradiz, Moravia), a monastery of the Premonstratensian Order, founded under Eugenius III; his letter survives, CLXXX, 1044.

**OF ST. ALEXANDER OF GRAFSCHAFT** (Saint-Alexandre de Grafschaft, diocese of Cologne), a monastery of the Order of St. Benedict in the diocese of Cologne, founded by Archbishop Anno, as his charter reports, in 1072, CXLIII, 1586. — Diploma of Archbishop Frederick, 1120, CLXVI, 1353.

**OF ST. MARY OF GRANDGOURGIT** (Notre-Dame de Grangoulet, Seine-et-Oise), a monastery of the Premonstratensian Order, built by several noblemen whose names may be seen in the privilege of Clement III, 1188, CCIV, 1298.

**OF GRANDMONT** (Grammont, diocese of Limoges), a monastery and a new order whose founder was St. Stephen of Muret about 1076. — Letter and privilege of Urban III, 1166, CCII, 1415, 1416. — On St. Stephen, founder of this order, CCIV, 997, 1011. — Peter Bernard, fifth prior, flourished in 1191; he was succeeded by William of Trahinac in 1177 and Gerard Itherius, ibid. — Letters of Clement III to the brethren of Grandmont, 1188, ibid., 1375, 1377, 1426. — Letters and privileges of Innocent III, 1198, CCXIV, 496; 1202, ibid., 945, 948; 1207, CCXV, 1141; CCXVII, 216.

**OF GREAT ST. BERNARD** (Le Grand-Saint-Bernard, canton of Vaud, Switzerland), a monastery of regular canons of St. Augustine, reconciled in a certain dispute with the brethren of Melliradio by Blessed Amadeus, bishop of Lausanne, in 1154, CLXXXVIII, 1292.

**OF GRAVACO, OR GRAVE** (Gravac, duchy of Piacenza), a monastery of the Order of St. Benedict, built about 746. Louis the Pious commanded in 820 that certain things taken from it be restored to it, CIV, 1095.

**OF ST. MARY OF GRANDVAL** (Notre-Dame de Grandval), a monastery of the Order of St. Benedict in the diocese of Strasbourg, built and enlarged under Abbot Gundoald by donations of Pippin in 770, XCVI, 1579.

**OF THE GREAT WOOD.** See **OF LA SAUVE-MAJEURE**.

**OF STS. PETER AND VICTOR OF GRASSELL** (Could this be Gréoux, in the Basses-Alpes?), a monastery of the Order of St. Benedict, founded in 692, LXXXVIII, 1088. — Privilege of Chlodovech [Col. 1075] III, ibid. — Charter of Aredius, 683, LXXVIII, 1204.

**OF ST. GRATA**, a monastery in the diocese of Urgell, rebuilt by Bishop Possidonius. — Privilege of Louis the Pious, 822, CIV, 1125; CXIX, 487.

**OF GOD’S GRACE** (Grâce-Dieu, diocese of Magdeburg, Germany), a monastery of the Premonstratensian Order, founded in 1131 by Count Otto of Crudorp and St. Norbert himself. — Privilege of Innocent II, 1138, CLXXIX, 377.

**OF GRATTER, OR GAZER**, a monastery of the Order of St. Benedict built in the city of Naples and in a place called Playa. St. Gregory the Great wrote to its abbot, LXXVII, 1113, 1255. — It was annexed, together with the monastery of St. Sebastian and another at Pozzuoli, ibid.

**OF ST. GREGORY ON THE RHINE** (Saint-Grégoire on the Rhine, diocese of Constance or Basel), a monastery founded in 989 by Gebehard, bishop of Constance, and taken under the protection of John XV, CXXXVII, 838. — Decree of Innocent III prohibiting the conferral of prebends upon secular persons, 1210, CCXVII, 199.

**OF ST. GREGORY** (Saint-Grégoire of Alsace, diocese of Strasbourg), a monastery of the Order of St. Benedict, to which Bodalus made certain donations in 747, LXXXVIII, 1211. — Charter of Sigfrid, 768, XCVI, 1564. — Diploma of King Carloman, 769, ibid., 1574. — Louis the Pious granted it the forest of Columbarium (Colmar) in 826, CIV, 1157.

**OF GRENFELD** (the nuns of Grenfeld, county of Lincoln, England), a nunnery founded in the diocese of Lincoln by the nobleman Ralph d’Aby, whose donations St. Hugh, bishop, confirmed at the end of the twelfth century, CLIII, 1122.

**OF GRIMBERGEN** (Grimbergen in Brabant, near Brussels), a monastery of the Premonstratensian Order, built and endowed by several devout men, who are mentioned in the privilege of Eugenius III, 1147, CLXXX,
1209.

GRISTANENSE OF ST MARY (Notre-Dame de Grestain, near Honfleur), a monastery of the Order of St Benedict, built by Herluin of Conteville in 1050. — Letter of Arnulf, bishop of Lisieux, to the abbot of this monastery, about 1175, CCI, 81; CCII, 1318.

GROENINGENSIS OF ST MARY (Notre-Dame de Groeningen, near Courtrai, Belgium), a convent of nuns of the Cistercian Order, built in 1238 by Joanna and Agnes, daughters of Walter, lord of Rodenburg. In 1439 Margaret, the abbess, gave the abbot of Clairvaux a portion of the relics preserved there, CLXXXV, 1742.

GROFFCHATTENSE. See above, GRAFFCHAPP.

GUALDENENSE OF ST BENEDICT (Saint-Benoît de Gualdena, Italy), a monastery of the Camaldolese Order, to which Clement III granted a privilege in 1188, CCIV, 1339.

GUASTALLA OF ST PETER (Saint-Pierre de Guastalla, diocese of Mantua), a monastery of the Order of St Augustine, built by Queen Ermingarde and the noble lord Gariman in 1095, and endowed with a privilege by Urban II, CLI, 412. — Privilege of Pope Innocent II, 1132, CLXXIX, 159. — Of Eugenius III, 1145, CLXXX, 1048. — Of Adrian IV, 1157, CLXXXVIII, 1497.

GUDHEMENSIS (the convent of Gudhem in Denmark), a convent of nuns built by King Canute V in the eleventh century. — Privilege of Alexander III, 1176, CC, 1060.

WILLIAM OF THE DESERTS. See GELLONENSE.

GUINGAMPENSE OF THE HOLY CROSS (Sainte-Croix de Guingamp, Brittany), a monastery of the Order of St Augustine, built by certain noblemen in the twelfth century. — Privilege of Clement III, 1190, CCIV, 1487.

ST GUNTHMAR (Abbey of Lierre, diocese of Meaux), a monastery of the Order of St Augustine, not far from Meaux, founded by the devout man Gunthmar, who was buried there, in 775, CXLIX, 142.

GURTHONENSE AND GUERDONENSE (Notre-Dame de Gourdon-en-Charolais), a monastery of the Order of St Benedict, in which the devout monk Desideratus, a priest, lived, in 570, LXXII, 893. See GABILONENSE OF THE LEPERS.

GYRENSIS CHARTERHOUSE (Charterhouse of Gyren, diocese of Gurk, Lower Carinthia), a monastery built by Henry, bishop of Gurk, in the time of Alexander III; his letter of 1174, CC, 949.

HAGUENONENSE OF SS PHILIP AND WALBURGA (Haguenau, diocese of Strasbourg), a monastery of the Order of St Benedict, constructed by the princes Frederick and Peter before 1102, when Paschal II confirmed it by privilege, CLXIII, 97.

HAIDENHEINNENSE, for HEIDENHEINNENSE.

HALBERSTATENSE OF ST JOHN (Saint-Jean d’Halberstadt), a monastery of the Order of St Benedict, whose goods and possessions Innocent II confirmed in 1138, CLXXIX, 376.

HALBERSTATENSE OF ST MARY (Notre-Dame d’Halberstadt), a monastery of the Order of St Augustine, whose goods Celestine II confirmed by privilege in 1143, CLXXIX, 784.

[Col. 1076] HALBERSTATENSE. See MICHAELSTEINENSE.

HALBERSTATENSE OF ST THOMAS (Saint-Thomas d’Halberstadt), a monastery of the Premonstratensian Order, founded by Bishop Theodoric shortly before 1192, in which year Celestine III confirmed it by privilege, CCVI, 911.

HALLENSE. See REICHENHALLENSE.

HALLENSE (Halle, in the duchy of Magdeburg), a monastery of the Order of St Augustine, otherwise called *Ad Novum Opus*, that is, “Made Anew”; Celestine III confirmed its goods and privileges in 1194, CCVI, 1048.

HAMANABURGENSE OF ST MICHAEL (Saint-Michel d’Hamambourg, diocese of Mainz), a monastery of the Order of St Benedict, founded by St Boniface, bishop of Mainz, about 748, LXXXIX, 647, 692 note.

HAMATGIENSIS OF ST EUSEBIA (Hamage near Marchiennes), a convent of nuns founded by the virgin and abbess Eusebia herself, at an uncertain date, CXLIX, 133.

HAMELENENSE (Hamelen or Hameln in Lower Saxony), a monastery of the Premonstratensian Order. Its administrator wrote to St Hildegard, abbess of Mount St Rupert, commending himself to her prayers, twelfth century, CXCVII, 302.

HAMENSE (Ham, diocese of Noyon), a monastery of the Order of St Augustine. Alexander III wrote to its abbot in 1172, CC, 764.

HAMENSE OF THE HOLY SAVIOUR. See GERWANENSE.

HAMERSLEBENSE OF ST PANCRAS (Saint-Pancrace d’Hammersleben, diocese of Halberstadt), a monastery of the Order of St Augustine, whose possessions and rights Paschal II confirmed in 1116, CLXIII, 399. — Privilege by which Honorius II subjected certain monasteries to it, 1129, CLXVI, 1303. — Privilege of Innocent II, 1138, CLXXIX, 373.

HAMERSLEBENSE OF SS PETER AND PAUL (Saint-Pierre d’Hamersleben, diocese of Halberstadt), a monastery of the Order of St Augustine, which Eugenius III took under his protection in 1145, CLXXX, 1059. — Celestine III confirms the gift of the church of St Stephen, 1195, CCVI, 1091.

HANCHIS (Hanches near Maintenon, diocese of Chartres), a small monastery or priory granted by Pagan, archdeacon of Chartres, to William, abbot of Marmoutier, in 1114. Privilege of Ivo, bishop of Chartres, CLXII, 295.

HARDEHUSANUM, or HERNVITHELENSENSE OF ST MARY (Sainte-Marie de Hardehausen, diocese of Paderborn), a monastery of the Cistercian Order, descended from Kamp and founded by Bishop Bernard in 1040; he chose burial there. Privilege of Adrian IV, 1155, CLXXXVIII, 1429.

HASELACENSE (Haselach, former diocese of Strasbourg), a monastery of the Order of St Benedict, founded by King Dagobert and Abbot Florentius in 633 in the diocese of Strasbourg (interpolated charter, LXXX, 524). — Privilege of Lucius III, 1182, CCI, 1140.

HASNONIENSE OF ST PETER (St Peter of Hasnon), a double monastery of the Order of St Benedict in the diocese of Arras, founded by Abbot John and his sister Eulalia in 678: one house was for men and the other for women, CXLVII and following. When it was almost ruined in the eleventh century, it was rebuilt from the foundations by the count of Hasnon under Pope Alexander II, in 1070, CXLVII, 898. — Abbot Roland was renowned for exceptional integrity, CXLVII, 598.

HASNUNENSE OF SS MARCELLINUS AND PETER (Saint-Marcellin-et-Pierre d’Hasnon, diocese of Arras), a monastery of the Order of St Benedict, once very wealthy in the diocese of Arras and perhaps in the same place as the preceding entry, owing to the similarity of the name. In the eleventh century it is found diminished and neglected, CXLIXX, 133.

HASSARODENSE, a monastery built beside the River Main in the diocese of Eichstätt (mentioned in Rabanus Maurus, eighth century), CVII, 54.

HASTERIENSIS (Hastières, Meurthe), a convent of nuns in the diocese of Metz, established by Countess Bertha, wife of Count Wideric, in 626, LXXXVIII, 1159. — Letter of Clement III to the abbot, 1190, CCIV, 1578.

HAVERHOLMENSIS (Haverholm, diocese of Lincoln, England), a convent of nuns mentioned in a letter of Innocent III, 1204, CCXV, 368.

HANNOGIENSE. See HONAUGIENSE.

HAY, OF THE ISLAND, OF ST COLUMBA. See HIENSE.

HEDERENSIS OF ST MARY (Notre-Dame d’Yerres or Hières near Corbeil), a convent of nuns of the Order of St Benedict, built by Stephen, bishop of Paris. Charter of foundation, 1138, CLXXIII, 1427. — Privilege of Innocent II, 1141, CLXXIX, 541. — These nuns assist the sisters of Gif, 1180, CC, 1292. — Decree of Innocent III concerning the number of nuns, 1208, CCXV, 1368.

HECKLINGENSE OF SS GEORGE AND PANCRAS (St George or St Pancras of Eglingen, Swabia), a convent of nuns formerly founded by the nobleman Count Bernard and endowed with a privilege by Innocent II in 1140, CLXXIV, 498.

[Col. 1077] HEGENSE OF ST MARY (Sainte-Marie d’Heyn, diocese of Mainz), a monastery of the Cistercian Order, founded in 1140 by Count Boppo of Reichenbach and his wife Bertha. — Letter of Innocent III, 1205, CCXV, 559.

HEGENENSE, HEGENHENSE, or HEGENBACENSE OF ST MARY (Notre-Dame d’Hégenbach in Swabia), a monastery of the Cistercian Order, founded in the twelfth century. Its abbot wrote to St Hildegard, asking her to commend him to God, about the middle of the twelfth century, CXCVII, 298.

HEIDENHEIMENSE (Heidenheim in Swabia), a monastery of the Order of St Benedict, built in the diocese of Eichstätt in 758 by St Willibald, son of Richard, king of the Anglo-Saxons, CXXIX, 869, 870. — Eugenius III took it under his protection in 1152, CLXXX, 1567, 1509. — Privilege of Adrian IV, 1155, CLXXXVIII, 1432.

HEIDENHEIMENSIS (the nuns of Heidenheim), a convent of nuns built beside his own monastery by the same holy Abbot Willibald; his sister St Walburga was its abbess, about 780, CXXIX, 869, 870. — It was granted to the monks under Eugenius III in 1150, CLXXX, 1439, 1440.

HEILSBROMENSE, or OF THE FOUNTAIN OF SALVATION, OF ST MARY (Notre-Dame d’Heilsbrunn, diocese of Bamberg, Bavaria), a monastery of the Cistercian Order, founded by Otto, bishop of Bamberg, in 1132, CLXXIII, 1279, 1308. — Otto’s charter concerning the foundation of this monastery, 1132, CLXXIII, 1346. — Privilege of Eugenius III, 1148, CLXXX, 1303, 1522.

HEINBERGENSIS OF ST MARY (Sainte-Marie d’Heinsberg, diocese of Cologne), a convent of nuns of the Order of St Augustine, according to the Premonstratensian reform, founded by Philip, archbishop of Cologne, and Rudolf, bishop of Liège. Celestine III confirmed it by privilege in 1194, CCVI, 1030.

HEISTERBACENSE OF ST PETER OF THE MOUNT (Saint-Pierre du Mont or du Val, at Heisterbach, diocese of Cologne), a monastery of the Cistercian Order, founded in 1188 by Philip of Heinsberg, archbishop of Cologne. — Privilege of Celestine III, 1193, CCVI, 1003.

HELDERENSIS CONVENT OF NUNS. See HEDERENSIS.

HELIONENSE OF SS FABIAN AND FELICITY, a convent of nuns. See ANDLAVIENSIS.

HELMENSTADENSE OF ST LUDGER (Ludger Cloister, in the duchy of Brunswick), a monastery of the Order of St Benedict, founded in the duchy of Brunswick by St Ludger, bishop of Münster, in the ninth century, XCIX, 748, 749.

HELMESWARDENSE, or HELMWARDESHUSENSE, a monastery of the Order of St Benedict in Westphalia, granted by Emperor St Henry II to the bishop of Paderborn in 1017, CXL, 335. — Privilege of Eugenius III, 1148, CLXXX, 1317.

HELMSTADENSE, or MONASTERY OF THE VALLEY OF ST MARY (Sainte-Marie de Valmoûtier at Helmstadt, duchy of Brunswick), a monastery of the Cistercian Order, founded before 1192, in which year Celestine III confirmed it by privilege, CCVI, 912.

HELWATESHUSENSE, a monastery whose abbot Innocent III wrote to in 1206. The location is not sufficiently certain, CCXV, 921.

HEMMERODIENSE, or CLAUSTRUM NOVUM (Himmelrod in the county of Hohenstein, Thuringia), a monastery of the Cistercian Order, built before the time of Innocent II, who confirmed it by privilege in 1140, CLXXIX, 530. — Privilege of Eugenius III, 1152, CLXXX, 1527. — Letter of Celestine III, 1196, CCVI, 1188.

HENIMENSE OF ST MARTIN (Hennin-Liétard), a small monastery of the Order of St Augustine, founded by Robert, bishop of Arras, in 1040 between Douai and Lens, CXLIX, 132.

HENLIENSE (Henley, county of Oxford, England), a monastery of the Order of St Augustine. — Letter of Innocent III concerning a matrimonial matter, 1203, CCXV, 46, 81.

HERENIENSE. See BLASII, IN THE BLACK FOREST.

HERDENSE (Herden or Huert, county of Nesselrode, Westphalia), a monastery visited by St Hildegard; its abbot wrote to that most devout abbess, asking to commend himself to her prayers, twelfth century, CXCVII, 302.

HERENSE OF ST PHILIBERT (St Philibert on the island of Herr), a monastery of the Order of St Benedict, built by Bishop Otto from grants of Charlemagne and later confirmed by Lothair in 830, CIV, 1183. — John VIII joined the monastery of St Porcian to it in 876, CXXVI, 687.

HERFORDENSE. See ERFORTENSE.

ST HERIBERT. See TUITIENSE.

HERINGENSE (Heringen in Thuringia), a monastery of the Order of St Benedict, built by Otto of the castle of Iringi (Heringen), with the assent of Calixtus II, in 1121, CLXIII, 1203.

HERIVALLIS OF ST MARY (Notre-Dame d’Hérivaux, Seine-et-Oise), a monastery of the Order of St Augustine, built in 1138 near Luzarches by the hermit Ascelin, under Maurice, bishop of Paris. [Col. 1078] — Privilege of Alexander III, 1163, CC, 210. — Of Clement III, 1188, CCIV, 1284, 1314. — Maurice de Sully confirmed the foundation in 1183, CCV, 902.

HERMENRODIENSE, a monastery whose abbot Innocent III wrote to concerning a certain dispute among the canons of Cologne, CCXIV, 749. It appears to be the same as Hemmerodiense above.

HERMERIENSE OF ST NICHOLAS (Saint-Nicolas or Notre-Dame d’Hermières, diocese of Paris), a monastery of the Order of St Augustine, founded before 1160. — Privilege of Lucius III, 1183, CCI, 1220. — Of Clement III, 1188, CCIV, 1284.

HERRISIENSIS, or HERTIENSIS (Herrs or Hertz, diocese of Paderborn), a convent of nuns built in the diocese of Paderborn. — Privilege of Pope Stephen, 891, CXXIX, 815. — Letter of Innocent III concerning the election of an abbess, 1205, CCXV, 559.

HERSWELDENSE, or HERSFELDENSE (Hersfeld, former diocese of Halberstadt), a monastery of the Order of St Benedict, founded in the early years of Charlemagne by St Lullus, archbishop of Mainz, in the diocese of Halberstadt, CXLI, 443. Its abbot was the distinguished Haymo, pupil of Alcuin and later bishop, in 839, CXVI, 185; CXLI, 1170. — Diploma of Emperor St Henry II, 1024, CXL, 380. — Privilege of Pope Paschal II, 1111, CLXIII, 286.

HERUTENSE, or HERUTEVENSE, that is, “Island of the Hart” (Hartlepool, county of Durham), a monastery of girls in the territory of Durham, founded by Oswiu, king of the English; his daughter St Hilda was its first abbess, in 655, XCV, 156, 208.

HERWETHESHUSENSE, a monastery whose abbot Innocent III wrote to in 1206, CCXV, 921. — Its location seems uncertain.

HESDINENSE (Hesdin, diocese of Saint-Omer, Pas-de-Calais), a monastery whose prior Innocent III wrote to in 1202 concerning the canons of St Omer, CCXVII, 94.

HESSENSIS OF ST MARY, SS MARTIN AND LAWRENCE (Notre-Dame or St Lawrence in Hesse), a convent of nuns in Alsace near Sarrebourg, built by Bruno, father of St Leo IX. Leo IX, formerly bishop of Toul, granted it many privileges in 1054, CXLIII, 740.

HETEWARDENSE (Hetewarden, diocese of Mainz), a monastery to which Innocent III wrote concerning the election of the abbess of Herrisiense, in 1205, CCXV, 359.

HEYLLSHEMIENSE OF ST MARY (Sainte-Marie d’Heiligen, county of Namur), a monastery of the Premonstratensian Order, built by the nobleman Rainer of Zetrud shortly before 1134, when Innocent II confirmed it, CLXXIX, 220.

HIENSE, or HYENSE (the island of Hy, opposite Scotland), a monastery on the Hiberno-Scottish island of that name (today Columba), built by St Columbanus in 563. SS Arculf and Adomnan flourished there in the eighth century, LXXXVIII, 721, 723, 725. — It is called the head of many monasteries by the Venerable Bede, XCV, 151. — Privilege of Innocent III, 1203, CCXV, 193.

HIEROSOLYMITANUM. See THE HOLY SEPULCHRE.

HIEROSOLYMITANUM OF ST MARY, a monastery existing in the time of Gregory, bishop of Tours, in 595, LXXI, 715.

HIEROSOLYMITANUS OF ST MARY MAJOR (the convent of Sainte-Marie-Majeure at Jerusalem), a convent of nuns built by the queen of Jerusalem and confirmed by the privilege of Innocent III in 1203, CCXV, 150.

HOSPITAL OF ST JOHN OF JERUSALEM (the Hospitallers of St John of Jerusalem), established by Geraud, provost, in 1112 for all pilgrims arriving at Jerusalem from different lands. Raymond was made its guardian, as appears from his own charter, CLV, 1257. — Later Gilbert, whose letter to King Louis VIII survives, 1270. — Privilege of Paschal II, 1113, CLXIII, 314. — Privilege of Pope Calixtus II, 1123, ibid., 1261. — Of Innocent II, 1131, CLXXIX, 77, 312. — Letter of Eugenius III to Master Raymond, 1152, CLXXX, 1550. — Charter of Walter of Sombernon, 1210, CLXXXV, 1423. — Privilege of Anastasius IV, 1154, CLXXXVIII, 1078. — Letters of Alexander III, 1167, CC, 524, 556, 950. — Of Lucius III, 1181, CCI, 1081, 1304. — Privilege of Urban III, 1187, CCII, 1468. — Of Clement III, 1189, CCIV, 1444. — Of Innocent III, 1198, CCXIV, 521. — Donation of the palace of Manusascha (Manosque) by the count of Forcalquier before 1209, when Innocent III confirmed this gift, CCXV, 143. — He likewise confirmed the donation of the king of Armenia in 1210, CCXVI, 305. — It is not permitted to celebrate in lands placed under interdict by the Church, CCXVII, 57, 149, 155.

HIKELINGENSE OF ST MARY (Heikling, diocese of Norwich, [Col. 1079] England), a monastery of the Order of St Augustine, whose goods and privileges Innocent III confirmed in 1209, CCXVI, 181.

ST HILARY. See CARCASSONNENSE GALEATENSE, PICTAVIENSE.

CONVENT OF NUNS OF ST HILARY. See FESSULANUS.

HILDESHEIMENSE OF ST MICHAEL (Hildesheim in Saxony), a very celebrated monastery of the Order of St Benedict, founded in the eleventh century by the Blessed Bernard, both abbot and bishop, CLXI, 1175; St Godehard succeeded him, ibid. — Distinguished men and bishops issued from this monastery, CXL, 1235. — Privilege of Eugenius III, 1153, CLXXX, 1570. — Of Celestine III, 1192, CCVI, 973.

HILLISINEBURGENSE (Helsinbourg, Sweden), a monastery of the Order of St Benedict, endowed by Bishop Arnold; Eugenius III confirmed its possessions and rights by privilege in 1153, CLXXX, 1609. (Among the doubtful entries.)

HILSEMBURGENSE, or HILLISINEMBURGENSE (Hilsenburg, diocese of Halberstadt), a monastery of the Order of St Benedict, founded by Arnold, bishop of Halberstadt; Pope Innocent II confirmed its rights and possessions in 1136, CLXXIX, 259.

ST HIMERIUS (Saint-Hymer, Calvados), a monastery of the Order of St Benedict, whose goods and privileges Pope Lucius III confirmed in 1183, CCI, 1210.

ST HIPPOLYTUS. See FAVENTINUM.

HIRSAUGIENSE OF ST AURELIUS (Hirsau, diocese of Speyer), a celebrated monastery of the Order of St Benedict, founded about 772 in the diocese of Speyer by Count Erlafrid, who also subjected it to Fulda, CVII, 95. — It flourished especially in 1085, CXLIII, 338. — Many monks went forth from it and came to the monastery of Petershausen to reform discipline at about the same time, 339. — On the restoration of its monastery, addressed to Count Adelbert by Leo IX, CXLIII, 377. — Privilege of Pope Gregory VII, 1085, CXLVIII, 714. — St William, abbot, 1091, CL, 889. — Hirsau constitutions, 927. — Privilege of Urban II, 1095, CLI, 402. — Letter of Celestine II concerning the election of an abbot, CLXXIX, 789. — The monks write to St Hildegard, CXCVI, 367.

HIRSFELDENSE. See HERSFELDENSE.

HOHENBURGENSIS (Hohenbourg, or Mont Sainte-Odile, diocese of Strasbourg), a convent of nuns in the diocese of Strasbourg, built by St Odile, abbess, about 720. Empress Judith made many grants and confirmed privileges in 837, CIV, 1285, 1287. — Privilege of Pope St Leo IX, 1050, CXLIII, 663.

HOIENSIS OF ST MARY (Sainte-Marie at Huy, diocese of Liège), a monastery of the Order of St Augustine, founded by Archdeacon Boso; later restored by Bishop Theodwin and enriched with many possessions in 1066, CXLVI, 1443, 1445.

HOLMECOLTRAMENSE OF ST MARY (Sainte-Marie de Homecoltran, on the island of Holm, belonging to England), a monastery of the Cistercian Order, founded by King Henry I and Ranulf, count of Chester. — Privilege of Lucius III, 1185, CCI, 1354.

HONAUGIENSE, also HOHENNAUGIENSE AND HONOVIENSE OF ST MICHAEL (Honau or Hohenhausen, former diocese of Strasbourg), a monastery of the Order of St Benedict in the diocese of Strasbourg, built by Adalbert, brother of St Odile, about 720. Theodoric IV granted a privilege to its abbot Benedict in 725, LXXXVIII, 1139. — Charter of the donor Aicho, 723, ibid., 1279. — Likewise of Boro, 1280, 1312. — Of Rodolf, 748, ibid., 1318. — Of King Pippin, XCVI, 1531, 1533, 1545. — Of Carloman, 770, XCVI, 1577; XCVII, 919, 927. — Of Charlemagne, 775, ibid., 953, 957, 961, 967. — Bruno, formerly of this monastery, became bishop of Strasbourg in 1130, CLXVI, 1347.

HORNBACENSE OF ST PETER (Saint-Pierre d’Hornbach, diocese of Metz), a monastery founded before 700 by St Pirmin, or Firmin, apostle of this region, at a place called Gamund, LXXII, 120. — Diploma of Louis the Pious, 821, CIV, 1107.

HORREENSIS OF ST MARY (Sainte-Marie d’Oeren, diocese of Trier), a convent of nuns of the Order of St Benedict, founded in the valley of Trier about 675 by Irmina, daughter of King Dagobert, and St Modoald, bishop, LXXXVII, 1303, 1309. — Some wrongly identify it with Echternach because the same Abbess Irmina indicated a place for the latter’s foundation by granting land. — Privilege of Adrian IV, 1154, CLXXXVIII, 1395.

HORSHAMENSE OF ST FAITH (Sainte-Foi de Horsham, county of Sussex, England), a monastery of the Order of St Augustine, built by the nobleman Robert, son of Walter, before 1163, when Alexander III confirmed it by privilege, CC, 225.

HORTENSE OF ST MARY (Sainte-Marie de Huerta, diocese of Sigüenza), a monastery of the Cistercian Order, built in [Col. 1080] 1150 by King Alfonso I. Alexander III took its privileges and possessions under his protection in 1164, CC, 312.

HOSPITALLERS OF JERUSALEM ESTABLISHED IN IRELAND, whose goods and privileges Innocent III confirmed in 1212, CCXVI, 646.

HOSPITALLERS OF JERUSALEM ESTABLISHED IN THE DIOCESE OF RHEIMS, whom Innocent III forbade to bury excommunicated persons in 1212, CCXVI, 645.

ST HOSPITIUS. See NICIENSE.

ST HUBERT IN THE ARDENNES (Saint-Hubert, in the Ardennes), a monastery of the Order of St Benedict, founded in the castle called Ambra by Duke Pippin and his wife Plectrude in 687, LXXXVIII, 1215. Its charter is regarded as spurious. See ANDAGINENSE.

HUESCENSE OF JESUS OF NAZARETH (Huesca, diocese of Pamplona), a monastery of the Order of St Benedict, built by King Peter of Aragon and endowed with privileges by Pope Urban II in 1089, CLI, 301, 504. — Privilege of Pope Paschal II, 1102, CLXIII, 82, 126. — Privileges of Innocent II, 1139, CLXXIX, 433, 477. — Of Clement III, 1188, CCIV, 1379.

HUGTTHOVIENSE OF ST MICHAEL (Saint-Michel d’Uthenhoffen, Bas-Rhin), a monastery of the Order of St Benedict, built by Count Werner shortly before 1135, when Innocent II confirmed it by privilege, CLXXIX, 336.

HUGESHOFFENSE OF ST MICHAEL (Saint-Michel d’Hugueshoffen or d’Hugoncourt, Bavaria), a monastery of the Order of St Benedict, built by Werner, count of Ortenberg. At the request of Countess Adelaide, Pope Calixtus II confirmed it by privilege in 1123, CLXIII, 1308.

HULMENSE (Hulm or Hulmen, England), a monastery of the Order of St Benedict in England, founded by King Cnut I in 1036; a privilege survives by which he granted it a certain piece of land, CLI, 1184.

HUMBLERIIS, or HUMOLARIIS, OF ST MARY AND ST HUNEGUNDIS (Notre-Dame d’Homblières, former diocese of Noyon), a monastery of the Order of St Benedict, built by St Eligius, bishop, and King Lothair in 650, originally for nuns. St Hunegundis lived and died there; but in 948 Count Albert of Vermandois rebuilt it and granted it to Benedictine monks. — Privilege of Agapetus II, 955, CXXXIII, 930. — Of John XII, ibid., 1015. — Berner became abbot of this monastery in 964, CXXXVII, 49. — Letter of Alexander III for the same monastery, 1174, CC, 935.

HUMILIMONTENSE, or MARSENSE OF ST MARY (Notre-Dame d’Humilimont or Marsans, near Wippens in the Gruyère, Switzerland), a monastery of the Premonstratensian Order, founded in 1137 by three brothers of noble birth. Its possessions and privileges were confirmed by Blessed Amadeus, bishop of Lausanne, CLXXXVIII, 1290.

ST HIMERIUS. See below, IMERIUS.

HUNTHINGDONIENSE OF ST MARY (Notre-Dame d’Huntingdon on the Ouse, England), a monastery of the Order of St Benedict, later called Burh, built by St Æthelwold, bishop, in 980, CXXXVII, 93. — Privilege of Eugenius III, 1147, CLXXX, 1266.

HUNULFOCURTENSIS OF ST PETER (Saint-Pierre d’Honnecourt, Nord), a convent of nuns on the Scheldt, founded by Amalfrid in 680. King Theodoric assigned it to St Bertin, abbot of Sithiu, in 687, LXXXVII, 1337; LXXXVIII, 1209. — Auriana, daughter of Amalfrid, was the first abbess, CXLIX, 129.

HURODLEICHESBERGENSE, a monastery of the Order of St Benedict in Germany, mentioned in the *Life of Blessed Rabanus Maurus*, CVII, 60.

HUYSBURGENSE, or HOYENSE (Huy, diocese of Liège, Belgium), a monastery of the Order of St Augustine, whose goods and privileges Pope Innocent II confirmed in 1134, CLXXIX, 215. — Privilege of Adrian IV, 1156, CLXXXVIII, 1471.

HYENSE. See HIENSE.

IBREIO (Ivry or Ivrey, diocese of Winchester, England), a monastery to which Alexander III assigned certain tithes, 1166–1169, CC, 512.

ST IGNY (Saint-Igny, Haute-Saône), a convent of nuns concerning which Alexander III wrote to the archbishop of Reims in 1165, CC, 325.

IGNIACENSE (Igny, Marne), a monastery of the Cistercian Order founded from Clairvaux in 1126 by Renaud, archbishop of Reims; his charter survives, CLXXII, 1345, 1350. — Abbot Guerric flourished in 1157, CLXXXV, 1; CLXXXVIII, 983. — Letter of Innocent III to the abbot, 1208, CCXV, 1518; CCXVI, 46.

IHAMENSE OF ST MARY (Sainte-Marie d’Iham, Flanders), a monastery of the Order of St Augustine, founded in the eleventh century by Count Godfrey and his wife Matilda, at Iham [Col. 1081] on the Scheldt near Aachen in the diocese of Cambrai, CXLIX, 442. — Their son built two new monasteries almost in the same place, one of St Lawrence and the other of the Holy Saviour, ibid.

ILBENSTADENSE, or ILSTADENSE OF ST MARY (Notre-Dame d’Ilstadt, Bavaria), a monastery of the Order of St Augustine, built by Counts Godfrey and Adon shortly before 1139. At the request of Provost Anthony, Innocent II confirmed it by privilege in that year, CLXXIX, 492. — Privilege of Pope Lucius II, 1144, ibid., 914. — Of Eugenius III, 1147, CLXXX, 1263.

ST ILLIDIUS (Saint-Allire, Auvergne, Puy-de-Dôme), a monastery of the Order of St Benedict, founded by that holy bishop in the city of Clermont in Auvergne, LXXI, 1018 note. — Privilege of Alexander III, 1165, CC, 380.

ST IMERIUS (Saint-Imer, diocese of Lisieux, Calvados), a monastery of the Order of St Benedict, founded and endowed by the counts of Montfort; Lucius III confirmed its possessions by privilege in 1183, CCI, 1210.

INDENSE, or OF THE FOREST OF INDE, OF THE HOLY SAVIOUR AND ST CORNELIUS (Saint-Corneille d’Inde), a monastery of the Order of St Benedict, founded in the Ardennes by Louis the Pious and ruled by Abbot Benedict. — Diploma, 821, CIV, 1105. — Said to have been founded by Benedict, abbot of Aniane, CLXVI, 1351 note.

INFERIOR MONASTERY. See RATISPONENSE.

INGELTINGUNENSE, a monastery in England whose abbot Trumher flourished under King Oswin in 655, XCV, 157.

INISBONFINDENSE, a monastery built in Scotland by Colman, bishop of Lindisfarne, in 667, XCV, 179.

OF THE ISLAND OF ARVERT, OF ST PETER (Saint-Pierre de l’Île, or the Arvert peninsula, Charente-Inférieure), a monastery of the Order of St Benedict, whose goods and privileges Innocent III confirmed in 1199, CCXIV, 610.
